News.title: Man charged after motorcyclist, 28, in fatal crash with car before driver left scene on foot as tributes paid to victim
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH HORROR Man charged after motorcyclist, 28, in fatal crash with car before driver left scene on foot as tributes paid to victim

A MAN has been charged after a motorcyclist was killed in a fatal crash in Romford.

Police were called to Whalebone Lane on the A12 on Saturday night following reports of a collision involving a car and a motorbike.



Despite paramedics’ best efforts, motorcyclist Anwar Shinwari, 28, died at the scene.

The driver of the car allegedly left the scene on foot, prompting a police search.



Lee Culleton, 45, was later arrested in connection with the incident on Saturday morning.

He has since been charged with causing death by dangerous driving, failing to stop, driving without insurance, driving whilst disqualified and fraudulent use of a registration mark.

Culleton appeared at Thames Magistrates’ Court on Monday and was remanded in custody.

He will next appear at Snaresbrook Crown Court on 25 August.

The victim’s friends have since set up a GoFundMe to help cover the funeral costs.

The description reads: “His family is going through an incredibly tough time.



“Every donation can help support them with the costs of transporting his body to Afghanistan and covering funeral expenses.”

An investigation to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the incident is ongoing.

News.title: Aircraft engineer, 23, crushed to death inside plane engine after machinery suddenly fell on him at Heathrow Airport
News.content:
AIRPORT HORROR Aircraft engineer, 23, crushed to death inside plane engine after machinery suddenly fell on him at Heathrow Airport

AN aircraft engineer has died after he was crushed to death inside a plane engine after machinery suddenly fell on him.

Popular aircraft technician Georgie Buxton was in intensive care for four weeks after being crushed in the horrifying accident in a hangar at Heathrow Airport.

He was carrying out maintenance tests on a Boeing 787 when machinery suddenly collapsed on him.



The Dreamliner plane he was working on has been taken out of service since the accident while experts try to understand how the tragedy occurred.



Virgin Atlantic bosses were in talks with plane manufacturer Boeing following the tragedy.

A source told The Sun last night: “Georgie was a young and very loved member of the team. Everyone at Virgin is in shock.

“It was not immediately clear what caused the death, and officials have grounded the jet until further notice on safety grounds.



“Heavy metal cannot fall from a jet engine and the plane be allowed to continue flying.”

The devastated family of the unmarried airport worker, who had worked for Virgin Atlantic for two years and lived near Heathrow in West London, kept a vigil at his bedside after the accident.

Life support machines were eventually switched off earlier this month.

Two years ago, Georgie excitedly took to social media to tell family and friends of his decision to leave Ryanair for his new job as an aircraft technician at Virgin Atlantic.



He wrote: “I’m happy to share that I’m starting a new position as an Aircraft Technician at Virgin Atlantic!

“It’s been a pleasure working with all the engineers and mechanics whilst at Ryanair in Stansted and I’ve been able to develop and learn a lot.

“Now it’s time to move on so I can develop and learn more on different airframes!!”

An inquest into the tragic death will be opened and adjourned later this week at West London Coroner’s Court.

Last night, as tributes poured in for the Heathrow employee, sources the airline confirmed it has launched its own safety investigation – and vowed to work with authorities and aircraft manufacturer Boeing to understand what happened.



Virgin Atlantic boasts 17 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners.

Each carrying up to 264 passengers they were once the youngest in the fleet, but a massive renewal roll-out means they are now some of the oldest, albeit with an average age of just around ten years.

A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson told The Sun: “We are heartbroken to confirm that a much-loved member of our engineering team has passed away.

“Our thoughts are firmly with Georgie’s family, loved ones, friends and colleagues at this incredibly sad and challenging time.

“We’re providing support to loved ones wherever we can and sharing our heartfelt condolences to everyone affected.



“Georgie’s family has asked for privacy at this very difficult time.

“The safety and wellbeing of our people is always our top priority, and we are devastated by this incident.

“We are working closely with relevant authorities and the aircraft manufacturer on the investigation to establish all facts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Out of respect for those involved and while the investigation is ongoing, we are unable to provide any further information at this stage.”

The Sun Online has contacted Heathrow Airport for comment.

News.title: Baby girl and her parents killed after car crashed into trees are named as tributes paid following heartbreaking tragedy
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Baby girl and her parents killed after car crashed into trees are named as tributes paid following heartbreaking tragedy

AN ELEVEN-month-old baby girl who tragically died alongside her parents after a car crashed into trees has been named for the first time.

Little Aisha Camara was in a red Hyundai carrying five people as it left a carriageway in a horror crash in Derby, Derbyshire, on Saturday night.

Her parents, Abubacarr Camara, 36, and Isa Jaiteh, 30, both Gambian nationals, also perished after the vehicle came off the A38.



Aisha was rushed to hospital but sadly could not be saved.



The Gambia Welfare Society in Leeds hailed Abubacarr as a “dedicated servant of his community” in a touching tribute.

A statement read: “Our community in Leeds, especially the Sarahuleh community, has been struck by a devastating tragedy.

“We are grateful that the driver survived the accident, and we pray that Allah (SWT) grants him a full and speedy recovery, eases his pain, and gives him strength during this incredibly difficult time.



“Abu was a dedicated servant of his community, passionate about his Deen, supporting the new mosque, and mentoring young children through football.

“He will be remembered for his kindness, humility, and selfless service.

“May Allah (SWT) forgive them all, have mercy on them, grant them the highest place in Jannatul Firdaus, and give their families strength and patience during this heartbreaking time.”

An 18-year-old woman – who has not been named – also died in the horror smash, Derbyshire Police confirmed.



Cops have since arrested a 33-year-old man on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving after taking him to hospital with serious injuries.

Emergency services were called to a stretch of road between the A50 Toyota Island and the A516 in Derby at around 11pm on Saturday.

Cops said all five people were from Leeds, West Yorkshire, and their family members are being supported by specialist officers.

A police spokesperson said “Abubacarr Camara (36), Isa Jaiteh (30) and Aisha Camara (11-months-old) died following the crash.

“Abubacarr and Isa are the parents of Aisha. An 18-year-old woman who died in the crash has not been named.



“All four people were passengers in the vehicle.

“The driver – a 33-year-old man – was taken to hospital to be treated for serious injuries where he remains today.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and has been bailed.

“Anyone who witnessed the crash is urged to please come forward.”

News.title: Zack Polanski should be arrested over ‘incitement to murder’, Farage says after Greens leader posts guillotine T-shirt
News.content:
FARAGE THREAT Zack Polanski should be arrested over ‘incitement to murder’, Farage says after Greens leader posts guillotine T-shirt

NIGEL Farage has reported Zack Polanski to the police after accusing him of incitement to murder over a social media post.

The Green Party leader shared an image on Instagram of an activist wearing a t-shirt calling for the Brexiteer’s decapitation.



The picture showed a bearded Leftie in a black top emblazoned with a guillotine and the words “we’re only making plans for Nigel”.

Mr Polanski deleted the picture yesterday after its contents were “brought to his attention” and insisted he “does not support this type of dangerous message”.



But Mr Farage blasted: “This is what Zack Polanski has just posted on his Instagram.

“If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski.”

Reform’s Zia Yusuf added: “This is incitement to murder. It should be treated as such by the police.”

And Reform’s Robert Jenrick slammed: “These people are sick.

This went out to hundreds of thousands of followers.

“How ironic, when Zack talks endlessly about being kind and loving to each other.”

A Green Party spokesman said: “After attending a public event, Zack accepted a request to collaborate on a post with several images.



“Once this image was brought to his attention he immediately unshared the post.

“He unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message.”

The Met Police said: “Earlier today – Monday, 27 July – we received a third-party report relating to an image shared on social media.



“We take reports of this nature extremely seriously, and officers are conducting enquiries into the matter.”

Earlier this month, an Afghan migrant with an AK47 tattoo on his face was jailed for threatening to kill Farage.

The man was held for ­vowing to shoot the Reform UK leader in the head.



And this came just a week after party spokeswoman Ann Widdecombe was murdered at her home – sparking fears over the safety of other public figures.

Last week, Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged with one count of murder over Widdecombe’s death.

Farage has also revealed he gets 300 threats a month.

The Reform leader has pushed for his party’s politicians to be given beefed-up security.

The Greens are continuing to fall away in the polls since Andy Burnham became Prime Minister.



Mr Polanski’s party are now haemorrhaging votes to Labour as the Government looks to lurch leftwards.

Back in April, Sir Mark Rowley publicly blasted Mr Polanski after he suggested the Met Police were too heavy-handed when arresting the suspect of the Golders Green terror attack.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Met Commissioner wrote a letter to the Green Party leader where he said he was “disappointed” in his “inaccurate and misinformed commentary”.

News.title: Body found on popular beach after two men were taking inflatable kayaks to sea as 2nd remains missing
News.content:
WAVE TRAGEDY Body found on popular beach after two men were taking inflatable kayaks to sea as 2nd remains missing

A BODY has been found in the desperate search for two men who went missing from a coastal town in Wales.

Simon Wilson and Connor Parfitt was last seen at 6.30pm on July 21 near to Hafan-y-Mor, Pwllheli, on the Llyn Peninsula.



The pair were thought to be heading towards the coastline with inflatable kayaks.

A huge search operation was launched and police have now revealed Connor’s body was found on a beach in Aberystwyth.



The 24-year-old’s family have now been informed and are being supported by officers.

Simon’s whereabouts is still unknown and search operations are ongoing.

A North Wales Police spokesperson said: “A man’s body has sadly been discovered during searches for two missing people.

“Officers were called at around 12.30pm yesterday, July 26, to reports of a body being found on a beach in Aberystwyth.

“The man has now been identified as Connor Parfitt, one of the men who we circulated as missing from Pwllheli last week. Connor’s family and the coroner have been informed.

“Sadly, Simon Wilson has not yet been found and officers are continuing to support his family.”



Chief Inspector Stephen Pawson added: “My thoughts remain with both Connor and Simon’s families at this incredibly difficult time.

“This is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, including the teams involved in the searches.

“Thank you to partner agencies, volunteers and members of the public who assisted in our searches over the last six days.

“We continue to appeal for any information or sightings of Simon to contact us quoting reference O120829.”

This comes as a heroic girl, 15, died alongside her mum while trying to save a boy, 7, from the tide in West Mersea, near Colchester, in Essex.



Selina Rahman, 41, and her daughter Samia Rahman were among a group of five caught up in the horror.

Cops and coastguard crews were scrambled to Sea View Holiday Park at around 5.30pm on July 22.

A seven-year-old boy was reportedly rushed to hospital in a coma.

News.title: Man spends £10k building realistic mini Greek village in his back garden – complete with its own bar
News.content:
CRETE IDEA Man spends £10k building realistic mini Greek village in his back garden – complete with its own bar

A MAN has spent thousands building a stunning mini Greek village in his back garden – complete with its own bar.

Michael Scherrer, 48, a content creator from Lake Constance, Switzerland spent over a year turning his garden into a tiny theme park.



The Mediterranean paradise is complete with a Greek village featuring cobbled streets, blue shutters and a tiny bar.

However, the project was repeatedly delayed by harsh weather conditions and Swiss building regulations.



The Greek village alone cost £10,000 to build, spanning roughly 250 square feet.

Michael said: “I wanted to make somewhere we could sit in the theme park to have a chat with our clients, so I thought of this – it took longer than you think to build because of permissions in Switzerland – and having to take a break for the weather.

“We picked the theme because we had just finished building this fairy tale alleyway, which was so complicated – the white and blue was so easy – and looked cool – so we picked that.”

“The idea to build the theme park came from us just wanting to garden and build.”



This latest project was designed to recreate the atmosphere of a sun-soaked holiday destination, except only metres away from your front door.

“Because it is summer, whenever I go in there I feel like I am transported,” Michael said.

“We tried to build the bar point so you are completely submerged in the mini village – and it really does feel like you are there.”

Michael said his family has even been able to convince their friends and colleagues they’re on holiday.

He said: “My friends come to the bar and love taking pictures – they fool their friends and people actually believe they are on holiday.



“My sister did it once to her co-workers, and when she came back, six different people came up to her and asked how her holiday weekend was!”

Michael is now hoping some of his creations could be used as a bedroom.

“I will leave the Greek village how it is right now with the homemade bar because there is not much point now it is getting closer to Halloween, when I stop working on it until spring.



“Once spring comes through, I reckon I will put a bed in one of the little homes and make it a sort of guest room or somewhere visitors can stay.”

The content creator said he has been working on the miniature village for more than four years.

He also revealed that he is already planning on future additions to his backyard attraction.

He said: “We have already made a Japanese garden with stonework and maple trees, and now we are planning to move on to a fishing village and a room for the guests – but we have to work this all out first!

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We want to make a pirate ship at one point.



“I might even make a U-turn and instead recreate the house in the TV series ‘Friends’ – who knows!”

News.title: Man, 19, charged with murder after teen, 18, dies in horror crash between motorbike and van outside pub
News.content:
MURDER PROBE Man, 19, charged with murder after teen, 18, dies in horror crash between motorbike and van outside pub

COPS have charged a teenager with murder following the death of an 18-year-old motorcyclist in a collision outside a pub.

Connor Todd, 19, is set to appear before Margate Magistrates’ Court on July 28 in connection with the fatal crash in Chestfield Road, near Whitstable, Kent.

The biker died at the scene just after 8.15pm on Friday.



The motorcycle he was riding was involved in a collision with a white Mercedes A180.



While his next of kin have been informed, he has not been formally identified yet.

An off-duty doctor and nurse were among those who came to the aid of the injured rider and CPR was performed until a team of paramedics arrived.

A defibrillator was also brought from the Chestfield Golf Club nearby.



Police and ambulance crews continued resuscitation attempts, but the teenager could not be revived.

At around 9.50pm on Friday, an 18-year-old man voluntarily attended Canterbury police station and was arrested in connection with the investigation.

He has since been released on bail.

Todd, of Seasalter, attended the same police station the following day, where he was arrested before later being charged with murder.



Detectives are continuing their investigation and have appealed for witnesses or anyone with dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage showing either vehicle before or after the incident to come forward.

Meanwhile, tributes have been left at the scene.

Flowers, candles and handwritten messages have been placed along the roadside outside the pub.

Cans of energy drinks, a bottle of Jack Daniel’s and Coke and a vape have also been placed beside a nearby tree in his memory.

Anyone with information is urged to call the appeal line on 01303 289600, quoting reference 46/120838/26, or submit information via the force’s Major Incident Public Portal.



Information can also be passed anonymously to Crimestoppers by calling 0800 555111 or completing its online form.

News.title: ‘World’s oldest cat’ Millie is 146 in human years and only drinks luxury mineral water and eats fresh prawns & salmon
News.content:
FUR-EVER YOUNG ‘World’s oldest cat’ Millie is 146 in human years and only drinks luxury mineral water and eats fresh prawns & salmon

THE owner of what is thought to be the world’s oldest cat lives on a diet of Buxton mineral water and eats fresh prawns and salmon.

Leslie Greenhough, 71, believes his tortoiseshell moggy, Millie, who was born in 1995, is currently the oldest living feline at aged 31, the equivalent of 146 in human years.



The puss was first owned by Leslie’s late wife, Paula, who passed away aged 55 in 2020 who got Millie the same year as a three-month-old kitten.

And Leslie has since said Millie’s incredible lifespan is down to feeding her only Buxton natural mineral water for the past decade – alongside “lots of treats” including “cuddles on the sofa”.



The purchasing manager from Stockport, Greater Manchester, celebrated her birthday earlier this year in March, treating her to a bowl full of chicken.

And due to the heat he says Millie always has two fans on her to keep her cool.



Leslie said: “I am very proud she has made it to 31, she is a real trooper.

“I have been feeding her mineral water for the past 10 years now.



“Nearby to our house, work was being done to the water pipes, and because I am old I was classed as a vulnerable person.

“So they began dropping off Buxton water at my doorstep which I drank and also gave to Millie.

“When I turned my taps back on afterwards, dirty water came out, so I chose to stick with the Buxton which I have stuck with ever since.”

“But I’m proud of Millie mainly for my wife really, she would be amazed with how well she is doing.

“Millie is around 146 in human years, I think that says it all really.



“Imagine being 146 years old, I can’t – it is only animals like tortoises that live to daft ages like that.”

Leslie met his wife on the dating site Plenty of Fish in 2012, and he was introduced to Millie after he overheard her “meowing” in the background of the calls.

The couple got engaged in 2013 on Valentine’s Day and married in 2014.

Leslie had owned a cat once before as a child, named Blackie, but hadn’t had a pet in several decades, until meeting Millie.

He said: “Blackie used to follow me everywhere; she was born in a paper mill and such a sweet thing.



“Millie was such a sweet cat when I first met her.

“Over the years Millie was bullied by other cats in her neighbourhood, so she stopped going out and became more of an indoor cat.

“She’s developed a cautious attitude – she’s very shy.

“I think that’s helped her live longer.”

Leslie’s wife Paula sadly passed away six years ago, in 2020, after contracting Covid-19.



His wife’s passing also affected Millie, who struggled to eat after losing her mum.

He said: “It was incredibly difficult on both of us.

“Millie and I had bonded before she died, she would sit on my lap and my wife said she could see how much the cat loved me.

“I think Millie knew my wife wasn’t well.

“Millie wouldn’t eat anything at first, I used to give her prawns and chicken, but over time she’s back to eating cat food.”



Leslie says his “life ambition” is to get her in the Guinness Book of Records, but sadly he can’t prove her age.

He said: “Unfortunately, the only person who can do that is my late wife.”

And the only item of proof he has is an image taken in 1995 of Millie eating out of a food bowl his wife took.

Leslie says Millie has begun to struggle in the heat so he has been pulling ice cubes in her water and blowing two fans in her direction.

He said: “She has also began sleeping on the floor, the air must be cooler down there.”



The retiree also says Millie’s personality has changed with her age with her now becoming more “relaxed” and “chilled out”.

Millie starts her day “messing” about with Leslie before jumping up onto his knee to sit on the back of the sofa in the sun.

Leslie also credits Millie’s longevity to 12pm wake-up calls and a diet of prawn and salmon.

The cat lover said: “She keeps herself to herself, she will wake up around dinner time and I will mess about her with for 30 minutes.

“She only drinks Buxton water and has a diet of salmon, prawns, chicken and tuna.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Millie likes to do her own thing; I will find her either asleep behind the sofa or asleep in my bed.

“Sometimes she will play out in the garden – a cat is a cat really.”

News.title: France wildfires live: Bordeaux threatened by 'fire of the century' that has 'life of its own'
News.content:
More than 220,000 people in south-west France's Gironde region have been evacuated as raging wildfires approach Bordeaux

France wildfires live: Bordeaux threatened by 'fire of the century' that has 'life of its own'

An 'unprecedented' wildfire raging seven miles from the French city of Bordeaux has been labelled the 'fire of the century' by its mayor, as fears grow that it could take months to contain.

Firefighters are struggling to contain the flames, which have burned 42,000 hectares - an area four times the size of Paris - leaving two firefighters dead and 88 injured. Volunteers, including local farmers, are helping by towing huge water tankers to the scene.

President Emmanuel Macron held a crisis meeting today as shifting winds and arid conditions have made the blaze difficult to control. France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the blaze has a "life of its own," and is behaving in "in a completely erratic manner" that makes it difficult to control.

Meanwhile in Spain, 25,000 people have been ordered to evacuate and almost 40,000 have been told to stay indoors. Wildfires near Madrid "slowed their advance" overnight but remain active, the regional government said today.

The Prince and Princess of Wales have also offered their condolences to those affected by the wildfires, which they claim are a “stark reminder of the challenges posed by an increasingly extreme climate”.

News.title: Volodymyr Zelensky receives chilling warning after Ukraine attacks Iran ship on Caspian Sea
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky receives chilling warning after Ukraine attacks Iran ship on Caspian Sea

Tehran parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Commission has issued the warning which suggests Ukraine could suffer after the attack on the commercial vessel

View 3 Images Volodymyr Zelensky speaks during a press conference (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Iran has today warned Volodymyr Zelensky it will avenge an attack by Ukraine on one of its ships.

‌



The commercial vessel was struck in the Caspian Sea, killing one sailor and injuring several others, despite Washington signalled a pause in fighting. It has led to alarm that the two fronts, Ukraine and Iran, could merge as warring parties draw closer - Ukraine and the west and Iran with Russia.

‌



And it is said the US may return to attacking Iran but on a larger and escalatory scale after meetings between Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump.

‌



Ukraine said it had targeted a Russian warship and vessels used for transporting Iranian-linked military cargo in the Caspian Sea. But the Foreign Ministry said Iran “has never intervened in the conflict between Russia and Ukraine.”

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Tehran parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, said on Monday: “Any attack on Iran always comes with a cost, and that remains true today; the US and Israel are well aware of this. Ukraine, too, may soon come to understand that Iran does not let actions go unanswered."

View 3 Images US forces clamp down with naval blockade on Iran (Image: US Central Command (CENTCOM)/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



'We've seen satellite surveillance'

Before setting off for today’s meeting with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Volodymyr Zelensky added: “Since the beginning of July, we have recorded active Russian satellite surveillance of the Gulf states and US military facilities located there. These images subsequently appear in Iran.”

The US has halted attacks on Iran for a third night going into this evening as talks on a way out of the war for both sides continue. It was Mr Zelenksy's first face-to-face meeting with the UK Prime MInister since the former Manchester Mayor took office.

View 3 Images Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Image: avishushan2/YouTube)

‌



But both sides Iran and the US are preparing their militaries for another escalation. Sources have told the Daily Mirror Iran has spent the past 48 hours moving military material including rockets, missiles and drones from hiding spots in the east to the west.

Much of Tehran’s arsenal is thought to have been moved to the east months ago and it still has enough weaponry to engage in warfighting for months. And there have been as many as nine interceptions by Israel of weaponry being smuggled from Iran to Lebanese Hezbollah via Israel.

A UK source told the Daily Mirror: “The US has paused its attacks for now but it could easily resume the offensive action after Netanyahu leaves the States. There has been a significant movement of arms in Iran from east to west and it is believed some of this equipment has come from China and Russia

Article continues below

"There is a feeling that Iran could pre-emptively strike Israel and Hezbollah is thought to have been re-supplied to a degree by Iran, although there have been a lot of interdictions of weaponry. It is doubtful there will be a return to fighting until after Netanyahu returns.”

News.title: Newquay deaths: Man and his daughter drown after 'fall from rocks' at Fistral Beach
News.content:
Beachgoers bravely tried to rescue a man and woman after they reportedly fell from rocks and died in the choppy sea at Britain's most popular surfing spot.

Newquay deaths: Man and his daughter drown after 'fall from rocks' at Fistral Beach

Scene at Fistral beach where witnesses say man and woman fell into water

A father and his daughter, in their 60s and 30s. have tragically died after rescue crews pulled them from the water at Britain's most famous surfing beach in Cornwall.

People at Fistral Beach, in Newquay, bravely attempted to rescue the pair - reportedly a father and daughter - with witnesses suggesting they had fallen from rocks.

Witnesses said nine emergency vehicles and a helicopter rushed to the 750-metre long sands, known as the 'home of British surfing' , last night. Police, the coastguard and the ambulance service were deployed at around 9.30pm. Images from Fistral last night showed people crowding on the sands trying to help with the rescue effort.

The area is well-known for having extremely strong and dangerous rip currents, particularly during outgoing tides. Locals said the sea currents were "very strong" last night.

The beach has regular lifeguard patrols but, tragically, the incident happened after they had finished for the day.

The Mirror has launched the Save Lives For Sam water safety campaign to tackle the UK's growing drowning crisis. Backed by MPs, Olympic champions, national water safety organisations and bereaved families, the campaign is calling for urgent action to make our waters safer.

Find out more about the campaign and how you can support it here.

News.title: Tate brothers to remain behind bars for two more weeks as they fight extradition to UK
News.content:
Tate brothers to remain behind bars for two more weeks as they fight extradition to UK

Andrew and Tristan Tate are fighting extradition from the United States to the United Kingdom, where the brothers are accused of rape and sex trafficking

View 2 Images Andrew Tate (L) and his brother Tristan Tate (stock image) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan will remain in jail for at least two more weeks until their next hearing as they fight extradition to the United Kingdom, where the brothers are accused of multiple counts of rape and sex trafficking, a federal judge said.

‌



US magistrate Lauren Louis set a detention hearing for August 13 to determine whether the social media influencers should stay in jail or be released during what could be a months-long extradition process.

‌



The Tates were not in court on Monday or required to be there and have remained in jail since making a brief court appearance two days after their July 18 arrest.

‌



Lawyers for the brothers said today that they want the US government to turn over documents that UK officials submitted to secure their arrest. “They don’t have anything but the accusations,” attorney Joseph McBride said after the hearing. “It’s just their word against our word right now.”

View 2 Images Joseph McBride is representing the Tates in the US court proceedings (Image: Getty Images)

The UK has until mid-September to turn over all of its materials to the State Department, US attorney Alejandra Lopez said in court. The brothers have long claimed that their violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes.

‌



Jackie Perczek, another one of their lawyers, said the Tates have shown they are not a flight risk by returning to Romania every month after they were accused there of luring women for sexual exploitation.

“For three years they have not fled,” she said. “They’ve travelled the world and every month they return to Romania.”

The former professional kickboxers, who have dual US and UK citizenship, have millions of social media followers and are vocal supporters of Donald Trump. The White House has said the brothers shouldn’t expect any help from the president.

‌



McBride said shortly after the Tates were arrested that “they’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they did not commit,” he said. McBride said the extradition attempt was politically motivated, though he provided no details.

Prosecutors in Britain said the new charges relate to four new accusers and were brought after authorities received evidence from police in Bedfordshire. The allegations, which span from 2010 to 2017, include rape, assault, trafficking and offences relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.”

The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015.

Article continues below

The brothers moved to Romania in 2016 and were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems.

News.title: Mum of tragic baby campaigns to ban parental rights for those who kill or harm children
News.content:
Mum of tragic baby campaigns to ban parental rights for those who kill or harm children

EXCLUSIVE: Jo Early, 54, said it was wrong that Gavin Gibbs was entitled to remain in contact with their daughter Abi, 18, after he was jailed for causing grievous bodily harm to her brother, Charlie

Mum of tragic baby's campaign to ban parental rights for those who kill or harm

The mother and twin of a baby who died after his dad broke his arm are campaigning for parents who seriously harm their children to be banned from having access to them or their siblings.

‌



Jo Early, 54, said it was wrong that Gavin Gibbs was entitled to keep in contact with their daughter Abi, 18, after he was jailed for causing grievous bodily harm to her brother, Charlie.

‌



Gibbs whispered "please forgive me'' as Charlie's life support machine was turned off in hospital in October 2008.

‌



He was later cleared of murdering the three-month-old but convicted of breaking his arm.

Currently parental responsibility is only removed when a person is convicted of killing their partner under "Jade's Law" named after Jade Ward, 27, who was murdered in her home in Shotton, Flintshire, by Russell Marsh in 2021.

Jo is now calling for parents who murder or cause serious harm to their children to be included in the ban.

‌



View 6 Images Jo Early and her ex Gavin Gibbs (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

She told the Mirror: "I don't want any other family to go through what we've gone through because when a perpetrator has access to a very young child the psychological damage that that does can rob them of their childhood.

"I just wanted to bring my daughter up but the process leaves you scarred for life." Abi, who received messages and presents from Gibbs twice a year until turning 18 last week, said: "He used to put his aftershave on the cards and I would open them and just smell it. That can be so confusing for anyone let alone a young girl.

‌



"The way I felt when I was a kid, it gave me something to fantasise about, the idea of having a dad. All the little girls at school had one who loved them and was there for them and was there for them, I had nothing.

"I didn't have a dad, so receiving cards from someone called Daddy was exciting, yet heart-breaking all at the same time. I think what my mum's doing is going to be life changing for future victims. I think had I not had all of this from him I think my life would look very different and for the better so I think that it is vital for this new law to be put in place."

Gibbs was sentenced to three years for grievous bodily harm. Following a successful appeal, it was reduced to two years. He was released after 11 months.

‌



Jo asked Gibbs to give up his parental responsibility which gave him legal rights over Abi but he would only do so on condition she allowed him access to her.

View 6 Images Jo Early and daughter Abi hold a picture of Charlie (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Jo is now campaigning for those rights to be removed automatically in such cases and has lobbied Baroness Alison Levitt KC and Victims' Rights Commissioner Claire Waxman.

‌



She is calling for the changes to be introduced in the Courts and Tribunals Bill currently going through parliament or in a separate Parental Responsibility Act.

Jo met her former husband at the London Ambulance Service, where she worked in the control centre in Waterloo and he was a paramedic.

On July 23, 2008, she gave birth to twins. Jo said: "It was the happiest day of my life, I was over the moon because I had a little girl and a little boy, they were twins. It was just so perfect we had this complete family."

‌



But three months later Abi was admitted to Queen Mary's Hospital, Sidcup, with bronchiolitis.

That night she got a phone call to say that Charlie was downstairs in A&E and he'd stopped breathing.

Jo said: "I saw him lying there and the doctors were working on him on this metal thing and I just collapsed and my legs stopped working and I was put into a wheelchair. I just couldn't believe this was happening."

‌



6 View 6 Images Jo with Charlie and Abi (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror) 6 View 6 Images Charlie Gibbs died aged three months (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Charlie was put on a life support machine and Jo went with him in an ambulance to Kings College hospital in Camberwell, South London. "I was just watching this nurse's hand pump oxygen to him all the time and I was thinking 'please don't stop'."

‌



Soon after arriving at hospital doctors said there was no sign of life and the life support machine would be switched off.

"We said our goodbyes and I just couldn't believe he was gone," Jo said.

Jo first defended Gibbs when he became a suspect, not being able to believe he could have harmed their child.

‌



But that changed months later when he changed his story and said that Charlie had fallen off the sofa three weeks before he died. Jo hasn't spoken to him since.

View 6 Images Gavin Gibbs with Charlie (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Gibbs, of Erith, Kent, told an Old Bailey jury that he said sorry to his infant son as he died because he had not been able to save him.

‌



The court heard that 17 days before Charlie died in hospital from brain damage, Gibbs deliberately twisted and broke his arm.

Sentencing him for the attack, Judge Timothy Pontius told him: "I put aside the remaining charges of which in their merciful verdicts the jury has acquitted you.''

But he added: "Such an appalling act of violence by a powerfully-built man upon a helpless baby merely weeks old must be punished by an immediate prison sentence.''

‌



View 6 Images Abi and Charlie (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

After Charlie died, it was discovered that he had a fractured skull, a broken arm and a broken leg.

Victims Commissioner for England and Wales, Claire Waxman OBE, is backing Jo's campaign. She said: “I welcome the positive steps this Government is taking to better protect victims and children, with Jade’s Law soon to be implemented and the Courts and Tribunals Bill removing the presumption of parental involvement in the Family Courts.

Article continues below

"However, I am clear that Government has more work to do, as we continue to see cases like these [referring to Jo's case], where abusive parents retain parental responsibility despite the most serious offending."

Sign Jo's petition on this link.

News.title: Lloyds and Barclays down: Hundreds 'can't make payments' as Halifax also hit
News.content:
Lloyds, Barclays and Halifax customers are all experiencing issues which include problems with the app, bank transfers and online banking

Lloyds and Barclays down: Hundreds 'can't make payments' as Halifax also hit

Lloyds, Barclays and Halifax customers have reported major problems with their banking this afternoon.

Customers say they are unable to make payments or transfer money, while others have received messages warning them payment had failed but later realised the money had actually gone through.

Lloyds Bank said it is investigating an issue affecting Faster Payments, which "may cause delays".

The bank also urged customers who have attempted to send money not to send it again as this may result in duplicate payments.

Hundreds of Barclays customers say they have been unable to receive external payments, while the majority of Halifax users reporting issues today said they were struggling to transfer funds.

News.title: Xbox down as frustrated gamers can't sign in after system hit by global outage
News.content:
Xbox users have reported a series of issues with the gaming platform on Downdetector. The problem appears to be global and there are hundreds of cases in the UK alone

Xbox down as frustrated gamers can't sign in after system hit by global outage

Gamers are reporting a a major global outage with Xbox with frustrated players saying they are unable to sign in.

Hundreds of users have taken to Downdetector, which reports online outages, to report issues with launching games and server connections.

Xbox Support issued a message earlier today, saying they were aware some users were encountering errors when "attempting to sign in, see your game library or launch games".

In their latest update, they said: "Just checking in on the game library, sign-in, and game launch issue. We know this has been going on a while and appreciate your patience while our teams keep working on it. "

News.title: Mum 'suffocated son and took her own life' after relationship breakdown, inquest hears
News.content:
Mum 'suffocated son and took her own life' after relationship breakdown, inquest hears

The bodies of Tasmin Paterson, 31, and her nine-year-old son Hudson Paterson were sadly found at a property in the Fletchersbridge area of Bodmin, Cornwall

View 2 Images Hudson Paterson, 9, was tragically found dead alongside his mum Tasmin Paterson, 31, at a property in Cornwall (Image: Devon & Cornwall Police)

A mother suffocated her nine-year-old son and took her own life before the pair were found dead at their home in Cornwall, an inquest has heard.

‌



The bodies of Tasmin Paterson, 31, and her son Hudson Paterson were found at the property in the Fletchersbridge area of Bodmin in September 2024.

‌



An inquest into their deaths on Monday heard there had been a breakdown in the relationship between Ms Paterson and her partner Marcus Hughes before he found the mum and son dead in a bedroom at the home they shared.

‌



The inquest heard Ms Paterson had previously separated from Hudson's father in an "amicable" split.

She had been living at the property with Mr Hughes but their relationship had grown "fraught" after she caught him on a dating site, Cornwall Coroner's Court was told.

Mr Hughes told the inquest: "We'd not broken up necessarily but we were on the verges, I felt. She believed it was to do with her ongoing health issues, but there were more things going on than that."

‌



He added that Ms Paterson had previously suffered a head injury and subsequent mobility problems, and that financial and housing issues had put further pressure on their relationship.

View 2 Images Mr Hughes called the police before finding Ms Paterson and Hudson dead (stock) (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Senior coroner Andrew Cox said: "Mr Hughes was Tasmin's partner at the time of her death and he accepted that, while their relationship had been good and healthy and strong at the outset, that more recently it had run into difficulties.

‌



"There had been arguments, never anything physical and never involving Hudson, but I think it's fair to say… that relationship was coming to an end.

"Mr Hughes accepted that Tasmin had caught him on a dating site.

"From Tasmin's perspective, the relationship had not worked out how she had hoped, with all the disappointment and regret that comes with that."

‌



The inquest heard Hudson was "poorly" the evening before he died and so his mother said she would share a room with him, which was not an "unusual" arrangement.

Mr Hughes said he had no concerns until the following morning, when the pair had not woken up. He knocked and shouted their names from the bedroom door, which was locked, and became increasingly worried when there was no reply.

He called the police and broke down the door before finding the bodies of Ms Paterson and Hudson inside.

‌



Ms Paterson was described at the inquest as a "doting" mother, and family members said they never had any reason to suspect she would harm her son.

Aaron Paterson, her ex-husband and Hudson's father, said the nine-year-old had been "everything" to his mother.

"She loved him with all of her heart and Hudson was her everything," he said. "She never hurt him, never raised a hand to him, never screamed in his ear or anything along those lines.

‌



"I never had reason to be cautious or suspicious."

Paying tribute to his son, Paterson said: "The grief we feel for the loss of a son, my son, stepson, nephew, and grandson cannot be understated. Hudson was a quiet but cheeky chappy, who's love for cars was as big as the love for his family and friends.

"Hudson was adored, loved, cherished, and everyday brought a smile to those that he loved and loved him.

‌



"Hudson no longer being here is truly devastating for me as his dad and my family. It's soul destroying and the grief is unimaginable.

"I thank those for the messages of love and support, we would appreciate respect and privacy for Hudson and my family during this heartbreaking time."

Tasmin's family paid tribute saying: "Tasmin was very much loved and will be missed by those who loved her. Our hearts are broken to lose a daughter and a beautiful grandson, who was the light of our lives. Life will never be the same again."

‌



Mr Hughes and his family said: "Tasmin had been a shining star who had left an overwhelming legacy of love and positivity on their lives and that they were privileged to have known her and would always continue to cherish her memory."

An investigation by police "very quickly recognised" Mr Hughes had not been involved in either death, the coroner said.

Mr Cox said: "The evidence of the police is that it is more likely than not that Hudson has died because he has been asphyxiated by Tasmin.

‌



"That is a shocking turn of events, it is difficult to comprehend but I accept that evidence and as a matter of fact I find that is what has happened.

"It is far more likely than not that Tasmin has taken her own life and intended to do so."

He concluded Ms Paterson's death resulted from suicide, and that Hudson died from an unlawful killing.

News.title: Funeral director who left people unburied breached families' trust 'on industrial scale', court hears
News.content:
A funeral director who failed to bury people and gave out wrong ashes has breached the trust of bereaved families "on an almost industrial scale", a court has heard.

Some 35 bodies and more than 100 sets of ashes were found by police raiding Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull in March 2024.

Owner Robert Bush previously admitted 67 offences, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial, and theft from 12 charities.

At the start of his five-day sentencing hearing on Monday, family members watching proceedings at Hull Crown Court gasped and were in tears as details of the "horror scene" at the parlour were described by prosecutors.

This story contains details some might find distressing.

Chris Paxton KC told the packed court bodies had been discovered "on the racks" of a cold storage area and one was found on a stretcher on the floor.

The vast majority were "uncovered and in varying states of decomposition", including one of a stillborn baby.

Bush, 48, was "entrusted by hundreds of bereaved families" but had "breached that trust on an almost industrial scale in a myriad of ways", Paxton said.

News.title: Reform UK reporting Green leader Zack Polanski to police over Instagram post
News.content:
Reform UK say they are reporting Green Party leader Zack Polanski to the police after he shared a post to his Instagram which included a photo of a man wearing a top featuring the name "Nigel" alongside an image of a guillotine.

Polanski accepted a request to collaborate with another account and shared a series of pictures of a Green Party event on Sunday with his 713,000 followers.

One of the images showed a man wearing a T-shirt which said: "We're only making plans for Nigel".

A Green Party spokesperson said: "Once this image was brought to [Zack's] attention he immediately unshared the post. He unequivocally does not support this type of dangerous message."

The Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, criticised Polanski on X.

Sharing a screenshot of what Polanski had reposted, he said: "If I was to post anything as inciteful then I would expect to be arrested, and so should Polanski."

It is understood Reform UK are reporting Polanski to the police. The party's home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, said "this is incitement to murder".

News.title: Man jailed for abduction and rape of girl, 15, in Edinburgh basement
News.content:
A masked rapist who abducted a 15-year-old girl from an Edinburgh city centre bus stop has been jailed under a lifelong restriction order.

Aaron Strachan, 21, pulled a knife on the girl on the city's Princes Street in May last year, before marching her to a basement storage area and raping her.

The High Court in Edinburgh heard that he also attacked a man with a hammer days later, and had a criminal record of violence, robbery and possession of weapons.

Strachan was jailed for a minimum of five years with an order for lifelong restriction (OLR). It means a parole board must decide if he is ever safe to be released.

Judge Michael O'Grady described Strachan's crimes as the "stuff of nightmares".

Strachan admitted raping the girl and charges of serious assault against two male victims in December last year.

The judge said he expected Strachan to be in custody or under supervision for the rest of his life.

News.title: Zelensky visit sends clear message of support for Ukraine, Burnham says
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the UK is "with Ukraine 100%" as Volodymyr Zelensky became the prime minister's first international visitor since entering No 10.

Burnham said the visit of the Ukrainian president was designed to "send a very clear message" about the UK's continued support.

"To put it simply, Volodymyr, I want you to know that we've got your back, you can count on me and you can count on us. You can count on the UK for as long as it takes," he said at a naval base in Portsmouth on Monday.

Zelensky, meanwhile, said Ukraine's relationship with the UK was "stronger than ever".

Addressing Zelensky, Burnham said: "I am personally with you 100%, Mr President, and I will honour every commitment this country has made to Ukraine in full."

Burnham added that he intended to visit Ukraine "soon" following the "very warm meeting" between the pair.

The PM also announced the sharing of the intellectual property behind the UK's new "Stone Cloak" electronic warfare system, enabling Ukraine to produce the technology at scale.

Burnham said: "It will help them to hit their targets and help save Ukrainian lives."

The Stone Cloak jammers are the size of a tablet computer and are designed to block the detection of any drones they are fitted to.

The Ministry of Defence has already given thousands of the devices to Ukrainian forces to bolster their drone operations.

Downing Street said that following its deployment in Ukraine, the technology will be built into the UK's next generation of long-range weapons.

It said this would include Project Brakestop, a government programme to develop low-cost cruise missiles - self-propelled guided weapons that fly like normal aircraft for much of their flight.

During Monday's visit, the two leaders also met more than 200 Ukrainian military personnel who have spent the last three weeks taking part in a maritime exercise in the UK.

Exercise Sea Breeze is aimed at strengthening warfighting capabilities and counter-mine measures in the Black Sea.

Burnham also said the UK would support Ukraine to get a "full and unconditional ceasefire".

"We will keep up the pressure, pushing for a ceasefire and a resumption of negotiations which must have Ukraine at the table and include a strong voice for Europe too."

News.title: TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie dies at 85
News.content:
TV presenter and comedian Bill Oddie has died at the age of 85, his agent has said.

Oddie became a household name in the 1970s as part of zany TV comedy trio The Goodies, before concentrating on his love of wildlife, as one of the original hosts of BBC TV's Springwatch and other shows about birdwatching.

In a statement, David Foster said: "It is with deep sadness that I announce the passing of Bill Oddie, the country's best-loved birder.

"Bill was a multi-talented celebrity â wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment."

News.title: UK's iconic Jodrell Bank telescope faces axe in science cuts
News.content:
The Jodrell Bank Observatory, which has housed the UK's largest telescope for nearly 70 years, has lost its funding and could now close, the BBC understands.

The observatory and its network of telescopes have been pivotal to the country's study of distant galaxies and training future astronomers. Scientists have described the decision as "heartbreaking" and "scientifically misguided".

All scientific observations at Jodrell are expected to cease on the 1 April 2028 unless alternative funding can be found.

The funding body, the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) agency, said it had to focus investment on projects that deliver "the greatest long-term impact".

Prof Brian Cox, professor of particle physics at the University of Manchester - which hosts Jodrell Bank Observatory - described the cuts as "hasty and ill-considered".

"The damage to the UK's science base has already been substantial. I am astonished that UKRI are still ploughing ahead and not working with the Burnham government to find a solution," he said.

In response, Jonathan Reynolds, who is the new Secretary of State in the expanded business department that now has responsibility for science, told BBC News that the UK's world class research was "absolutely central to creating a better future for the UK".

"I am committed to working with UKRI to ensure the UK remains able not only to sustain its world-leading research capabilities, but also to invest in the next generation of scientific facilities and infrastructure that will underpin discovery, innovation and growth in the years ahead."

The Jodrell Bank site was first established in 1945 and pioneered radio astronomy and the study of galaxies beyond our own.

It was also pivotal during the Cold War, when it was used to monitor Soviet missiles during the height of nuclear tensions between the USSR and Nato powers.

Its contribution to global scientific efforts earned it Unesco World Heritage status in 2019.

But the UKRI, which has an annual budget of just under Â£10bn, says it has had to cut the observatory's annual Â£2.8m budget because planned research costs for physics and the running of its labs had escalated.

The announcement is part of broader cuts to astronomy, nuclear and particle physics research over the next four years which will also impact on other projects.

The UK will no longer participate in research at the James Clark Maxwell Telescope in Hawaii, which scientists are using to image supermassive black holes at the centre of galaxies.

UKRI has also cut funding for the UK's involvement in two instruments on the Extremely Large Telescope which is being built in Chile to search for signs of life on other Earth-like worlds.

And a number of upgrades to improve experiments at the Large Hadron Collider will not be paid for by the agency.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts for parts of UK ahead of next heatwave
News.content:
Amber heat health alerts have been issued for much of eastern England for later this week as temperatures rise again.

The East Midlands, East of England, London, and the South East are all under the amber alerts from 9am on Wednesday until 9am Thursday.

With the temperature forecast to peak in the mid-30s Celsius on Wednesday, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), which issues the alerts, warns that significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures.

Yorkshire and the Humber, the West Midlands, and the South West are all under less severe yellow alerts for the same period.

This latest heatwave comes after some of the driest regions of the UK missed their chance of rain over the weekend.

Parts of the northern and western UK saw some rainfall on Saturday and Sunday, with further showers and unsettled conditions expected over the next few days.

But southern parts of the country - where the least amount of rain has fallen - are set to see temperatures climb once again, with more dry and sunny weather in the forecast.

It comes as parts of Wales have officially entered drought status, while parts of southern, central and eastern England remain in "prolonged dry weather", the final stage before drought is declared.

The coming days will only exacerbate dry conditions as another heatwave is expected to be declared, with temperatures peaking around 34-35C (93-95F) in south-east England or the East of England.

News.title: Teen denies endangering lives of 165 people on migrant boat crossing
News.content:
A teenager accused of endangering the lives of 165 migrants by allegedly piloting a record-breaking dinghy crossing of the English Channel is to stand trial.

Chan Mathok Atak, 19, originally of Sudan, appeared at Margate Magistrates Court earlier, where he denied endangering lives at sea during the attempt which set off from France last Thursday.

He appeared with the aid of an Arabic interpreter and when asked how he wished to plea, denied having piloted the dinghy.

Atak was then remanded into custody and will next appear at Canterbury Crown Court on 24 August.

Prosecutor Lucie Fish told the court that, on Thursday, a rigid hulled inflatable boat departed the French coast headed towards Dover carrying the migrants.

The vessel was intercepted by Border Force and Atak is alleged to be one of two people controlling its speed and travel.

The boat was poor quality, overcrowded and "appeared to be deflating upon interception", the prosecutor added.

Pictures of Border Security Command towing the dinghy into Dover showed to be about the same size as a standard bus, at 13m (42ft) long.

During the hearing, the court heard that the French authorities had recovered the body of a man who had suffered head injuries - but there was no indication in court whether his death was related to the record-breaking dinghy.

A spokesman for the National Crime Agency told BBC News: "We are aware of an incident on Thursday 23 July in which an individual died in French waters. French partners are leading the investigation into the circumstances".

Endangerment at sea is a new offence that was created by the government under Sir Keir Starmer to target those alleged to have steered small boats over the English Channel.

In June, two men were the first to be jailed for the crime, each receiving sentences of more than two years.

The previous record arrival in a single vessel was 128 people.

Home Office figures show that while the overall number of arrivals this year is down by about 45% on 2025, the number of migrants per boat has gone up.

News.title: 'Antisemitism felt relentless' - Jewish students on life at UK universities
News.content:
Like many campuses across the UK, Cardiff University has seen pro-Palestine protests in recent years and Oliver said he believed some behaviour he witnessed crossed the line from criticism of Israel into antisemitism.

Holding Jewish people responsible for the actions of the Israeli government is a form of antisemitism, according to the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance.

"That first year was absolutely terrifying," he said.

"You go home and think, 'do I carry on? Do I try to go to the next day?'"

Oliver said he stopped speaking Hebrew outside his home, and hid his Star of David pendant when on campus.

Over the following three years, Oliver said the antisemitic abuse he experienced at university became "relentless".

"I've been in clubs [or] just wandering around the uni and you hear these conversations and you see pamphlets being handed around where it's literally saying that your belief and your history is fake," he said.

"I've been at house parties where, when someone's found out I'm Jewish they started calling me Netanyahu behind my back.

"Like you found out my religion and you've decided I'm a bad person."

Oliver said when he had reported antisemitic incidents that had happened to him and others, he had felt they had been often "swept under the rug" by the university.

Although he said some positive action had been taken, he feels more needs to be done.

Cardiff University said it was sorry that "any student felt unsafe" on campus and that it adopts a "zero-tolerance approach to harassment and discrimination of all kinds".

It said there was no place for antisemitism or hatred at the university and there were "robust procedures" in place for investigating allegations of antisemitism. Where it is found, the university said appropriate action would be taken.

It said it had reached out to the university's Jewish Society and reminded students to report incidents to them.

News.title: Very strong tide led to West Mersea drownings, relative says
News.content:
A mother and daughter who drowned off the Essex coast were swept out to sea by a "very strong" tide, a relative has said.

Shahin Ahmed said six members of his family were paddling at West Mersea beach when they were knocked off their feet on Wednesday afternoon.

Shelina Rahman, 41, and 15-year-old Sameeha, died in the tragedy, while Ahmed's seven-year-old son Musa was airlifted to hospital in a critical condition.

Ahmed said his son, who is from east London, remained on a life support machine at a hospital in London.

Three others were also taken to another hospital by ambulance after the incident. Ahmed said 12 of them were visiting West Mersea that day.

"This was 20 minutes before we were going to go home. The whole day, alhamdulillah (praise be to God), was really nice," Ahmed told Bangladeshi newspaper Surma News.

News.title: Ex political advisor admits fraud over expense claims
News.content:
A former advisor to a Labour MP has admitted claiming fraudulent expenses on the Parliamentary travel booking system.

Matthew Torbitt worked for Bury South MP Christian Wakeford when, between August 2022 and September 2024, he claimed rail tickets that were "not for Parliamentary purposes", Thames Magistrates' Court heard.

He also admitted making a false claim for travel and accommodation expenses on 2 October 2024.

Torbitt, 35, has most recently worked as a political commentator and regularly appears on programmes including GB News, LBC, Sky News, BBC Newsnight, and Times Radio.

Prosecutor Maisha Mannan told the court the claims totalled more than Â£6,000, according to an early estimate by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), but the exact sum will be calculated at a later date.

Torbitt, who appeared in court dressed in a navy blue suit, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud by false representation.

District Judge Navneet Sher sent the case to Snaresbrook Crown Court for sentence at a later date, which has yet to be fixed.

"It's unlikely to be before four weeks, in any event," she told the defendant.

Torbitt worked in various advisory roles for Labour frontbenchers between 2018 and 2024.

An investigation was launched after police received a report that a member of staff working for an MP had allegedly made unauthorised purchases through a travel booking system, the Metropolitan Police previously said.

He was charged by postal requisition on 9 June.

Torbitt is engaged to women's rights activist and 2021 Love Island contestant Sharon Gaffka.

The couple welcomed a baby boy earlier this month, according to Torbitt's Instagram page.

News.title: Fit schools, hospitals and new homes with air con, say Lib Dems
News.content:
In a report published earlier this year,, external the UK's independent adviser on tackling climate change, the Climate Change Committee (CCC), estimated that 92% of existing homes would be at risk of overheating by 2050.

Speaking to Matt Chorley on BBC Radio 5 Live, Farron said: "We want to make sure that we're not being hysterical but we're recognising that we have more extreme temperatures, more extreme weather.

"I want the homes that people live in in the future to be ready for that, that we be climate-ready and prepared."

The party said the cost of its policy to developers would be small compared to the overall cost of building a home, and that cooler homes would be more attractive to buyers in the future.

Farron said forms of air cooling systems should be installed without adding "to the climate crisis", pointing to the potential of air source heat pumps.

There have been concerns that while decreasing temperatures indoors, air conditioning units can increase outdoor temperatures.

Michael Whittall, sustainability manager at property developer Fairview New Homes, told news agency PA: "Air conditioning systems work by removing heat from inside buildings and releasing it outdoors.

"When this happens at scale, particularly in dense urban areas, it can contribute to the urban heat island effect â adding to higher outdoor temperatures and increasing heat stress in cities."

He said the focus should be on "passive cooling" such as better designs, shading and ventilation.

Amanda Williams, head of environmental sustainability at the Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB), said air conditioning or reversible heat pumps would "undoubtedly have a crucial role in some circumstances".

However, she added that making it the default option "risks locking in higher energy consumption" and that the priority should be designing homes that "remain comfortable for as much of the year as possible".

A spokesperson for the Home Builders Federation said: "New build homes are required to be exceptionally well insulated which helps keep them both warmer in winter and cooler in summer.

"This makes living in a new build more comfortable and significantly cheaper to run than older, less well-insulated homes."

The Liberal Democrats have also argued that the government should fund the cost of fitting essential buildings such as schools and hospitals with air conditioning.

The party said the costs of inaction dwarfed the costs of acting immediately, pointing to the CCC's report, external which said climate impacts could cost Â£60bn - Â£260bn a year compared to the Â£7bn - Â£22bn it would cost to protect people from the impacts.

The Lib Dems said the cost of fitting hospitals with air conditioning would come from its Â£10bn investment plan for the NHS.

News.title: 'Cruel' carer jailed for abuse yelled 'I hope you die' at 81-year-old victim
News.content:
A "heartless and cruel" carer who was caught on camera abusing an 81-year-old woman with dementia has been jailed.

In footage shared online, carer Louise Harris could be seen screaming at Elizabeth Anne Shipton in her home in Pontardawe, Neath Port Talbot, and drunkenly shouting: "I hope you die in your sleep you... horrible cow."

As Elizabeth lay in bed, Harris knelt down and put her arm on her chest, demanding to know where her money was.

Elizabeth complained the arm was hurting her, but the carer yelled: "I don't care, where's your money?"

Harris, 42, was given a three-month sentence at Swansea Crown Court - but the victim's family believes it should have been a significantly longer sentence.

Elizabethâs daughter, Tracy Faram Shipton, said her mother was "horrifically traumatised" and had filed an appeal, arguing the sentence handed to Harris last week was unduly lenient.

She had known Harris, a former neighbour, for many years and had trusted her with her mum's care.

"She'd been a carer since she was 18. I checked everything with her - she was trained on dementia, manual handling, incontinence. I'll never get my head around how she could do this," she said.

Tracy said Harris had known her mother had been in a fragile state, having recently been in Morriston hospital for seven weeks with sepsis. She was also grieving the death of her husband, who she had been with since the age of 16.

"My mother had come out of hospital in December, my dad's funeral was in January, and then this happened in February. Louise knew everything my mother was going through," she said.

Tracy said Harris was on her first trial shift, after the family had advertised on Facebook for someone to help while they had waited for a care package to be put in place by social services.

Tracy said Harris had been meant to stay for four hours in total.

"I was there for the first hour and Louise seemed amazing. Almost as soon as I left she turned," she said.

She said that, after she had left, Harris "got drunk and ripped up my mother's knitting".

"I'd explained to her that knitting was the only thing helping my mother through the grief, it was giving her something to live for... It was just cruel."

Harris found a bottle of vodka in the fridge and downed it. The court heard she was a recovering alcoholic who had "succumbed to temptation".

Harris's rage appeared to be sparked by Elizabeth accidentally pressing her emergency alarm, which triggered a phone call to a crisis response helpline.

Tracy said this had happened often and the helpline operator quickly ended the call after Harris said everything had been fine.

The court heard how, at one point, Harris went into the kitchen and waved a large kitchen knife around while trashing the property.

Tracy said she had been horrified when she had accessed the security system's camera to check how things were going, and had witnessed Harris abusing her mum.

"The police had to break the door down," she said.

Abul Hussain, prosecuting, said the victim had lain helpless in her bed thinking she was going to die.

Harris had been "slumped on the floor" when police had entered the property, he said.

Harris pleaded guilty to being a care worker who ill-treated the victim and to criminal damage.

She had originally been charged with attempted robbery because of her demands about Elizabethâs money, but the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) dropped that charge.

Tracy said it "beggars belief that they couldn't see any physical assault there".

Andrew Evans, representing Harris, said his client was genuinely remorseful for her "wholly unacceptable behaviour", which he said was the result of her finding the vodka in the fridge.

Judge Rees imposed a three-month jail term, of which 40% will be served in custody.

Tracy added: "The judge's hands were tied by the sentencing guidelines. You could see he was raging.

"For her to be serving just over a month is unbelievable... We've been living this day in, day out, with my mother getting worse."

She said her mum "can't be left on her own at all now".

"She keeps thinking Louise is going to come back, and she has such vivid flashbacks that she's been put on sedatives.

"The effect is my mum will not wear the lifeline device because she thinks if she presses it the same thing will happen. We've had to fit a new front door with glass in the middle so she can see if someone is on the other side."

She said she wanted all homes where carers attended to be fitted with cameras, "because what if we didn't have this camera?"

Judge Rees said elderly people were entitled to be treated with "respect, dignity and humanity" but the defendant had been "heartless and cruel", showing a "callous disregard" for her welfare.

News.title: NHS 'will collapse' without social care reform, PM tells BBC
News.content:
Andy Burnham has told the BBC "the NHS will collapse" if social care is not reformed but said he could not put a timeline on changes.

In his first major interview since becoming prime minister, Burnham said he would not want to leave office without bringing in "substantial change" to the social care system.

The prime minister also suggested making it harder to claim benefits, saying the country had to get serious about getting the welfare bill down.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has meanwhile written to the prime minister, saying he should rule out tax rises or increased borrowing to fund social care reform.

Burnham told the BBC that if the government did not reform social care, the NHS would "collapse under the weight of trying to care for people who've really not needed to end up in the NHS system".

But pressed on whether he would create a new system before the next election, he said he "couldn't put a timeline on it right here, right now", though he would put "whatever political capital I have into fixing broken social care".

Burnham first proposed a universal system of social care in England in 2009 when he was health secretary under Gordon Brown and pursued the idea of a compulsory levy to fund it.

That Labour government also floated the idea of allowing people to defer the payment until after they died, which led to the Tories branding it a "death tax".

Burnham is due to make a speech on adult social care on Wednesday.

The BBC understands the PM will stop short of unveiling plans for a new system in this speech, instead announcing he is speeding up the Casey Commission, an independent review that has been considering possible solutions for social care.

Baroness Louise Casey is not expected to give her final recommendations until 2028, but Burnham wants to bring her schedule forward.

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Sarah Woolnough, chief executive of healthcare think tank the King's Fund, said the current "punitive system" meant that "quite a lot of people go without care that they need", with one in seven paying in excess of Â£100,000 for social care.

While Burnham has not yet outlined any plans, Woolnough told the BBC Radio 4's Today programme that reforms could range from making social care free at the point of need to placing a cap on the amount people spend.

"The PM has for a long time mooted the idea of a social care system similar to NHS," she said.

"It would be expensive but on the scale of what we spend on other public services - around Â£200bn on the NHS - we are talking for some of these options low billions per year."

Adult social care has proved a complex issue to tackle for successive governments.

Two years ago Sir Keir Starmer was criticised when Labour scrapped plans for an Â£86,000 cap on the amount people in England would spend on social care in their lifetime.

Badenoch wrote in her letter to Burnham that "any solution to the issues around social care must also be fair to those who have made provisions and saved up over the course of their lives".

Layla Moran, the Liberal Democrat MP who chairs the Health and Social Committee, told the Today programme: "We do need to discuss where the money is going to come from but also we need to all be putting our political capital into this."

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said he was ready to do "whatever I can to find a real and lasting consensus on social care".

"Family carers must be at the heart of any new system, everyone must get the care they need and no one should lose their home as a result," he said.

Reform Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said social care needed fixing but warned the party would fight any proposal for a "universal death tax".

He said: "It's not fair to raid people's life savings and drags hundreds of thousands more families into paying tax when their loved ones pass away."

News.title: Teens in court accused of murder after stabbing
News.content:
Three teenage boys have appeared in court charged with murder after a fatal stabbing in Luton.

Bedfordshire Police were called to reports of violent disorder at Kingsway Recreation Ground at about 18:30 BST on Friday, where a 17-year-old boy was found with stab wounds. He later died in hospital.

A 16-year-old and two 17-year-olds, who cannot be named because of their age, appeared at Luton Magistrates' Court charged with murder, violent disorder and possession of a bladed article.

They were remanded in custody pending a further court appearance.

Another 17-year-old boy arrested over the weekend has been released on bail pending further inquiries, while a further 17-year-old who was arrested on Friday, and who was being treated in hospital for serious injuries, remains in police custody.

Det Ch Insp Nick Gardener said: "We understand this was a shocking incident for the local community and we would like to reassure them that we have had detectives working tirelessly on this case throughout the weekend.

"High visibility patrols and an increased police presence in the area will continue."

News.title: Protester who climbed Big Ben tower sentenced
News.content:
Judge Tony Baumgartner, the recorder of Westminster, said: "This was well-planned offending and you knew precisely what you were doing."

He added that Day had "foolishly" climbed up the tower "far enough to cause very serious harm to you and possibly others if you fell".

The judge found Day had "little insight into your offending or any real remorse", but he noted he had not offended since the Big Ben incident and had strong personal mitigation including failing eyesight.

Day was ordered to attend up to 20 rehabilitation days and he will be electronically monitored for four months as part of his suspended sentence.

Prosecutor David Matthew previously told the court that Day's actions caused "serious disruption", including the closure of Westminster Bridge.

Jurors were told that mattresses were put down at the base of the tower to try to protect him because he was in a "precarious position".

Transport for London lost an estimated Â£25,000 in bus fares as diversions were put in place and routes curtailed, jurors were told.

CCTV played in court showed Day, wearing a black coat and a baseball cap, scaling the building barefoot.
