Emergency services tackling massive wildfires in Spain and France are in a race against time to get the blazes under control before another 40C heatwave hits Europe this week.

In France, flames have burned through an area roughly four times the size of Paris and are now just nine miles outside the country’s sixth-largest city of Bordeaux, with no sign of slowing down. In central Spain, three separate fronts remained active in the mountains northwest of Madrid in the provinces of Madrid, Toledo and Avila.

The crisis is expected to intensify further with temperatures set to hit 40C in Spain and France within days, according to the meteorological agencies of both countries. The soaring temperatures come amid warnings the wildfires in France could burn for weeks, if not months.

open image in gallery A forest fire rages in Saint-Jean-d'Illac, less than 20 miles from Bordeaux in France ( AFP/Getty )

“We are still in the midst of a crisis; we must remain vigilant," Sophie Brocas, prefect of Bordeaux’s Gironde region told Le Parisien on Monday. “The fire is not contained and remains extremely dangerous.

“This unprecedented blaze does not follow any known pattern; it creates its own winds and requires constant adaptation.”

Authorities have so far evacuated about 250,000 people in France, including holidaymakers and residents, while in Spain around 116,000 have been told to leave their homes or seek shelter. Wildfires have also impacted Italy and Portugal, with the UK government confirming on Monday it is preparing for a similar crisis.

“What we're experiencing isn't a succession of isolated events,” Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday. “It's the most painful expression of a climate emergency that is making sixth-generation wildfires more ferocious, heatwaves more frequent, and our territory more vulnerable.”

open image in gallery Emmanuel Macron during a situation briefing in the crisis room at the Departmental Fire and Rescue Operational Centre in Bordeaux on Monday ( AP )

open image in gallery Firefighters tackle a blaze as wildfires rage near Le Las, outside Bordeaux on Monday ( AP )

KEY FIGURES SO FAR:

116,000 hectares burned in France this year, including 42,000 from the blaze near Bordeaux

360,000 people evacuated, including 250,000 in France and 116,000 in Spain

2,500 firefighters, 1,500 military personnel, and 1,200 police officers and gendarmes battling blaze in Gironde, France

75 firefighters injured and at least two dead

162 people arrested on suspicion of arson in France

On Monday, French president Emmanuel Macron called a crisis meeting of his cabinet to discuss how to battle the fires, after reassuring the country over the weekend that the government would offer support to people “for as long as is needed”.

Mr Macron urged fire crews to “stay strong”, warning that the fight will take time but vowing: “We will win this battle together.”

On a visit to a coordination centre for the massive firefighting effort in southwest France on Monday, Mr Macron heard how the blaze raging since last week has been wildly unpredictable, transforming at times into a self-feeding fire storm.

“We're facing a completely unprecedented fire,” Mr Macron said, describing the situation as France's worst fire-related crisis since the Second World War..

He praised firefighting teams who stopped the inferno's progression after successive days of spreading flames. But with woodlands still smouldering, he cautioned that the battle isn’t yet won. The weeks ahead will be hard,” he said.

France’s prime minister Sebastien Lecornu said the country was going through an “unprecedented fire season”, with the area burned already having surpassed the previous record year of 2022. The European Union's European Forest Fire Information System estimates that over 300,000 hectares have burned in France and Spain as a result of wildfires since January this year.

The extreme fires come after a series of scorching heatwaves across western Europe, with highs of 45C reported earlier this month.

open image in gallery Smoke rises as flames burn during a wildfire at Ares, Gironde ( Reuters )

France’s meteorological agency, Météo-France, warned that the next heatwave would settle over the country on Tuesday and that on Wednesday temperatures will continue to rise, with intense heat peaking across much of the western half of the country.

Emmanuel Cerisier, who lives near Bordeaux, told The Independent that there is an overwhelming feeling of “tension and anxiety” as people wonder whether they will have to evacuate.

“Over the last two or three days, we’re experiencing fog and clouds of ashes and you get the smell pretty much all the time,” said Mr Cerisier, who lives with his wife and daughters, aged 18 and 16.

“Even in the city centre of Bordeaux, when the winds get stronger, you can get clouds of ashes that darken the sky. It’s easy to spot here when it starts and it can stay a few hours.

“Elderly people are wearing masks in the city so if you go out in the city centre, it will remind you of the Covid era.

“You get the taste of ashes that burn in your throat when you’re in the middle of those clouds. My kids and wife don’t want to go out when the winds are blowing in our direction.”

open image in gallery An aircraft dumps water over a wildfire burning near San Martin de Valdeiglesias, about 40 miles west of Madrid ( AFP/Getty )

Authorities warned that some of the fires had become so large they had generated their own rare weather system, sparking thunderstorms and strong winds.

“This smoke cloud generates its own weather system, causing anything in its path to spontaneously combust. It is unprecedented in France,” said Eric Brocardi, a spokesperson for the National Firefighters Federation of France. The “fire cloud” phenomena is typically witnessed during volcanic eruptions and can create its own wind and lightning.

Tourists have also been advised to stay away from the region due to low air quality, and on Monday the Bordeaux airport hotel zone was evacuated until further notice, although the airport itself remains operational.

In a statement overnight, the airport said that the decision to close all hotels in its immediate vicinity was made in accordance with the Gironde prefecture.

While flights are still operational, the airport said no accommodation can be provided at the airport itself, which closes overnight. It advised travellers to look outside the evacuated areas or at the Parc des Expositions.

The Lord of the Rings trilogy made billions at the box office, but actor Sean Astin has admitted that his salary was so ”small” he had to sell his house.

A former child star who rose to fame at 13 as the star of The Goonies, Astin is best known to audiences for his role as the loyal Samwise Gamgee in Peter Jackson’s epic film series.

In a new interview, the actor, who starred in the three Lord of the Rings films between 2001 and 2003, told The Guardian that while starring in the franchise gave him a “level of visibility and access” he was unprepared for, the financials left much to be desired.

“There was a disconnect between the attention that I was getting and how much money we had,” the 55-year-old said. “It was not a lot of money! In fact, I had to sell my house because I negotiated such a small amount on the trilogy.”

open image in gallery Astin said that there was a ‘disconnect’ between the film’s success and the cast’s salaries ( Getty )

Back in 2017, actor and trade union leader Astin revealed in an interview that he was paid $250,000 (£190,000) to appear in the trilogy, adding that he got “no residuals” either.

Directed by Peter Jackson, the Lord of the Rings films were blockbusters. Made on a budget of around $281m (£214m), they brought in $2.9bn (£2.2bn) worldwide.

That this was not reflected in the cast’s salaries has been touched on by members of the ensemble in interviews over the years.

Appearing on Watch What Happens Live, Cate Blanchett, who played Galadriel in the JRR Tolkien adaptation, said that ”no one got paid anything to do that movie”, before jokingly adding: ”I basically got free sandwiches, and I got to keep my ears as pay.”

Elijah Wood, who played Astin’s on-screen best friend (and the franchise’s lead) Frodo Baggins, also opened up about the pay issue last April.

Wood explained that production company New Line Cinema had taken “a real gamble” on the massive ensemble cast, leading to an “understandable” trade-off where the cast were on “not massive salaries” as a result.

open image in gallery Elijah Wood (left) and Sean Astin in 2004, one year after the final Lord of the Rings film was released ( Getty )

The actors also shot the films back to back, Wood explained, and “because we weren’t making one movie and then renegotiating a contract for the next, it wasn’t the sort of lucrative scenario that you could sort of rest easy for the rest of your life,” he revealed.

The actor disagreed with rumours that he was paid $250,000 (£190,000) to star in the first instalment, The Fellowship of the Ring, saying that it “doesn’t matter” what the real number was.

“The benefit of that was that we were also signing up for something that was going to be a part of our lives forever,” he said.

Orlando Bloom, who played Legolas, said in 2017 that he received $175,000 (£133,000) for all three films.

“Nothing, nothing, nothing. I got nothing. 175 grand for three movies,” he said, going on to clarify: “No, listen, greatest gift of my life, are you kidding me? Would do it again for half the money.”

News.title: Idaho college killer Bryan Kohberger claims he was duped into pleading guilty and now wants a trial
News.content:

Bryan Kohberger, the 31-year-old man who pleaded guilty to murdering four University of Idaho students, said in a statement Monday that he wants to abandon his confession and go to trial, citing concerns he had with the plea deal process.

Kohberger, a former criminology student convicted of murdering the four students in their home in 2022, said he was innocent and that the plea deal “hinged on false promises and blatant disinformation,” in a statement to the New York Times.

“Over a year later, it is self-evident that, in State v. Kohberger, justice was not served,” Kohberger wrote. “Unanswered questions seem to multiply with each piece of discovery unsealed, and the public demands the truth.”

“My actual innocence is my truth, and the plea, hinged on by false promises and blatant disinformation, MUST be withdrawn.”

Kohberger did not explain what specific concerns he had with the plea deal, though he mentioned evidence, the probable cause affidavit and a “broken plea.”

open image in gallery Bryan Kohberger, who last year pleaded guilty to murdering four college students, maintained his innocence in a new statement ( Getty )

“Why am I breaking my silence?” Kohberger told the New York Times by phone on Sunday. “A lot went wrong in those plea discussions. I really do want that to be heard.”

He declined to discuss specific evidence in a phone interview with the New York Times. Still, he said that “the intention is for all of those questions to be investigated and answered appropriately in a trial setting.”

Kohberger is currently serving four consecutive life sentences for the murders of Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Ethan Chapin and Xana Kernodle, which he confessed to in July 2025 just weeks before a trial was set to take place.

As part of the plea deal, the death penalty was taken off the table in exchange for Kohberger’s admission. He also waived his right to any appeal or the chance of parole in accepting the deal.

open image in gallery Kohberger, pictured in 2023, had initially refused to enter a plea in the murders of Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Ethan Chapin and Xana Kernodle – he later entered a guilty plea in exchange for taking the death penalty off the table ( Getty )

The four University of Idaho students were murdered inside their off-campus house in Moscow, Idaho, on November 13, 2022. The tragedy rocked the town, which had not experienced a homicide in seven years, and captivated the nation.

Kohberger was arrested weeks after the murders, in late December.

Law enforcement officials had linked Kohberger to the murders through DNA evidence from a knife sheath found at the scene of the murders, as well as surveillance footage of a car that matched Kohberger's in the area at the time of the murders, and cell phone tower data.

News.title: Holly Willoughby hints first YouTube channel guest is Hollywood icon
News.content:
Holly Willoughby has teased the first guest on her new YouTube channel, who appears to be a Hollywood star.

The former This Morning presenter has launched her new lifestyle series, Together, which will cover topics such as practical advice, fashion, beauty and health.

Stanley Tucci appears to be Willoughby’s first guest.

“Not only is he in every single film that has ever existed, he also happens to be an extraordinary cook,” Willoughby hinted in a teaser video posted to her Instagram on Monday (27 July).

Dance Moms alum Paige Hyland is firing back at people who make comments about her body.

The former reality star, 25, shared a video on her TikTok account Saturday responding to “diabolical” comments accusing her of having an eating disorder in the comments of her latest Instagram post, which featured her wearing a bikini on vacation.

“Get ready with me while we talk about why it’s never okay to comment on someone’s body,” said Hyland, who was on the first four seasons of the hit Lifetime reality show. “It’s 2026, I thought we all knew this but I guess we need a little refresher.”

She went on to say, “I posted this picture on Instagram and honestly, the comments I got were actually diabolical. There were so many people saying I looked anorexic, I’m promoting unhappy eating habits and that, as an influencer, I shouldn’t be encouraging this behavior.”

“But as an influencer, I feel like it’s my responsibility to stand up for people whose bodies naturally look like mine,” Hyland said.

Hyland said that she has been thin her entire life and that “losing weight has never been a goal.” She then shut down claims about her having an eating disorder.

“I’m also seeing people confidently say that I’ve opened up about having an eating disorder, which is just not true,” she said. “I’ve never came out and said that because I’ve never had one, which I’m extremely grateful for.”

She said: “But if I did have an eating disorder, imagine reading comments from thousands of people picking apart my body and diagnosing me when they have no idea what’s going on? That is not concern, that is public body-shaming disguised as concern, which is not cute.”

Hyland went on to insist that she has always been naturally thin, despite the fact that she “eats everything.”

Paige Hyland, pictured here in April 2024, was on the first four seasons of reality show 'Dance Moms' ( Getty )

“While I’m confident in myself, I know there’s other girls who probably look like me that are reading the comments on my picture thinking there’s something wrong with their bodies,” she said. “That genuinely makes me sick to my stomach. Just like it’s wrong for shaming someone for being bigger, it’s also wrong for shaming them for being smaller.”

She ended the clip by demanding that the body positivity movement include all types of bodies.

“So before you go to comment on someone’s weight, whether it’s, ‘You look too skinny,’ ‘Eat a burger,’ whatever it is, just don’t,” she concluded. “Instead, maybe compliment their smile or tell them that you like their outfit. There’s so many other things you can do besides commenting on someone’s body.”

If you or someone you know struggles with an eating disorder, visit the National Alliance for Eating Disorders website or call their hotline at (866) 662-1235

Labour has overtaken Reform UK in the polls for the first time in more than a year, buoyed by the momentum from Andy Burnham’s first week as prime minister.

According to a survey by pollsters More in Common, Labour is now leading with 28 per cent, up four points, while Nigel Farage’s Reform are down two points on 24 per cent.

It is the first time since March 2025 that Labour has led the way, with Reform in second place and the Tories just behind in third on 22 per cent.

Labour appears to have benefited from the “Burnham bounce”, as well as a fall in support for the Greens, who had been winning voters from Labour’s left flank but have gone down three points in a week to a mere 8 per cent.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Alastair Grant/PA) ( PA Wire )

Luke Tryl, the UK director at More in Common, said: “It’s only been a week since he entered office, but it’s clear that momentum is on the prime minister’s side. After a jam-packed week of high-profile policy announcements and media appearances, the Labour Party has surged in our weekly poll.

“With all the caveats that it’s just one poll, Labour now leads for the first time since March of last year, and holds their highest vote share since the early months of this government in 2024. And with both Reform and the Green Party dropping to their lowest vote share in months, it seems that this early focus on the cost of living has appealed to voters Labour has lost on both the left and right.”

The findings come a week after Mr Burnham officially took over as prime minister from Sir Keir Starmer, who was forced out after Labour MPs lost confidence in his ability to beat Mr Farage.

Even more significantly, the poll suggests that if there were a general election, Labour would win with 325 seats, down 86, giving them a very narrow working majority.

The Tories would come second with 124 seats while Reform would be in third place with 88.

In an interview with the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg, Mr Burnham has moved to rule out a suggestion of an early election.

He said: “There is no early general election, and the thing I would say to you is 20 plus – how many million people you just mentioned voted for a manifesto, we’re in a parliamentary democracy so that is what people voted for.”

While Mr Burnham has been criticised for avoiding press conferences and scrutiny, his attempts to love-bomb voters with social media clips appear to have had early returns.

Meanwhile, Mr Farage has found himself in crisis over questions about an undeclared £5m donation from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne and his associations with convicted money launderer George Cottrell.

The Reform UK leader has also become a figure of fun after forcing a by-election in his own constituency with the main parties boycotting it, while he is up against 33 minor candidates, with the main challenger being the comedic candidate Count Binface.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to keep one of its largest and most expensive detention facilities open for at least another year despite calls to close it over reported human rights abuses, according to a notice published last week.

ICE plans to extend the no-bid contract of the firm that runs Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, through Sept. 30, 2027, at a potential additional cost to taxpayers of $776 million, the notice says. This is on top of a $452 million initial contract that the firm, Amentum Services Inc., was awarded in March when it was hastily installed to take over the camp’s operation from a contractor removed for poor performance.

For months, Democratic members of Congress and several advocacy organizations have called for Camp East Montana to be closed, citing reports that detainees have been routinely mistreated since its opening in August 2025.

A report released earlier this month by Human Rights Watch and the American Civil Liberties Union alleged that staff routinely beat detainees, denied them medical care, made them live in filthy conditions and fed them inedible meals. Reports by federal agencies have also found unsafe detention conditions and that the Army and ICE have wasted millions of dollars paying for unnecessary services. At least three Camp East Montana detainees have died.

The facility at Fort Bliss, an Army base near the U.S.-Mexico border, has housed an average of more than 2,000 male and female detainees a day since Oct. 1, though its population has declined significantly in recent months, according to ICE data.

“Extending Amentum’s contract while ignoring well-documented abuses is reckless and demonstrates the Trump administration’s full-scale assault on human rights,” said Angélica César, a fellow at Human Rights Watch and the ACLU who was a lead researcher for the report. “Instead of holding private contractors accountable, DHS is choosing to perpetuate a system of harm and abuse.”

Chanel Mann, a spokesperson for Amentum, referred questions to ICE and its parent agency, the Department of Homeland Security, which didn’t immediately return messages seeking comment.

ICE's notice was a justification for extending Amentum Services’ contract for a year without a competitive bidding process.

The agency argued that relocating detainees to other facilities would be “impracticable” due to a lack of available bed space elsewhere. Transitioning to a different contractor would require replacing Amentum’s “proprietary infrastructure” and finding new workers, which would lead to duplicative costs, it said.

“Any lapse in contract coverage would directly threaten the life, safety, and well-being of detainees, severely disrupt law enforcement operations, and expose the government to substantial operational, legal, and humanitarian risks,” the notice says.

ICE's notice said the Army's initial contract, awarded to Acquisition Logistics LLC, “did not accurately reflect ICE's operational needs or the actual usage of the facility.” Acquisition Logistics had no prior experience operating detention facilities.

In all, Virginia-based Amentum stands to be paid more than $1.2 billion if it operates the camp from March 2026 through September 2027, the notice says.

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on thousands of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

News.title: Amazon has ended support for pre-2013 Kindles. What to do if you’re affected (and what to avoid)
News.content:
It seems like a lot of devices, but Amazon told Engadget that the move will affect around three per cent of current users. In theory, if you’re using a device that’s affected, then Amazon should already have notified you via email. If in doubt, however, the company has a support page with pictures and specifications of every Kindle ever released. If you’re still unsure, entering the model number into Google should reveal the exact version you’re using. This can typically be found on the back of devices.

For Kindle Fire tablets, the process is simpler. Open the Settings menu and select “Device Options”. You’ll find the model you’re using either under “Device Model” or “About Fire Tablet”.

Why did this happen?

Nobody expects electronic devices to be supported forever, but it’s disappointing that the Kindle’s most enthusiastic early adopters got cut off. Given the basic functionality of e-book reader technology, there doesn’t appear to be a technical reason behind the decision, making it appear like an anti-consumer move to push older customers towards the purchase of newer devices where existing Kindles would become an e-waste casualty.

When asked why these devices were losing support, we received a response defending the (admittedly impressive) longevity.

“These models have been supported for at least 14 years – some as long as 18 years – but technology has come a long way in that time, and these devices will no longer be supported moving forward,” an Amazon spokesperson said. “We are notifying those still actively using them and offering promotions to help with the transition to newer devices.”

At the initial time of writing, the promotions mentioned appeared to be 20 per cent off “select new Kindle devices” alongside a £15 eBook credit. While the latter was welcome, the highlighted discount is somewhat disappointing for a number of reasons. Firstly, according to the promotion’s terms and conditions, the “select” caveat excludes the most expensive model, the Kindle Scribe. It doesn’t apply to Fire devices for those tablet owners looking to replace like-for-like, either.

More importantly, the prices aren’t all that impressive considering happy owners of older Kindles weren’t budgeting for this purchase. Amazon frequently discounts its own-brand devices like Echo smart speakers and Fire tablets, and 20 per cent isn’t that unusual. Last year’s Black Friday sale saw discounts of over 30 per cent on the basic Kindle and Kindle Colorsoft, and the price-tracking site CamelCamelCamel shows that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition has been as low as £183 in the past – a 32 per cent discount on its current price of £269.

There was added time pressure, too. Amazon said the discount and credit offer was only valid until June 20, one month after support for the older Kindles ended.

Additionally, owners of the earliest UK Kindle will see that prices have gone up over the past decade. The £109 they paid in 2010 is some way off the £159.99 Kindle Paperwhite, even with a 20 per cent discount, let alone the £219.99 Kindle Colorsoft. That said, at £94.99, the basic Kindle 12th Generation remains a bargain for no-frills readers, with a 20 per cent discount taking it down to £75.99.

Possible upgrades

If you’re affected by this news, the silver lining is that while e-book technology moves relatively slowly, things have still advanced significantly in the past 14 years. Resolutions are higher; most are backlit for bedtime reading; there’s support for audiobooks; and storage has increased. There are also optional extras like colour screens, blue-light filters to prevent eye strain and waterproofing.

As outlined in our guide to the best Kindles, our pick for most people is the 12th Generation Kindle Paperwhite, which costs £159.99 with lockscreen ads or £169.99 without. The seven inch screen with warm lighting makes for a comfortable reading experience, and it’s waterproof for bathtime or poolside reading.

At £94.99 (or £104.99 without ads), the basic 11th Generation Kindle is a great budget pick, however. It’s slightly smaller at six inches, and like the Paperwhite, can hold around 8,000 e-books with support for audiobooks through Audible. It lacks the warm light and waterproofing, however, and its battery life is around half that of the Paperwhite — albeit still a generous six weeks of normal use.

The two remaining Kindles occupy specific niches. The Kindle Colorsoft has a colour screen, making it well suited to those who enjoy graphic novels. The Kindle Scribe, meanwhile, has a bundled stylus for note taking.

Can I still use my old Kindle?

Yes, Amazon said users would be able to “continue to read books already downloaded on these devices”. If you factory reset your older Kindle, however, or you deregister it, you won’t be able to use it anymore.

News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

Sports.title: Chelsea lead race to sign Jordan Henderson in shock free transfer as two more clubs battling for England star
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are plotting a shock swoop for Brentford star Jordan Henderson.

The Blues are aiming to add more experience this summer and see the England veteran as an ideal addition.



Henderson, 36, joined Brentford on a two-year deal ahead of last season following 18 months at Ajax.

Keith Andrews‘ side could now grant him a free transfer to Chelsea as he prolongs his career at the top level.



The Blues are not the only club interested, however, with two other Prem sides believed to be chasing the midfielder’s signature.

Henderson was part of Thomas Tuchel‘s England World Cup squad and was seen as a valuable leader in the dressing room.

This makes him a suitable candidate for Chelsea’s transfer strategy this summer, which has pivoted from almost entirely focusing on recruiting talented young players to aiming for more experience.

Earlier this summer the Blues targeted Sunderland’s 33-year-old former Arsenal midfielder Granit Xhaka.

And today it emerged that they want to add Brighton striker Danny Welbeck, 35, to their forward line.

SunSport also reported last week that the Blues are considering a swoop for John Stones, who is a free agent after leaving Manchester City at the end of last season.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Henderson began his career at Sunderland and played 79 times for the Black Cats before landing a move to Liverpool in 2011.

The boyhood Mackem starred at Anfield for 12 years, succeeding Steven Gerrard as captain and going on to win a Premier League title, the Champions League, an FA Cup, two League Cups and the Club World Cup.

After seeing his minutes start to decline, Henderson opted to reunite with Gerrard at Al-Ettifaq in the summer of 2023.

The England star received plenty of criticism for his Saudi move and quickly decided to return to Europe, signing for Ajax in January 2024.



Henderson soon got his career back on track in Amsterdam, playing 57 times for the Dutch giants ahead of a Premier League return with Brentford in 2025.

He subsequently helped the Bees to a ninth place finish.

Having been in the international wilderness between November 2023 and March 2025, Henderson has since become a regular in Tuchel’s England squads.



The 90-cap star was picked for this summer’s World Cup, but was limited to just one cameo appearance from the bench.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

During the celebrations of England’s 3-2 win in Mexico, Henderson suffered a broken arm as he fell while vaulting an advertising board.

It remains to be seen when he will fully recover from the injury.

Sports.title: Former Premier League manager left so furious by calamitous pre-season goal he starts vaping on sidelines
Sports.content:
WALTER MAZZARRI was left so glum he started vaping after two goalkeeper howlers in a pre-season loss.

Mazzarri, 64, took over Greek minnows Iraklis earlier this month and oversaw their first friendly against Bologna on Saturday in Italy.



The Elder went on to lose 2-0 in Bolzano after two errors committed by two different keepers.

The Serie A outfit opened the scoring after just seven minutes when Giorgos Athanasiadis committed the first blunder.



Athanasiadis, 33, got such a heavy touch on the ball that he lost it and set up Thijs Dallinga for an easy opener.

The Greece international was replaced by Panagiotis Tsintotas in the second half when Bologna got a penalty that shouldn’t have been given.

Former Norwich ace Jonathan Rowe took it on and doubled the Italians’ lead on 58 minutes.

Tsintotas, 33, got to the ball as he lunged to his right and could have held on to it but it still slipped out of his hands.

That’s when the camera panned in on Mazzarri watching from Iraklis’ bench.

The ex-Watford boss looked bewildered – probably from the two errors as well as the referee’s wrong decision to award Bologna a penalty.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

So much so that the ex-Napoli boss started smoking his vape while the game continued.

The ex-Sampdoria boss’ assistant Ieroklis Stoltidis was also left completely frustrated.

Mazzarri joined Iraklis after two years without a club as his second stint at Napoli ended in 2024.

The ex-Inter Milan boss spent a year at Watford but he left in 2017 despite securing Premier League status after a gruelling relegation scrap.

Sports.title: Premier League and EFL to implement radical new rule forcing teams to play with TEN men starting this season
Sports.content:
ENGLISH football is set to trial a new rule in a bid to prevent goalkeepers “bending rules” by going down for treatment.

Last season saw plenty of instances in which goalkeepers were seen by a physio on the pitch, allowing team-mates to receive instructions from their managers and breaking up the action.



When an outfielder is seen by the physio, they must leave the field – unless an opponent has been carded for the challenge that caused the injury.

The rule was taken on ahead of the 2023/24 campaign but goalkeepers had been immune and could get treatment on the pitch.



According to the BBC, however, that is about to change.

They report that the PGMOL have opted to trial a system that will see teams have to nominate an outfield player to go off for one minute if their goalkeeper has had treatment.



If no player has been selected within 10 seconds, the captain will be forced off.

The trial is subject to being approved by global refereeing body IFAB.

It is set to be used across the Premier League, English Football League, Women’s Super League and National League.

The trial could begin as soon as Saturday, when Tranmere host Rochdale in the Carabao Cup preliminary round.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After Gianluigi Donnarumma went down during a clash between Leeds and Manchester City last November, Whites boss Daniel Farke said: “If we don’t educate our players in football what to do in terms of fair play and sportsmanship and whatever and if we just try to bend the rules and even do a fake injury in order to do an additional team talk, it is not what I like personally.

“But if it is within the rules I can’t complain.”

In February last year, Bolton boss Steven Schumacher even admitted to using the ploy as a deliberate tactic.

Schumacher said: “I can’t complain about it because I have done it myself, so I’m not immune to it.

“It’s a ploy, a tactic that kills the momentum of the game when the opposition is on top and if you time it right you can really affect the game and there’s a chance to get your team in.



“It happens pretty much in every game now, even in the Champions League. I was laughing last week watching one of the Champions League games and thinking ‘we’ll it’s not just in England then,’ so it’s just part of the game now.”

After using the tactic last season, Plymouth Argyle boss Tom Cleverley admitted: “My thoughts are, to be completely honest with you, I think it’s wrong, there’s an element of embarrassment when you do it.

“Schuey was the same last weekend, but why would you not? I’m here to get results for this football club so if there is something I can do to help that I’m going to do it.

“Do I feel like it should be taken away from us as coaches? Yeah. There should be a caveat to that.

“That’s my feelings, but whilst I can do something to help our football team I will do it.”

Liam Delap and Emmanuel Emegha joined the club for a combined total of £51.5 million last summer.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Girona live stream: How to watch the Gunners’ first public preseason game
Sports.content:
THE reigning Premier League champions will face the cameras for the first time this preseason as they jet off to Girona.

Mikel Arteta‘s title winners kickstarted preparations to retain their crown in 2026/27 by swatting aside MK Dons 3-0 in a secret training ground meeting held behind closed doors.



A sprinkling of World Cup stars are set to rejoin the Gunners’ ranks, with Kai Havertz, Piero Hincapie and Viktor Gyokeres‘ respective firepower back at Arteta’s disposal.

Those among the travelling party will look to cut through the off-field noise, amid rampant rumours that the club could splurge on superstars such as Bradley Barcola, Bruno Guimarães or Vinicius Jr.



While penalty heartbreak denied Arsenal from completing the Champions League and Premier League double in their last competitive fixture, their Catalonian opponents endured the ignominy of relegation from LaLiga.

Girona will be hoping to draw on fonder memories from their own title charge in 2023/24, when they led the Spanish top flight until December before ultimately finishing third.



The two sides are familiar foes, having locked horns in a closely fought Champions League encounter in January 2025, during which Girona snatched an early lead before Arsenal secured a 1-2 comeback.

How to watch Arsenal vs Girona and is there a live stream?

Arsenal’s return to public action can be streamed live on the club website and app with a valid subscription.

Their Catalonian affair kicks off at 7pm BST on Saturday, August 1 at Girona’s Estadi Montilivi.

What other games are available to watch this preseason?

Fans can catch all four of the Gunner’s remaining preseason outings via Arsenal’s online or in-app channels by taking advantage of a £9.99 early-bird offer (available until 9am BST on August 1, subsequently £14.99).

The North London titans will also be available to watch on TNT Sports later next month when they go head-to-head with Manchester City for the Community Shield.

Sports.title: Man Utd in advanced talks with Juventus over loan transfer exit with £30m option to buy
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Joshua Zirkzee is a top target for Juventus after a deal for Randal Kolo Muani collapsed.

Zirkzee looks to be out of favour at Old Trafford after starting just five Prem games under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick last season.



The Dutchman, 25, is a wanted man this summer and SunSport understands Juventus are now leading the chase to sign him on loan with a £30million option to buy.

The Turin outfit looked set to sign France international Kolo Muani from Paris Saint-Germain after his unsuccessful loan with Tottenham last season.



But Juventus have been unable to agree a fee with PSG after negotiations stalled.

The Serie A giants have now quickly pivoted to Zirkzee as they line up a new No9.



The club weren’t happy at the pace of talks and were concerned they were losing time in their bid to bolster their attacking options.

Juventus are the most serious club pursuing Zirkzee, though Roma also have a long-time interest in the forward.

Luciano Spalletti’s side are the favourites for his signature, however, after moving much faster in talks.

Zirkzee, who has netted just nine times in 75 appearances for the Red Devils, is keen on a move to the Allianz Stadium.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He knows Serie A well after spending one season on loan at Parma and two playing for Bologna.

Zirkzee sees the Italian top flight as a much better tactical fit for his style of play.

He has struggled for confidence at United and sees Juventus as the right step for his career at this stage.

SunSport has been told that Zirkzee’s representatives have given a positive response to the approach from Juventus.



United are willing to accept a loan move and £30m buy option despite spending around £36.5m to sign him in 2024.

Officials recognise the fee is a fair reflection of his value after failing to deliver consistency at the club.

Zirkzee is currently behind Benjamin Sesko and Mateus Cunha in the pecking order, while Marcus Rashford could return to the squad this season.

Juventus are desperate to bring in Zirkzee after Dusan Vlahovic left the club on a free transfer, while Jonathan David has also struggled for goals.

David scored just six times in 35 games in Serie A last season.

Sports.title: Benjamin Sesko injury update after Man Utd striker missed first two pre-season friendlies with shin problem
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED striker Benjamin Sesko is on schedule to return from a shin injury before the new season starts.

Sesko, 23, missed United’s first two pre-season friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg as he continues to follow a rehabilitation program.



Carrington sources say Sesko’s recovery is going to plan and he was never scheduled to participate in the opening friendlies.

Sesko was already nursing a shin injury that he aggravated in the 3-2 win against Liverpool on May 3.



United were vague about the extent of the injury at the time and the final three games of last season that Sesko sat out are set to be the only ones he misses.

The Slovenia international started outdoor training last week and has a chance of being involved against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday.



Sesko is likely to start against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on August 8 and United fly from Sweden to Dublin for a six-day training camp.

United play Leeds United at Croke Park on August 12, their penultimate friendly before they start the Premier League season against Hull City on August 22.

Sesko’s absence allowed Joshua Zirkzee to start against Wrexham and Rosenborg, despite United’s preference to sell him.

A sale is a long shot as United would require around £21million to avoid a loss on Zirkzee, who arrived for £36.5m in July 2024.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Zirkzee, 25, has generated interest from a number of Italian clubs during his time at United and a loan return to Serie A remains likely.

United want to sign a new striker to support Sesko but denied there had been any contact with Danny Welbeck before Chelsea registered their interest in the Brighton forward.

Welbeck scored 14 goals for Brighton last term and has always been open to a possible homecoming at United.

But Chelsea have moved for the 35-year-old, who is out of contract at Brighton next year.

Sports.title: Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing
Sports.content:
Chelsea want Jordan Henderson as Xabi Alonso lines up another shock signing

Jordan Henderson is a target for multiple Premier League clubs, with Brentford willing to let him go on a free transfer, and Chelsea are understood to be leading the race for his services

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is another shock target for Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Chelsea are working on a surprise move for Jordan Henderson, sitting first in the queue of Premier League clubs who are interested in signing him. Henderson, 36, has an agreement which will him to leave Brentford on a free transfer, despite having one year left on his contract.

‌



The midfielder is currently injured after breaking his arm during England's celebrations following their last-16 win against Mexico at the World Cup. Henderson stayed in North America for the rest of the tournament, remaining a key figure within the dressing room.

‌



His leadership and experience are part of why Xabi Alonso wants to bring him to Stamford Bridge. The Athletic report that Chelsea are the leading contenders for the former Liverpool captain's signature.

‌



It's added that multiple Premier League clubs also want to sign him. Chelsea's interest comes after they opened talks with Brighton to sign 35-year-old Danny Welbeck, further proof of their change of transfer policy since Alonso was appointed.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Last month, the Blues bid £8m for Granit Xhaka after the Sunderland captain signalled that he'd be willing reunite with Alonso, who he played under at Bayer Leverkusen. Sunderland flatly rejected the offer and Xhaka will stay.

‌



Henderson is seen as alternative, with Alonso wanting an experienced head in midfield, while he also gets on well with Chelsea's new £117million signing, Morgan Rogers. The England international only joined Brentford a year ago from Ajax, previously playing for Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq having left Liverpool in July 2023.

But his impact off the pitch is valued, too. After beating France 6-4 in the World Cup third-place play-off, England boss Thomas Tuchel revealed that the 35-year-old had given a powerful speech pre-match speech which motivated his team-mates.

"Jordan Henderson gave a very impressive speech today in the hotel to put this in the right frame and put everyone in the right mindset," Tuchel explained. "So he helped unbelievably today.

‌



Should Jordan Henderson join Chelsea? Have your say in the comments section.

"That was very emotional and very, very impressive to put this game into perspective. I won't say what he said, but it puts into it perspective because he was part of this match eight years ago.

‌



"It was very emotional and he put into perspective what you might feel in the very moment, that you might give in to the feeling 'I don't want to be here'. He took all of that away because he said that it means the world in the end, and he would give anything if he hadn't broken his arm to be part again in this match.

"You never know when you get a World Cup match for England. He said it much, much better than me and more emotional, and it was very impressive. He set the tone and the mindset for this match."

Sports.content:
Man Utd star takes drastic action as Ruben Amorim plots transfer reunion

One Manchester United player could be set for a departure from Old Trafford and a reunion with a former boss in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Manchester United star Noussair Mazraoui has been linked with a reunion with Ruben Amorim (Image: (Photo by Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Manchester United defender Noussair Mazraoui has reportedly switched agents as speculation continues to mount regarding a potential departure from Old Trafford. Reports earlier this summer suggested new AC Milan manager and former United boss Ruben Amorim was interested in reuniting with the Morocco international.

‌



The Serie A outfit is searching for a wing-back to feature in Amorim's favoured 3-4-3 system, with Mazraoui being considered. Italian reports indicate the Serie A side would pursue a deal for the United defender, provided decision-makers at Old Trafford signal their willingness to sell.

‌



Amorim had previously heaped praise on Mazraoui during his Old Trafford tenure, saying: "He’s a top player. He understands the game. He knows how to attack, he’s very technical, he’s very good defensively and he’s very good one-on-one."

‌



There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

There are, however, questions about what position the Moroccan World Cup star would occupy in Amorim's setup, having also featured as a centre-back under the Portuguese manager during his spell at Old Trafford. According to Fabrizio Romano, Mazraoui has joined new agency Panthera, who will handle his representation going forward, though it's unclear whether there's any direct link between that choice and a potential transfer this summer.

‌



Amorim, speaking in December 2024, added: "He’s a modern player. I think he’s the future of our team. When you think about him, you think we need more players like Nous that can control the tempo, they are really, really good and comfortable with the ball. So, Nous, I’m really happy with him."

The Moroccan defender was a regular for his country as they reached the latter stages of the World Cup, just a few months on from reaching the African Cup of Nations final. The 28-year-old defender made 20 appearances for United last season, sitting out a substantial portion of the campaign for the African Cup of Nations.

‌



Mazraoui found it difficult to regain his spot in Michael Carrick's team after coming back from the winter competition, but did catch the eye of the then-interim United manager, eventually reclaiming his place in the starting XI.

"Yeah he's come back well, Nous," Carrick said last season after reintegrating Mazraoui back into the side. "It was a difficult one, obviously, on the back of the final and how it panned out.

"[He had] a few days to digest that then back in and around it. He's been fantastic in and around the group and around training.

"Obviously, he came on at the end of the game and played a part for us, as you'd expect. So yeah, again [we want to] just keep thickening the squad, bolstering the squad and it's great to have him back."

Sports.content:
Man Utd get fresh Benjamin Sesko injury update after star missed pre-season friendlies

Benjamin Sesko continues to edge towards full fitness after missing Manchester United's early pre-season friendlies and is on target to play in their Premier League opener

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit for the start of the Premier League

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko is on course to be fit before the Premier League season starts despite missing successive pre-season friendlies.

‌



The Slovenian has been struggling with a shin injury and that meant he was absent for games against Wrexham and Rosenborg as he continues to follow a rehabilitation program. Sesko was already nursing a shin injury that he aggravated in the win over Liverpool in early May.

‌



United kept their cards close to their chest regarding the extent of the injury at the time as the striker missed the last three games of the campaign having been a regular up until then.

‌



However, The Sun reports that Sesko’s recovery is going to plan and he was never scheduled to participate in their opening two friendlies.

The ex-RB Leipzig man began outdoor training last week and has a chance of being involved against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm on Saturday as he bids to build on what was an impressive debut season, despite a slow start leading to some doubts over his signing.

‌



Sesko is likely to start against PSG in Gothenburg on August 8 before the entire United squad fly from Sweden to Dublin for a six-day training camp. The Red Devils play Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

United begin their Premier League season against Hull City on August 22 as Michael Carrick prepares for his first full season in charge following a stellar spell in the dugout as an interim, with his results ultimately landing him the job permanently. Sports.content:
Man Utd in 'advanced talks' with European giants over Joshua Zirkzee exit

Joshua Zirkzee started just one of Michael Carrick's 17 games in charge last season and the Manchester United star looks to be on his way out of Old Trafford, with Juventus keen to sign him

View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee wants to leave Manchester United (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Manchester United are in advanced talks with Juventus, who are negotiating a deal to sign Joshua Zirkzee on loan with a £30million option to buy. Zirkzee, 25, finds himself out of favour at Old Trafford, with Michael Carrick's appointment last season failing to change his fortunes.

Having started just one of the 17 games Carrick was in charge for, the striker missed out on making the Netherlands' 26-man squad for the World Cup. Zirkzee only scored two goals last season, his most recent coming in December against soon-to-be relegated Wolves.

‌



After Juventus' move for Paris Saint-Germain forward Randal Kolo Muani collapsed, their focus is on Zirkzee. The Sun report that Juve are leading the race to sign him, with fellow Italian giants Roma also interested.

‌



It's understood that Zirkzee is keen on a return to Serie A. The former Bayern Munich star scored 14 goals and provided eight assists in 58 games for Bologna which convinced United to shell out £36.5m to sign him in 2024.

Joshua Zirkzee could be set for a loan move away from Manchester United this summer having struggled to convince at Old Trafford

Juventus are holding advanced talks with Manchester United over a loan deal for Joshua Zirkzee. The move would also include a £30million option to buy for the Italian outfit.

‌



The striker has been strongly linked with an Old Trafford departure this summer, but is keen to secure a place in Michael Carrick's plans. The Dutchman has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter during his time in with the Red Devils - unable to break into Ruben Amorim's plans or Carrick's since joining the club under Erik ten Hag in 2024.

‌



The 25-year-old has netted just five goals in 56 Premier League outings for United. The Red Devils are said to be receptive to Zirkzee's departure this summer, though the former Bayern Munich prospect is understood to be happy to stay.

‌



Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

It is suggested that he feels European football at United in 2026/27 will provide him with greater chances under Carrick. The Netherlands international sought to leave in January but was informed by United that it would not be feasible.

Nevertheless, The Sun now suggest a transfer could be possible with Serie A club Juve in advanced negotiations. The Turin side appeared poised to capture France international Kolo Muani from Paris Saint-Germain following his underwhelming loan stint with Tottenham Hotspur last season.

However, Juventus have reportedly failed to reach an agreement on a fee with PSG after talks broke down. It is understood that the Italian club have swiftly turned their attention to Zirkzee as they seek a new frontman.

‌



Juventus are said to be the most serious suitors for Zirkzee, though Roma have also harboured a long-standing interest in the striker. Luciano Spalletti's outfit are reportedly the frontrunners for his signature, having moved considerably quicker in negotiations.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest

Arsenal are keen on landing Vinicius Jr and the Brazilian will remain away from Real Madrid as his representatives continue to negotiate with the Spanish side - who want him to lower his demands

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr's future at Madrid remains unclear (Image: Getty)

Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr will not return to training this week as his contract talks rumble on with Arsenal waiting in the wings.

‌



The Brazilian has been given an extended break having played at the World Cup, but will not return before the month is out despite there being an expectation that he would be back in the Spanish capital for pre-season.

‌



Vinicius is staying away while his representatives try to make progress in talks over an extension to his contract, which will run out at the end of the upcoming season. Real do not want to let him leave for free, and there is a scenario whereby they will cash in.

‌



Arsenal are waiting to see how the saga plays out and the major issue with Los Blancos and their player stems from his wage demands. Vinicius wants financial parity with top earner Kylian Mbappe, but the La Liga giants want him to lower that request, reports the Daily Mail.

If he fails to do that then the door opens for the Gunners, who have internally discussed signing the 26-year-old but no bid has yet been tabled.

Vinicius Junior's next club odds as Real Madrid star linked with move to Arsenal READ MORE :

Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update READ MORE :

Jose Mourinho is back in charge at Real following his initial stint from 2010 and 2013 and had a public spat last season involving Vinicius. The Special One has wasted no time in bolstering his squad, adding the likes of Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konate and Marc Cucurella.

‌



Real are now closing in on the £115million signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, one of the most in-demand wingers of the summer. PSG had looked like his most likely destination but they refused to match his financial demands and the Spanish giants are ready to break their own transfer record to land the Ivorian.

Diomande, who scored 12 goals and registered eight assists last term, would serve as a replacement for Vinicius if he does make a move to the Bernabeu.

Arsenal want a left-sided attacker and have just missed out on Morgan Rogers, who chose to move to Chelsea. BBC Sport claims that the Brazilian is viewed internally as the club's number one target and any move would almost certainly be a club-record deal.
