The former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are now being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: Spurs’ plans for new training facility in London park blocked by high court
Sports.content:
A council’s decision to allow Tottenham Hotspur Football Club to build a new training facility in a park in north London has been quashed by a judge at the high court.

The campaign group Guardians of Whitewebbs told a hearing in June that Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for a new women’s and girls’ football academy on 6.5 hectares (16 acres) of land in Whitewebbs Park was unlawful.

The group’s lawyers told the hearing in London that the council breached the rules when making its decision, as councillors were not provided with all relevant information regarding the development’s environmental impact, meaning they were “materially misled”.

Campaigners also claimed there was a “real possibility of bias” in the decision as Spurs had “unparalleled access” to senior council figures at the time of the application.

Enfield council, which was Labour-controlled at the time but is now run by a Conservative minority administration, withdrew its defence to the claim last month.

But Spurs continued to oppose the challenge, claiming it should be dismissed as the result “would inevitably have been the same” had the information been provided.

The club also said the allegations of bias were “completely overblown”.

In a ruling on Monday, Sir Tim Kerr, sitting as a high court judge, quashed the decision to approve the plans, finding the result “could well have been different” had all the relevant information about the scheme been available.

He dismissed claims concerning potential bias, describing the group’s arguments as “weak” and stating that “cordial relations” between the council and the club were “normal given the overlapping functions and interests”.

Spurs agreed a 25-year lease for the site in 2023 – a decision that was unsuccessfully challenged at the high court in 2024 – and the council resolved to approve the planning application in February last year.

The plans would have seen the construction of 10 football pitches and other work on the park, which is near the club’s men’s training facilities.

Jenny Wigley KC, representing Guardians of Whitewebbs, said in written submissions that the ecologist Giles Sutton had carried out a report into the environmental benefits of the plans in November 2024.

Sutton told the council that while he did not oppose the scheme “as such”, it was “counterintuitive” to accept the club’s claims that the site would benefit the local environment as about 40% of the park would be lost.

“In my opinion, if the council were to accept this, their decision could be easily challenged,” he added.

But Wigley said council officers had said in a planning report for councillors that there was “no objection to the proposed development”, despite Sutton telling the authority that this did not reflect his advice.

She continued that Sutton’s report “clearly informed the planning officers’ views” on the environmental impact of the scheme and should have been presented as a “background document”, meaning members of the public could have inspected it.

Wigley said: “[The law] does not permit this kind of salami slicing, where a planning officer can disclose parts of a report they agree with but can avoid public scrutiny of the parts of the report they do not agree with.”

James Maurici KC, representing Spurs, said Sutton’s views were “no more than an assertion” and that Guardians of Whitewebbs had “failed to provide any evidence” that it had been prejudiced by the council’s failure to provide the document.

He continued: “It is highly likely, indeed inevitable, given the absence of any evidence of prejudice, that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred.”

But Kerr said the council’s noncompliance with rules was “serious” and that councillors were “materially misled” by the exclusion of Sutton’s report.

Alessandro Georgiou, the Conservative leader of Enfield council since May 2026, said the authority was delighted with the decision and that it withdrew its defence as it would “not have been in the best interests of residents across the borough”.

He added: “We said we would protect Whitewebbs Park from this unacceptable proposal and we will now move forward with plans that reflect the needs of the local community and also preserve and protect this important area of Enfield.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Vinícius to Arsenal? Club football’s military industrial complex kicks back into gear
Sports.content:
VENI, VINÍ, VICI?

If this is an attention economy, there is no greater attention-seeker than club football. Not content with dominating the sporting agenda for 11 months of any calendar year, it has been a summer of “look at me”, largely in vain as the Geopolitics World Cup’s often grubby charms snaffled up football focus. Often faint, sometimes shrill, the keening sound of season 2026-27 approaching, of this meaning more, was never far away as clubs congratulated or commiserated their players out in North America in grasping for relevance. And with the GWC safely bagged up, the club football military industrial complex is kicking back into gear, via the usual fashion, a transfer saga, and as is customary, one that involves Real Madrid.

The central protagonist this time of a patchwork of preparing bids, coming days, exploring moves and eventual here-we-going is Vinícius Júnior. The eternal Brazilian Ballon d’Or hopeful – and refusenik – has been linked with, gasp, Arsenal. As myriad examples in recent history prove, Liverpool’s summer of 2025 as the most obvious, winning the transfer market means little in the actual, material world. Though in the summer months, there is no levy placed on the wild fantasy scenarios being played out in the minds of Gunners fans. Arsenal plus Viní equals limitless glory, orgiastic scenes of the great man thwacking corners for Gabriel and William Saliba to convert. Leandro Trossard, farewell, the new king is in town. Though what about Christos Tzolis, the Greek flier signed just last week as replacement for the departed Belgian?

Those who profess to know about this stuff – and often get things right – suggest there are legs in this. There are, though, flags on the play. Real Madrid and Florentino Pérez, recently re-elected Madrileño overlord – have form for using monied Premier League clubs as pawns. Viní has been in contract negotiations, his current deal expiring a year hence. He is reported to earn £400,000 per week, and is hardly likely to want less. Madrid do not wish him to depart for free. And this is Arsenal, whose owners have spent big in recent years, though have sometimes baulked at top dollar. Last year, they opted for Viktor Gyökeres rather than enter the Alexander Isak affair, a move that worked out well enough and Viní’s is a very different stratosphere to such dealing.

Attached to all that flimflam is Yan Diomande, the Ivorian winger, one of those players who’s become a household name despite very few of us having the time to watch RB Leipzig. Everybody wants him, it seems, but Madrid are now said to have beaten PSG to his signature, which then opens up questions of Bradley Barcola’s potential, probably very expensive, move to Liverpool. Thus, Football Daily finds itself pulled into the miasma, that aching sense of what might be, of who will go where, what it will all look like. Just when we thought we were out, they pulled us back in.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all. To those behind their pens and papers, behind ⁠their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are ​on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness” – Fifa big cheese Gianni Infantino posts an open letter on his social media disgraces, urging detractors to “take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray” after a GWC marked by controversies including US visa restrictions affecting supporters and officials from several countries, concerns involving teams from conflict-hit regions, soaring ticket prices for fans … and the suspension of an automatic one-match ban imposed on USA USA USA striker Folarin Balogun after US president Donald Trump called Infantino directly.

View image in fullscreen Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

double quotation mark The passing of Kevin Keegan brought back memories of Hull City when Paul O’Riley, a young pro, went to Firewall FC on loan for six weeks. After his loan finished he came back raving about this kid who was so dedicated. He wanted to win all the long runs, sprints and would come back in the afternoon to run up and down the terraces with weights in his hands. Being from Donny I already knew about Kevin Keegan (also a Donny lad). Vince Grimes, a fellow pro at Hull, was always banging on about Terry Heath and a young kid called Kevin Keegan. Vince kept telling the coaching staff at Hull about Keegan and that they should buy him. Their response was they’d been to watch him play several times and didn’t fancy him. Not long after all this Keegan went to Liverpool and the rest is history. Many years later when he was managing Newcastle, I wrote to him asking if he’d allow from a lad from Australia to have a spell at Newcastle. He wrote back and said he’d be welcome. Not only that, they picked the lad up from the airport, sorted out his digs, took him to Wembley on the first-team bus for the Charity Shield game and Alan Shearer gave the lad his match boots” – Micky Dale.

double quotation mark ‘People talk about it being impossible. That means nothing. I truly believe that we can do something special” – Jermain Defoe, 6 April … ‘Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking FC. Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position’ – Jermain Defoe, 24 July. Apparently ‘impossible’ does mean something after all” – Phil C0ckburn.

View image in fullscreen Jermain Defoe at his Woking unveiling, recently. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Micky Dale. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Arsenal and Liverpool battle it out for Bradley Barcola?
Sports.content:
Like baggy trousers, small sunglasses and leopard print, transfer rumours are back in a big way. And there can be no doubting the transfer ambition of the Premier League champions, Arsenal, who are eyeing up either Vinícius Júnior or Bradley Barcola as a deluxe Leandro Trossard replacement.

One sticking point for the Gunners is the former’s apparent desire to stay put at Real Madrid, while Liverpool appear to be favourites for Barcola if they can muster the £145m Paris Saint-Germain are demanding for their fourth-best forward. The path may become clear for Vinícius to leave the Bernabéu, however, with the club closing in on a deal for the Ivorian World Cup sensation Yan Diomande. Perennial prospect Endrick has also been touted for a move away from Madrid this summer.

Staying with wingers, Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye is coveted by the Saudi Pro League’s Al-Hilal, while a potential fight for the signature of Pedro Neto could be upon us, with a few Saudi clubs in the mix with Liverpool and Manchester City. Why on earth Chelsea would want to sell such a talent is a good question, but balancing the books at Stamford Bridge is imperative after the £117m splurge on Morgan Rogers. Forgotten City wide man Savinho could be heading to Tottenham to make room for any new arrival at the Etihad.

Manchester United are staying out of the scramble for wide guys and instead concentrating their efforts on centre-forwards. If Joshua Zirzkee leaves this summer – with Juventus targeting the Dutchman – Ollie Watkins, 31 before the year is out, a possible replacement. United could ship out their young left-back Harry Amass to Coventry, either permanently or on loan, which has got some fans very excited about the possible arrival of Lewis Hall.

João Palhinha’s future has been the subject of some speculation. Bayern Munich’s sporting director, Christoph Freund, has made no bones about trimming their squad, paving the way for the Portuguese to join Aston Villa, but the midfielder would prefer to stay put. Mind you, he previously said he wanted to extend his loan stay at Spurs. Marco Silva – a former manager of the midfielder at Fulham – wants him at Benfica on loan.

Remember Mohamed Salah? Well the Egyptian King is still without a club after leaving Liverpool and enjoying some holiday after the World Cup. His next stop could well be Besiktas, with a stunning Darwin Núñez reunion on the cards if the Uruguayan also joins the Turkish club from Al-Hilal. Plenty of Saudi clubs are still on the Salah case and even Sporting Kansas from MLS have been linked.

Sports.title: ‘Great bitterness’ – Andrea Pirlo being denied Italy job sparks shock double resignation
Sports.content:
Paolo Maldini has quit as technical director of the Italian Football Federation after Andrea Pirlo was not appointed head coach.

The federation's president, Giovanni Malago, opted not to appoint Pirlo due to his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.

5 Maldini and Leonardo have left their jobs just 16 days after being appointed due to the Pirlo drama Credit: Getty

5 Pirlo had been removed from the running for the Italy job due to commercial ties with Russia Credit: Fonbet

Pirlo had emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Gennaro Gattuso after former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola turned down the post.

The AC Milan icon, who was part of the last Azzurri side to lift the World Cup as a player in 2006, had strong support from the newly-appointed Maldini and his adviser Leonardo.

But the fallout from Pirlo's role as a global ambassador for Russia's largest bookmaker, Fonbet, led to political resistance.

And, according to Sky Italy, the decision not to name the Italy legend as boss has led to Maldini and Leonardo stepping down.

Maldini was only given the role as technical director 16 days ago.

Pirlo will not be Italy's new head coach

“Out of respect for the institutions, the federation and everybody involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now,” Pirlo wrote in a statement, confirming he won't be Italy boss on Instagram.

“However, after learning last night that I am no longer a candidate for the Italy national team head coach position, I feel it is necessary to clarify a few points.

“Over the past few days, I have watched with great bitterness as the debate regarding my name and the possibility of my taking on the role of Italy national team head coach unfolded.

“Throughout my career, first as a player and then as a coach, I have always performed my duties with full respect of the laws of the countries I have worked in and the contracts I signed.

“The professional collaboration that is the subject of recent controversy came about as part of my working experience in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature. Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing convictions to me that I have never expressed and that I do not hold.

5 Former Italy captain Pirlo made over 100 appearances for his country Credit: AFP

“I wish to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the respect and faith that they showed in me. I know their competence, their seriousness, and the love that they have always dedicated to Italian football.

“However, it is regrettable that a decision based on sporting grounds was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing motives and intentions to my name that never existed.

"My love for Italy does not depend on a job. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.”

Why did Guardiola reject Italy?

Guardiola was the first-choice candidate to succeed Gattuso, who left his post in March after Italy failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup.

Italian football expert Daniele Fisichella explained on the latest talkSPORT episode of Danny Kelly's Trans Euro Express podcast: “The name of Guardiola has been invented, has been named since May.

“Basically, the Italian FA, with the newly appointed Paolo Maldini, the former player, as a managing director, and Leonardo [Araujo], the Brazilian, as an adviser, they tried to get the best manager available on the market, which is Pep Guardiola, they met in Barcelona last Saturday, hours before the World Cup final, to explain the proposal and the idea of him managing not only the first team, but also be in charge of the restructuring of the Italian football.

5 Pep Guardiola bid farewell to Manchester City in May after a decade at the club Credit: Getty

“Of course, a fascinating proposal, albeit for the fact that there is quite a lot of work to do in the Italian FA and in the Italian national team.

“Guardiola was honoured; he said, but very politely replied, thanks, but no thanks, for different reasons.

“Also because he wants to take a step down for a bit from football, for personal reasons, for family reasons,” Fisichella continued.

“So even the idea of living in Barcelona and almost working remotely and then going to Italy to manage the team every three or four months didn't quite appeal to him.”

Who did Italy try to hire next?

Fisichella continued: “So then the Italian FA tried to convince Carlo Ancelotti, via Paolo Maldini, of course, his former teammate and former player at AC Milan. But Carlo Ancelotti had already committed to stay at Brazil.

“So the first choice, really the only viable choice, remained Andrea Pirlo, who, by the way, is a great friend of Paolo Maldini, having played together at AC Milan.

5 Pirlo was named a global brand ambassador for Fonbet in October 2025 Credit: Getty

“And Paolo Maldini has always been a big sponsor of Andrea Pirlo. Why? Because Andrea Pirlo is considered almost somebody who has also got this aura.

“He was a fantastic player, but he's considered somebody who is destined to be a great manager.

“Unfortunately, his CV and his career doesn't quite tell the same story. His first ever coaching experience was at Juventus in 2021, and he didn't do really well there. They finished second; they won the cup.

“But that team never really convinced and was never able to impose themselves, despite still having Cristiano Ronaldo in very good form as well.

“Then he went to manage Sampdoria in the second division, got sacked after a year and a half, then went to Turkey and managed to finish fourth with a team outside of the top three anyway.

“And last year was managing in Dubai's second division, which, by the way, he won the championship there. So at least he got United FC promoted to the first division.”

Pirlo's ties to Russian betting company

Regardless of his less-than-glittering managerial CV, Pirlo looked set to become 'the new Italian manager on a very cheap contract'.

“Only 1.5 million euros [£1.2m], compared, for example, to [Jurgen] Klopp, who earns 7-8m at Germany,” Fisichella added on talkSPORT on Sunday evening. “So he's obviously much, much cheaper.

“However, it has emerged that Pirlo earlier this year in May flew to Russia to participate in a testimonial game and to do some sponsorship for a betting company, which, of course, has been frowned upon.

“Now, a big crisis has started in the last few hours.

“Even politicians got involved in Italy, saying that whoever represents Russia or helps Russia should never, never be appointed into public office. So you can imagine the things have unravelled.

“And Paolo Maldini, who's been in the job less than three weeks, might resign if Pirlo, his friend, is not appointed. I mean, there's never a boring moment in Italian football. Let's face it.”

Fisichella ended up being correct in his statement too, as Maldini has now gone on to step down from his position.

Sports.title: Chelsea lead race in shock move to sign Jordan Henderson on free transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea lead race in shock move to sign Jordan Henderson on free transfer

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign England international Jordan Henderson, talkSPORT understands.

Brentford have given permission for the 36-year-old to leave on a free transfer this summer.



6 Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Henderson from Brentford on a free transfer Credit: Getty

Henderson is keen on a move to Stamford Bridge ahead of the new Premier League season.

Xabi Alonso's side currently lead the race to sign the veteran midfielder.

Having signed for the Bees on a two-year deal last summer, Henderson has less than 12 months remaining on his current deal.



The Liverpool legend, who boasts a Premier League winners' medal to his name made 32 league appearances last season, scoring once and adding three assists.

Blues target

He was also part of England's squad at this summer's World Cup in North America.



However, Henderson made just one appearance for the Three Lions, with his tournament ending early after surgery on a broken radius.

The injury, which he suffered celebrating England's last 16 win over Mexico, ruled Henderson out of the final three fixtures.



He was still able to collect a bronze medal following the third-place play-off win over France, though.

Henderson's move to Brentford in July 2025 followed spells with Ajax and Al Ettifaq since his Liverpool exit three years ago.

During his time at Anfield, he won eight major trophies including the Champions League, Premier League and Club World Cup.

6 Brentford are willing to allow Henderson to leave for free this summer Credit: Getty



6

Across spells with Liverpool, Sunderland and Brentford, Henderson has made a total of 463 Premier League appearances.

Meanwhile, he has scored 34 goals and provided 56 assists in those outings.

Chelsea transfer plans

Alonso's interest in Henderson comes as Chelsea weigh up a move for Brighton striker Danny Welbeck.



Talks are at an early stage between the two clubs regarding the veteran forward, talkSPORT understands.

Welbeck's Seagulls contract is currently set to expire at the end of June 2027.

Brighton would not stand in his way of an exit if a fee can be agreed.

6 Chelsea are also considering a surprise move for Brighton striker Welbeck Credit: Getty



Since joining the club in October 2020, Welbeck has scored 51 goals in 201 appearances across all competitions.

Last term saw the 35-year-old produce a career-high Premier League goal tally for the second year in a row after finding the net 13 times.

talkSPORT verdict

Ade Oladipo and Rory Jennings both reacted to the news of Chelsea's interest in Henderson on Drive.

Jennings had earlier claimed that Chelsea need an experienced title winner like Welbeck in the dressing room.



When Oladipo put those comments back to him, he replied: "I don't think we need a dressing room full of it."

The talkSPORT co-host continued: "I don't think you need to sign the England team of 2018. I don't think that's what we need to do.

6 Jennings doubts whether Henderson is the 'right answer' for Chelsea Credit: Getty

"I think what we need to do is bring in some standards for sure. I don't think Jordan Henderson is the right answer.



"I quite like Henderson. I don't necessarily rate him, but I quite like him.

"I think what he did for Liverpool was an integral part of their success. He was an integral part of everything that Jurgen Klopp built."

Jennings then added: "We've had a transfer strategy over the past four years where we've bought nothing but young, unproven footballers. Something needs to change. You need to equalise it.

"So I do understand what Xabi Alonso's problem is. I do understand why he's thinking about a way of resolving this. I would argue that Jordan Henderson isn't quite the answer.



"You know when it was Granit Xhaka? That made more sense to me. Granit Xhaka is still a good player, still a player that can do a job.

6 Chelsea have already completed the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers this summer Credit: Getty

"I'm not convinced that Jordan Henderson is the answer. I'm not convinced that he's ready to play at this level. The fact that we're linked with him is minorly troubling."

Chelsea were linked with a move for Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka earlier this summer, but have been issued with a firm hands-off warning.



Meanwhile, Alonso has already added to his squad with the British-record £117million addition of Morgan Rogers.

The England forward has joined the club from Aston Villa on a seven-year deal.

Sports.title: EFL set to demand change to landmark £1.5bn deal after Premier League clubs vote
Sports.content:
The Football League could be set to push back on a proposed ten-year deal with the Premier League worth £1.5billion.

That is according to football finance expert Kieran Maguire ahead of this week's vote.

3 Premier League clubs will vote this week on a proposed 10-year EFL deal worth £1.5billion Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Top-flight clubs will vote on the proposed 'New Deal' on Thursday, according to Sky News.

At least 14 of the 20 Premier League clubs must vote in favour of the plans before the proposals can be put to the EFL.

If approved, an initial annual payment of £100million would be made to EFL clubs before rising to more than £130million in year two.

That figure would then increase to £160million for the third year and remain at that amount for the remaining seven years of the agreement.

A lifeboat fund worth £20million will also be introduced to assist any EFL club which falls into administration.

However, clubs must spend 20 per cent of the money they receive through the 'New Deal' on infrastructure, as part of the proposal.

There are hopes that a binding agreement can be reached within weeks if the proposal is approved on Thursday.

How will the payments be funded?

There are currently two sources being proposed to help fund the £1.5billion deal.

The first would see the Premier League's levy on domestic transfers raised from four per cent to six per cent.

Meanwhile, there is also a proposal to gradually reduce the three-year parachute payments received by relegated clubs.

3 The EFL is currently opposed to the proposed funding agreement, says football finance expert Maguire Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Explaining how the deal would be funded, Maguire told talkSPORT on Monday: "It looks as if it’s going to be funded through a couple of sources.

"First of all, the levy, which arises on domestic transfers. That’s going to go up from four per cent to six per cent.

"So if you’re signing a £100million player, that’s an extra £2million which goes into the pot.

"Secondly, it looks as if parachute payments are going to be scaled down. I think that will please the EFL because ideally they’d like them abolished, but I think they acknowledge that they do serve a useful purpose."

EFL stance

Maguire continued: "So you put those sums together, plus the fact that the Premier League is very successful, I think it’s going to go through the £7billion barrier for the first time in season 2025/26.

"So all of that is more money coming into the game. The regulator doesn’t want to get involved, but this is an opportunity for the Premier League to show that it can negotiate with the EFL.

3 Reduced parachute payments and an increase to the Premier League's transfer levy are set to fund the plans Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"But first of all, it has to go for a vote of Premier League clubs and then we’ve got to see what the response of the EFL is."

Even if the Premier League clubs vote in favour of the proposed deal, the EFL could still push back on the terms put to them.

Maguire admits this could likely be the case based on the current composition of the proposal.

He added: "Certainly the noises coming out of the EFL aren’t that positive, but it certainly does look a step forward.

"Even though it might need further negotiating and sort of tapering off at some point."

Sports.title: Heartwarming reason why Leeds starlet Ollie Pickles wore No.66 shirt against Wrexham
Sports.content:
Leeds United's Oliver Pickles had a day to remember as he made his first appearance for the senior team on Sunday.

And the shirt number he was given has made it even more memorable, as it has a heartwarming reason behind it.

3 Pickles played for Leeds against Wrexham with the No.66 on his back Credit: Getty

It's not certain whether the teenager was given the No.66 with this reason in mind, or whether it is completely coincidental.

But Pickles having the 66 on his back relates to a great story, as images of his name and number spread around social media.

Perfect pick for Pickles

Leeds have handed their academy star a number that combines brilliantly with his surname and an iconic England moment.

In 1966, before the World Cup, the Jules Rimet trophy was stolen from Westminster's Central Hall and couldn't be found.

That left the FA in a panic, as there were just four months left until their home tournament was set to get started.

Police then investigated how the trophy was taken, with the FA having to get a replica made at the time.

Soon after, a ransom note demanding £15,000 was received with then FA chairman Joe Mears pretending to agree to it.

That false agreement led to the arrest of the suspected culprit, but the Jules Rimet trophy was still missing...

Now, here comes the connection to Leeds' youngster Pickles.

A dog named Pickles would remarkably end up finding the trophy whilst sniffing around outside a flat in south London.

3 The World Cup trophy would have been lost before the World Cup in 1966 if it wasn't for Pickles the dog Credit: Getty

His owner, Dave Corbett, told BBC Sport in 2016: "Pickles was running around over by my neighbour's car. As I was putting the lead on, I noticed this package laying there, wrapped just in newspaper but very tightly bound with string.

"I tore a bit off the bottom and there was a blank shield, then there were the words Brazil, West Germany and Uruguay printed.

"I tore off the other end and it was a lady holding a very shallow dish above her head. I'd seen the pictures of the World Cup in the papers and on TV so my heart started thumping."

After Pickles' discovery, the Jules Rimet trophy was taken to a police station and returned, with the dog being given a medal by the National Canine Defence League alongside other awards.

Of course, England would then go on to win the World Cup and Bobby Moore would lift the title to create an iconic picture.

Pickles' heroics in '66 have become a legendary story, with Leeds' Pickles donning the No.66 seemingly reigniting some memories.

3 Pickles' number has led to a re-telling of an iconic 1966 World Cup story Credit: Getty

Pickles' Leeds career so far

Pickles will hope to be seen a lot more in his No.66 shirt this season, having signed his first professional deal last year.

He played 14 minutes in a 3-2 friendly defeat against Wrexham on Saturday in his maiden first-team appearance.

For the Leeds academy, the 18-year-old midfielder has played almost 100 games, including 43 for the under-21 set-up.

He's scored four times and provided two assists for the U21s, also playing 50 times for the U18s beforehand.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso details Chelsea ‘plan’ to start record signing Morgan Rogers alongside Cole Palmer
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is confident Cole Palmer and new signing Morgan Rogers will have plenty of on-pitch chemistry in the Chelsea starting XI.

Rogers joined the Blues from Aston Villa in a British record £117million move last week as the statement signing of the summer thus far.

3 Palmer and Rogers are club teammates once again, this time at Chelsea Credit: Getty Images - Getty

The 24-year-old has reunited with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer, with the pair being close friends off the pitch.

Both players have similar profiles - attacking midfielders who possess top-level technical ability and a keen eye for goal.

They look set to form part of a new-look Chelsea attack under Alonso, who is ready to deploy them together in the new season.

When asked during a pre-season press conference if he has a strategy for the duo, the Blues boss said: "Yes, I have a plan, I have an idea.

"I can see them linking really well. We need to have a good mix, good stability, players that can play with more freedom.

"If we get that balance right, and we get those special players in the right positions with good control, I think that we will be more competitive."

Chelsea have 'good feeling' with Rogers

Arsenal appeared to be the likely destination for Rogers ahead of the defence of their Premier League title.

However, Chelsea managed to complete a deal within 48 hours, with co-owner Behdad Eghbali having a significant role in the pitch to the player.

Rogers will wear the no. 17 shirt at Stamford Bridge, and is an arrival that has inspired optimism within the Chelsea squad.

"It's a great signing," Alonso said. "I think, in that position, we needed an important player, and I'm sure that there were not many more better options than Morgan.

3 Alonso has revealed that he can envisage a strong partnership between the pair Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"So, we are delighted. It means a lot for everyone, and for the players that are already here as well.

"They have a good feeling and are looking forward to having him in a few weeks."

Having reached the World Cup semi-finals with England, Rogers is not part of the Chelsea squad for their pre-season tour.

They are up against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday for their first friendly, with kick-off at 10:45am UK time.

All change at the Bridge

There was little to no chance of Chelsea having a quiet summer after finishing tenth in the Premier League last season.

Alongside Rogers, Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda have all completed moves to west London.

3 Rogers has joined Chelsea as their club-record signing Credit: Getty

Maxence Lacroix looks set to be their fifth signing, and his £55m switch from Crystal Palace will take Chelsea's spending north of £280m.

Meanwhile, talkSPORT brought you the news of their shock interest in Brighton striker Danny Welbeck earlier on Monday.

Talks are in the early stages, and it's understood that Brighton will not stand in the 35-year-old's way if a fair fee is agreed.

Chelsea are also battling against Arsenal and Italian clubs to sign John Stones following his exit from Man City.

Off the pitch, Austin MacPhee is on the brink of joining from Villa as a set piece coach.

His arrival into Alonso's coaching team comes after Bernardo Cueva switched from set piece coach to technical analyst at Chelsea.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Chelsea in battle with two Italian giants in race to sign John Stones
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Chelsea in battle with two Italian giants in race to sign John Stones

Inter Milan and Juventus are both in talks with John Stones' camp over signing the free agent, talkSPORT understands.

The England international is currently without a club having left Manchester City following the expiry of his contract in June.



4 Stones has boosted his future prospects after an impressive World Cup Credit: Getty

In demand

Arsenal and Chelsea have been linked with Stones, with both clubs considering a move for him.

Liverpool have also been urged to make an approach for the 32-year-old, but his Premier League suitors could now have a battle on their hands.

Serie A giants Juventus and Inter Milan have now joined the race for his signature, with negotiations set to take place this week.



Stones is understood to be open to a move to Italy, with the centre-back not short of options ahead of the new season.

Should he decide his future lies on the continent, the Englishman will then face a choice between being part of Juventus' revival, or joining Inter as they look to build on their recent glory.



Inter clinched the Serie A title for the second time in three years last term, once again qualifying for the Champions League.

They have been looking to strengthen their back line, having already held talks with with Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.



Meanwhile, Juventus endured a disappointing 2025/26 campaign, finishing sixth in the table and missing out on Champions League qualification.

And both Italian sides may have been handed a boost in their pursuit of Stones, with Chelsea closing in on the signing of Maxence Lacroix.

But they may face stiffer competition from Arsenal, who could need a new centre-back to fill in for William Saliba, who looks set for a lengthy absence after suffering a back injury while on World Cup duty with France.

4 Stones bid an emotional farewell to Manchester City after playing a reduced role in his final season at the Etihad Credit: Getty



4 Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti is looking to tempt Stones to Italy

Recent revival

Stones has a decision to make over his future in the coming weeks, having put himself in the shop window at the World Cup.

He made five appearances for England on their run to the semi-finals, as the Three Lions ultimately went on to finish third.

The defender left Man City in June, following ten years with the club having signed from Everton in 2016.



During that time, he won 19 trophies including six Premier League titles, the Champions League and the Club World Cup.

However, he played a bit-part role in his final season at the Etihad Stadium, featuring just nine times in the Premier League.

Only five of these were starts, as the Citizens finished second to Arsenal in the title race.

4 Stones won six Premier League titles during 10 years at City before leaving at the end of June Credit: Getty



Stones' league outings contributed to a total of 18 appearances across all competitions, with injuries reducing his involvement.

As well as Arsenal and Chelsea being among his Premier League suitors, Liverpool have been backed to make a play for the experienced defender.

Reds fan and Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony made this claim recently on talkSPORT, insisting Stones would be the perfect partner to Virgil van Dijk.

MacAnthony said: "I’d love Liverpool to sign him.

"We have two centre-backs, young ones, paid a lot of money for one (Jeremy Jacquet) and a lot of money for the other one (Giovanni Leoni), who did his ACL last year.



"We obviously we have (Virgil) Van Dijk and obviously then Joe Gomez has got injury-proneness to his resume. I would love Stones with Van Dijk, just to bed in those two younger players who were coming back from injury."

Sports.title: Where to watch Liverpool v Wrexham plus UK kick-off time, squads and location
Sports.content:
Where to watch Liverpool v Wrexham plus UK kick-off time, squads and location

Liverpool continue their American tour against Wrexham this week as they look to build on a winning start under Andoni Iraola.

The Reds defeated Premier League rivals Sunderland 4-2 in Nashville, Tennessee on Saturday despite missing several key players.

3 Jacquet is not being rushed into the matchday squad due to the risk of injury Credit: Getty

Wrexham also got off to a fying start Stateside, edging Leeds United 3-2 in their pre-season tie, after defeating Manchester United in Helsinki.

The Championship side will aim to beat a third top-flight opponent of the summer as they look to build momentum ahead of another promotion push.

Where to watch Liverpool vs Wrexham

The fixture will be played on Thursday, July 30.

It is scheduled to kick off at 12:30am BST (7:30pm local time).

It will take place at the Yankee Stadium in New York - home Major League Baseball side, the New York Yankees.

It will be available to watch on All Red Video, Liverpool's dedicated streaming service.

All Red Video costs £42.99-a-season while you can also claim a 14-day free trial before paying £4.99-a-month.

All Liverpool's pre-season games can be viewed via All Red Video on their official website.

3 Iraola has a completely different project at Liverpool than he did at Bournemouth Credit: Getty

Liverpool vs Wrexham: Squads

Injury-prone Joe Gomez lasted only ten minutes before being forced off against Sunderland, as Iraola called it 'the worst news' of the day.

It was reminder to the Reds that they may need to call in reinforcements and cannot rely on Gomez to stay fit for an extended period of time.

Liverpool

Sports.title: Neymar furiously debunks ‘lies’ over alleged dressing room clash on Santos return
Sports.content:
Neymar has slammed reports that he was involved in an outburst towards two of his young Santos teammates.

The Brazilian legend is claimed to have clashed with some of the squad during his side's 2-2 draw with Chapecoense.



2 Neymar was allegedly involved in a dressing room clash during Santos' latest match Credit: Getty

He featured in his first game back with Santos following the World Cup, playing all 90 minutes and scoring twice on Saturday.

But a day later, local outlet Globe Esporte reported that Neymar had raged at two teammates during the game.

The 34-year-old was alleged to have called 21-year-old star Gabriel Bontempo an 'idiot' and criticised 19-year-old centre-back Joao Ananias in the dressing room rant.



It was also claimed that the behind-the-scenes clash led to anger from Santos' players, coaching staff and board members.

However, Neymar felt he had to respond to the rumours, speaking on social media to debunk the 'lies' being told.



Neymar hits back

Speaking on his Instagram story, he began: "What's up, everyone? Hope you're all having a good Sunday.

"I see some rumours going around about me rebuking the younger players in the dressing room.



"This is not true at all. I ask whoever spread these words not to do so, don't lie. You can ask anyone in the dressing room, it was a rebuke of the team.

"I spoke, and Lucas [Verissimo] spoke, and [Willian] Arão, and Gabi [Barbosa], and [Gabriel] Brazão... everyone, and of course there were rebukes, because we are competitors who want to win.

"But nobody was picking on the young players. I'm not going to tolerate people saying that."

2 Neymar hit back at the reports of his rant following the game where he scored twice Credit: Getty



Neymar then added: "Moving forward, I'm not going to accept these lies you're spreading on the internet.

"Holding each other accountable in the dressing room is completely normal in football. It’s what teams that want to win do.

"The people writing these malicious, fake articles know nothing. You don't know what football is, and you've never been part of a real squad."

Another Santos controversy

This isn't the first time that Neymar has been alleged to have been involved in a bust-up whilst back at Santos.



He returned to his first club in 2025, 12 years after leaving as a youngster, but he's been involved in some drama this year.

On top of the latest claims, in May, Neymar was said to have been involved in a training ground clash with another teammate.

The iconic forward was reported to have slapped Robinho Jr, who is the son of the ex-Manchester City and Real Madrid forward.

The pair allegedly squared up and engaged in a pushing and shoving match, with Neymar then slapping Robinho Jr.



Neymar is said to have apologised following the incident.

Sports.title: Italian football in CHAOS as Paolo Maldini and Leonardo QUIT after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from becoming new national team coach amid links to Russian betting firm spark
Sports.content:
Italian football in CHAOS as Paolo Maldini and Leonardo QUIT after Andrea Pirlo was blocked from becoming new national team coach amid links to Russian betting firm spark

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Italian football has been rocked by the news that Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have quit in the wake of Andrea Pirlo being ruled out of the running as next national team boss.

Pirlo is no longer in the frame to become Italy's next manager after 'political' concerns were raised over the football legend's sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company.

Pirlo, 47, was backed by former team-mate and new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) technical director Maldini to land the role after legendary ex-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly declined the opportunity.

The former AC Milan and Juventus star was on the brink of agreeing a deal with the crisis-hit football nation before several Italian politicians raised concerns about Pirlo's role as an ambassador for Russian betting firm Fonbet.

It was felt Pirlo, who had been prepared to leave his current job as coach of Dubai United, should not have conflicting views on Italy's support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

In the subsequent fallout, Maldini and his assistant Leonardo are reported to have stepped down, too, after just 16 days in their jobs.

Pirlo himself confirmed that he was no longer in the running in an Instagram post on Monday, urging that his Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is 'exclusively for commercial and sports' purposes.

His claim has been refuted by Dubai United owner Sergey Lomakin, who stated that Pirlo's involvement with the firm was not an involuntary aspect of his deal.

Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after a dramatic twist

The Italy legend's appointment has been blocked after 'political' concerns were raised over his sponsorship deal with Russian betting company Fonbet in the United Arab Emirates

Pirlo said in a statement: 'In recent days, I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of Head Coach of the Italian national team.

'Out of respect for the institutions, the Federation, and all those involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now.'

'However, I feel it is my duty to clarify certain aspects.

'Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always conducted my activities in full compliance with the laws of the countries in which I have worked and the contracts I have signed.

'The professional collaboration at the centre of the recent controversy arose as part of my career in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature.'

It is understood Maldini was furious by the decision made by FIGC president Giovanni Malago and quit his role as technical director after Pirlo's appointment was blocked.

Adverts, endorsements and sponsorship deals pertaining to betting are strictly prohibited in Italy.

Pirlo added: 'Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing to me beliefs I have never expressed and that are not mine.

'I would like to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the esteem and trust they have shown me. I know their expertise, their seriousness, and the love they have always dedicated to Italian football.

Paolo Maldini was furious at the decision and has decided to walk away from his role as a result

'I regret that a sporting decision was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing to me meanings and intentions that are not mine.

'My love for Italy does not depend on a position. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.'

Pirlo was at best a third-choice after Carlo Ancelotti and Guardiola turned down offers to coach a team that has failed to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.

Now former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are back being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: First Danny Welbeck, now Jordan Henderson! Chelsea plot deal for England veteran, 36 - with Blues also closing in on move for Brighton star, 35, after he scored 13 Premier League goals last season
Sports.content:
Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Jordan Henderson on a free transfer from Brentford.

After missing out on Sunderland’s Granit Xhaka, the Stamford Bridge club have moved for 36-year-old Henderson to fulfil a role on the pitch and crucially in the dressing room.

As Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed, Chelsea are already closing on a move for Danny Welbeck as manager Xabi Alonso looks to add older heads to a young squad.

Alonso has determined that the squad dynamic needs to change to help Chelsea achieve their goals and maintain a successful challenge to rivals.

There are a number of clubs interested in Henderson, who is still recovering from a fractured arm suffered during the World Cup, including two other Premier League sides, but Chelsea are favourites to sign him.

Chelsea are working on a deal to sign Brentford veteran Jordan Henderson

It comes after Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed talks with Brighton's Danny Welbeck

Earlier on Monday, Daily Mail Sport revealed how 35-year-old Brighton striker Welbeck has emerged as a player of interest within Stamford Bridge, and is now a contender to join the Blues squad under Alonso.

Welbeck has scored 46 goals in 176 games in the Premier League for the Seagulls, having previously played for Manchester United and Arsenal, among others.

Chelsea currently have five strikers on their books in Joao Pedro, who is considered untouchable, Emmanuel Emegha, Liam Delap, Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

The Blues have been looking at sales or loans to trim down their options up front.

Welbeck scored 13 times in the league for Brighton in 2025-26, and was considered unfortunate not to make the England squad under Thomas Tuchel.

Joao Pedro and Delap are currently on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, with Emegha absent due to injury. Jackson is not involved due to his run at the World Cup with Senegal and Guiu has not been selected.

Welbeck joined Brighton in 2020 and triggered a one-year contract extension in March. If he moves to Stamford Bridge he would add to the lengthy list of signings Chelsea have made from Brighton in recent years - including Marc Cucurella, Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez and Joao Pedro.

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare is joining Ajax on loan with a view to a £17million permanent deal.

Ajax have to cover his salary in full on top of a £1m loan fee and have agreed further bonuses if they qualify for European competitions.

Last week, Arokodare forced the cancellation of a Wolves training session after he refused to leave the pitch.

Wolves had rejected a bid from Fiorentina while Trabzonspor had also made an offer but the forward was reluctant to make that move.

Arokodare denied that he refused to train, but he is understood to have put himself into a training session which he was not due to be involved in.

The striker was not involved in last Wednesday's friendly at Maidenhead United after the incident.

Tolu Arokodare trains in Portugal just over a week ago

Afterwards, on social media Arokodare wrote: 'Throughout my career, I have always taken great pride in conducting myself professionally and maintaining the highest training standards.

'My commitment has always been to prepare myself as well as possible so that I can contribute to my team-mates and the club whenever I am called upon.

'I remain under contract with Wolves, and my only intention is to fulfil my responsibilities professionally by training, doing my job, and contributing to the team in accordance with that contract.'

Sports.title: Micky van de Ven warns Tottenham's rivals to prepare for a brand new Spurs after last season's relegation survivors splashed £237MILLION on new stars - and praises the club's 'ambition'
Sports.content:
Micky van de Ven has warned their Premier League rivals to be prepared to see a new Tottenham Hotspur after their ambitious summer spending spree.

Spurs have already spent £237million on signing Sandro Tonali (£100m), Mateus Fernandes (£85m) and Jan Paul van Hecke (£52m). They have also brought in Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

Those acquisitions have helped convince Van de Ven and Spurs’ existing players that they are ready to forget their relegation concerns and focus on a European push instead.

Speaking in Australia, where Spurs are set to face friendlies against Sydney FC and Chelsea this week, the 25-year-old Dutchman said: ‘It’s really good that you can see the club has made some changes. They have brought a really good new manager, and some really good new signings.

‘You can see the club has new ambition. It's something that's really important for players that have been there for a long time. It’s better when you go with a fresh mind into the new season.

'Last season was a stressful season so to leave everything of that behind and go into the new season fresh means a lot. Spurs is a team that needs to play Europe every year, so obviously the European spots are something we are going to aim for.

Micky van de Ven has warned their Premier League rivals to be prepared to see a new Spurs

Spurs have spent £237m on signings including Sandro Tonali (left) and Mateus Fernandes

'The most important thing is we play our football, and that we are a difficult team to play against.’

Spurs' summer signings may help convince Van de Ven to sign a new contract. His current deal runs until 2029. It has been reported that talks could open soon.

Spurs kickstarted their pre-season tour with a 2-0 win over A-League champions Auckland FC on Sunday. Having moved on from New Zealand to Australia, Van de Ven added that Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi will be bringing a brand new style of football – one far superior to that overseen by his predecessors, Igor Tudor and Thomas Frank.

Asked if we will see a different Spurs under De Zerbi, Van de Ven said: ‘I know that for sure.

'It’s going to be different compared to the former manager we had last season. It’s going to be more with the ball I think, more playing football. I think it’s going to be more enjoyable also for people to watch, when playing offensive football.

‘The last couple of weeks of last season, you saw he brought a lot of passion into our group, a lot mentality wise, passion wise, on the pitch. It is something we needed because everybody was a little bit down.

'We started to play a lot with the ball, because he loves us to be on the ball, he loves to play the football he wants to play, and that’s also something I really enjoy.

‘Hopefully it will be (a better season). It's something we are going to work really hard on. Make some differences because last season was a bit unacceptable from our side.’

Sports.title: Spain's Dani Olmo accuses Argentina assistant who punched him in shameful World Cup scenes of LYING - and claims coach 'isn't sorry at all'
Sports.content:
Dani Olmo has accused the Argentina coach who punched him after Spain's World Cup final victory of lying in his attempt to downplay the incident.

Spain's 1-0 triumph was marred by shameful scenes of violence and thuggery as Argentina's players and coaching staff brawled with their opponents after the final whistle before refusing to watch them lift the trophy at MetLife Stadium in New York.

Olmo was one of four Spain players attacked by Argentina during the post-match melee, with coach Roberto Ayala appearing to throw a punch that caught the midfielder in the neck.

Ayala attempted to downplay the incident by stating it was 'more of a shove than a punch' and claimed he had reacted to 'some words' uttered by Olmo and his nearby team-mate Eric Garcia.

The Argentina assistant also issued a public apology and vowed to say sorry 'in person' if he ever sees Olmo again.

Speaking about the incident for the first time since Spain's World Cup final victory on July 19, Olmo refused to accept Ayala's apology and accused him of lying.

Dani Olmo has accused the Argentina coach who punched him at the World Cup of lying

Roberto Ayala clashed with Garcia before he appeared to strike Olmo after last Sunday's final

He told Spanish newspaper Diari de Terrassa: 'Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry.

'He is lying because I didn't say anything to him, so he doesn't need to apologise. What truly defines us is not the mistake, but the courage to acknowledge it with humility, honesty and dignity.

'When my children, my family and all those fans watch the game, I want them to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour, because the importance of football means that us players are an example for children and the new generations, and that brings with it a huge responsibility.'

When questioned about the incident earlier this week, Ayala had said: 'Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

'For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be.

'It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person.'

FIFA have launched an investigation into the deplorable post-match scenes, which could see Argentina heavily fined for failing to control their players and staff.

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes could also face a lengthy ban for lashing out at Garcia before throwing Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle.

Nahuel Molina, meanwhile, was caught on camera striking Rodri in his stomach as Spain's captain ran on to the pitch to celebrate with his team-mates.

Ayala tried to downplay his clash with Olmo by saying it was 'more of a shove than a punch'

Announcing their probe into what had gone on in the aftermath of last Sunday's game, FIFA said: 'Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

'Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.'

Sports.title: The master and the apprentice meet AGAIN in highly-anticipated Goodwood showdown as veteran Trawlerman hunts for revenge over upstart Scandinavia
Sports.content:
The master and the apprentice meet AGAIN in highly-anticipated Goodwood showdown as veteran Trawlerman hunts for revenge over upstart Scandinavia

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

With racing still basking in the afterglow of Saturday’s captivating King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Ascot, Goodwood provides the latest chapter of their ‘Duel on the Downs’ drama in today’s Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup.

By common consensus the Ascot Gold Cup, fought out in captivating fashion on a sweltering Berkshire afternoon last month by the leading men, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, was billed as the race of the season.

That description may have undersold the engrossing confrontation as those with long memories likened it to the ‘Race of the Century’ between Grundy and Bustino in the 1975 King George.

Whatever label is used, the gripping battle is reprised today as the apprentice and the master return to the track for another eagerly awaited showdown as Scandinavia bids to extend his winning sequence to a magnificent seven, while the veteran Trawlerman hunts revenge for his last-gasp Ascot defeat.

At the age of eight, Trawlerman is a complete anomaly.

Capable of running to extraordinarily high levels at an age when most of his counterparts have cried enough, the son of John and Thady Gosden’s 2015 Derby winner Golden Horn will again be equipped with ski goggles in the paddock and on the way to post as his eyes have become sensitive to light.

The Ascot Gold Cup was fought out in captivating fashion last month by the leading men, Scandinavia and Trawlerman, and was billed as the race of the season

Tuesday's tips Goodwood, 1.50pm – Midak each-way The colours of Fitri and Dr Jim Hay are often seen to the fore at the Qatar Goodwood Festival and Midak could begin the meeting in the best possible fashion for the renown owners. The Footstepsinthesand gelding was highly tried for his former handler winning three races in the spring of 2025 prior to having a tilt at the Derby where he went to post at Epsom at just 9/1 to beat Lambourn, Delacriox et al. He has since moved to Ian Williams for 300,000euros and, although he's showed a propensity to race keenly in Britain, today’s assignment represents a first dip into handicap company and the prospect of a true gallop and some cover courtesy of a big field should present more ideal conditions. Goodwood, 3pm – Qirat There is little doubt Lake Forest deserves to be market leader for this event following his eye-catching fifth over six furlongs in Group 1 company at Royal Ascot and he emerged best of those that were held up well off the pace in last year’s contest. However, Qirat was a surprise winner of last year’s Sussex Stakes when afforded the pacesetting role and the victory, albeit a major shock, did enforce that the ability to handle the undulations of Goodwood can go a long way to determining the result, even for a 150/1 shot. The idiosynchratic Sussex venue suits some more than others with its undulations and contours and that certainly applies to recent York scorer Qirat who bids to extend his unbeaten course record to four in this intriguing renewal. Goodwood, 4.45pm - Savage Mariner This six furlong maiden wouldn't be on the radar as one of the best betting heats of the day for many punters, but I'm happy to afford Savage Mariner another chance following his blip at Royal Ascot. The selection chased home impressive Albany Stakes winner Libertango at Leicester in a fast time on debut before failing to take a hand in the Albany Stakes on his latest start after being backed at big prices to figure. The Blackbeard colt holds two Group 2 entries going forward so connections clearly feel he ought to be winning his maiden before heading on to better things.

The affliction nearly cost him a place in the starting line-up at Ascot with Gosden senior admitting it was a race against time to have him ready for the Group 1 marathon before the condition was diagnosed.

In the buildup to this showdown, Gosden junior reports that Trawlerman 'still has all the enthusiasm he has always had' and 'has sharpened up a little bit since' Ascot which augurs well for today’s rematch where he again takes on a rival half his age.

While it isn’t quite Lionel Messi facing Lamine Yamal in a World Cup Final, the main protagonists are at vastly different ends of the age scale and will each have their supporters with the front-running Trawlerman’s prominent run style contrasting nicely with Scandinavia’s more patient approach.

The old boxing adage that styles make fights is certainly appropriate, but today’s feature also boasts strength in depth with the likes of Amiloc, Lazy Griff and Rahiebb all looking to muscle in on the main event and disrupt the status quo.

The former, unbeaten in two starts on the Sussex Downs, tackles two miles for the first time and arrives on the back of an encouraging effort in the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes at Royal Ascot, a contest which produced Saturday’s marquee winner Kalpana.

Lazy Griff represents a team with plenty of heritage in this mid-summer feature, with trainer Charlie Johnston’s father Mark saddling the redoubtable Double Trigger to win three times in four years in the late 1990s.

The Middleham operation also enjoyed success with Royal Rebel (2000) and Darasim four years later and their representative, equipped with the headgear for the first time, remains largely unexposed over today’s trip and will appreciate the efforts of the Goodwood groundstaff who have spent recent weeks watering around the clock.

Rahiebb is another intriguing runner in a race packed full of intrigue and one which should set the scene for a magnificent meeting forecast to be blessed with good weather.

We don’t have to wait long for another prize fight either with tomorrow’s Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes providing another fascinating duel with Betfred 2000 Guineas winner Bow Echo and Gstaad going head-to-head for the third time this season.

The former leads 2-0, but the smooth two and three quarter length margin of victory from the first Classic of the season at Newmarket in May was whittled away to a short head in the St James’s Palace Stakes at Ascot seven weeks ago.

The market suggests the unbeaten Bow Echo will again prevail, but with the highly talented four-year-old Opera Ballo also in opposition, the result is no foregone conclusion and we are set for more drama on the Downs.

Sports.title: Vinicius Junior stays AWAY from Real Madrid training as transfer saga rumbles on: Arsenal target skips pre-season return date amid contract stand-off - with Spanish giants making stance clear
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior stays AWAY from Real Madrid training as transfer saga rumbles on: Arsenal target skips pre-season return date amid contract stand-off - with Spanish giants making stance clear

Arsenal target Vinicius will not return to Real Madrid training this week as doubts over his future rumble on.

The Brazil winger was knocked out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage and with new manager Jose Mourinho laying down the foundations for his second spell in charge of the club the expectation in Madrid was that Vinicius’s could return before the end of the month.

But the player is staying away while his representatives try to revive talks over an extension to his contract that runs out at the end of this coming season.

Madrid’s position is that the player’s future is in his own hands. If he lowers demands to be joint top earner with Kylian Mbappe he will stay.

But if he does not the 15-times European Cup winners have no plans to make an improved offer and the way will be left clear for Arsenal.

Vinicius Jr has not returned to Real Madrid pre-season training amid his contract stand off

New Madrid boss Jose Mourinho had expected the Brazilian to return to training this week

In a move seen as an illustration of that intention not to fold to the players’ will, Real Madrid moved closer yesterday to making their 100m euros capture of Ivory Coast winger Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig official.

The player, represented by the same Roc Nation agency as Vinicius, gives Mourinho yet another attacking option in an already over-populated forward line.

The Daily Mail Sport understands Roc Nation’s talks with Real Madrid will centre on Vinicius’s huge commercial worth to the club.

The player’s current contract means he gives around 50 per cent of publicity-deal revenue to them, during the World Cup he had lucrative deals with 15 multinational sponsors – a number topped only by his international team-mate Neymar.

The 26-year-old has the same representatives as Diomande, who was also on Arsenal's radar, and there has been interest from Saudi Arabi over the past 12 months.

Vinicius is one of a number of forward targets Arsenal are exploring, with Julian Alvarez, Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola also of interest.

Liverpool are considered favourites for Barcola but his situation could change if PSG fail to land Diomande with Madrid leading that charge and trying to close the deal quickly.

He is in the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

The deal would represent a sensational coup for Arsenal if they were successful but the clubs are still to open official talks.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Vinicius Jnr has scored 128 goals across eight seasons in Madrid, and narrowly missed out on the Ballon d'Or to Rodri in 2024.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that Gabriel Martinelli is up for sale as Mikel Arteta looks to add more firepower to his forward line.

Leandro Trossard has already been sold to Besiktas, while Arsenal confirmed the signing of Greek winger Christos Tzolis for £34million from Club Bruges on Thursday.

Sports.title: Chelsea star hails Xabi Alonso's plan with parting dig at Enzo Maresca's style
Sports.content:
Chelsea star hails Xabi Alonso's plan with parting dig at Enzo Maresca's style

Xabi Alonso is the latest man in charge of Chelsea and his style has quickly left a mark on Levi Colwill, who believes he has release the shackles seen under previous managers

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has just taken charge at Chelsea

Chelsea's Levi Colwill has hailed Xabi Alonso's style of football as he took a swipe at his former bosses who had been "really rigid".

‌



The defender spent most of last year on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury in pre-season, restricting him to only four outings across a campaign that saw the Blues have three different men in the dugout - Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane.

‌



Alonso is the latest man to take on the hot seat at Stamford Bridge and the ex-Liverpool boss arrives with some serious pedigree. He claimed the Bundesliga title whilst in charge at Bayer Leverkusen, breaking the stranglehold Bayern Munich had on the German top flight.

‌



His style of play aided Leverkusen as they won the double and he's been quick to get those ideas across during his early weeks at Chelsea - with Colwill praising his principles when compared to those who've come before him.

Chelsea line up shock Danny Welbeck swoop after Xabi Alonso green lights transfer READ MORE :

Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers READ MORE :

He said: "Xabi wants free flowing football, I've had a lot of managers who are really rigid and want you in right positions, but with him, play what you see, find the space and exploited it at a fast pace."

The Blues finished tenth last term after a dire season but Colwill believes the squad have it in them to mix it with the champions. He said: "I feel like the players we've got in our team are ready to do that. With having a manager of this quality now, when it all comes together we're definitely going to be able to challenge and push for the Premier League."

‌



Chelsea have not won the Premier League since 2017 and, under their BlueCo ownership, they've only finished in the top four once. Alonso has refused to go public with any major targets and has suggested that things may not click as quick as some hope.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca and Mauricio Pochettino are the only two managers Levi Colwill has consistently played under

"I don't want to talk too early about what's our goal," he said. "We want to have a good season. We want to deserve to be as high as possible, and for that we need to work hard. We need to develop this team with new players, new coach, new ideas. Sometimes it takes longer, sometimes it happens quicker.

Article continues below

"So be ready to try to develop this idea that we have, this plan. But so far, good feeling. Good energy. The players are working hard, and that's what we want."

Sports.title: England to play two of seven Euro 2028 matches away from Wembley in best-case scenario
Sports.content:
England to play two of seven Euro 2028 matches away from Wembley in best-case scenario

England will co-host Euro 2028 with Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland

View 2 Images England are set to play the majority of their Euro 2028 matches at Wembley Stadium (Image: PA Wire)

England may have to play just two matches away from Wembley Stadium at the European Championships in 2028 if they make it all the way to the final. Thomas Tuchel's side will be among the favourites to win the tournament as hosts and having finished third at the recent World Cup.

‌



The Three Lions still have to qualify for the competition, as per new UEFA rules which means only two of the host nations will qualify for the tournament. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will all have to navigate the usual qualifying campaign.

‌



If any of the nations fail to qualify, then the two country's with the highest qualifying rank will take one of the backup spots. It means that in a worst-case scenario, the two highest ranked nations are still guaranteed a place.

‌



Pep Guardiola's telling reasons for rejecting Italy job as England learn stance READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Northern Ireland had been in contention to host the tournament with the rest of the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, but it failed to secure the £400million funding to bring Casement Park up to scratch.

Games will be held across nine different venues in eight cities, in London at Wembley Stadium and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, The Etihad Stadium in Manchester, the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, St James' Park in Newcastle, Villa Park in Birmingham, Hampden Park in Glasgow and the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

‌



If England qualify for the tournament, they'll play their first game at the Etihad Stadium, before two games at Wembley Stadium. Should they qualify at the top of their group, they'll likely play their round of 16 clash at St. James' Park in the only two games to be played on the road.

View 2 Images Euro 2028 will take place in the UK and Ireland (Image: James Manning/Getty Images)

Each of the four host nations will host a quarter-final tie, with the Three Lions clash still on home soil in the North East of England. England will then return to Wembley Stadium for the quarter-final and semi-finals, with the showpiece finale also held at the home of English football.

‌



Unlike the recent World Cup, fans will be able to watch the majority of games, with kick-offs at normal times throughout the tournament.

The tournament itself will get underward on will kick off on June 9, 2028, with the curtain raiser at the Prinicpality Stadium in Cardiff, running for a month until July 9, 2028, with the final at Wembley.

There'll be 24 teams qualify for the tournament, with four nations in six groups, playing a total of 36 matches over 12 days - a stark difference compared to this summer's World Cup.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd boss wanted to re-sign Danny Welbeck as Chelsea open transfer talks
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd boss wanted to re-sign Danny Welbeck as Chelsea open transfer talks

Chelsea have opened talks with Brighton to sign Danny Welbeck, who could've returned to boyhood club Manchester United had a former Red Devils manager got his way

View 2 Images Danny Welbeck was linked with a return to Manchester United (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester United blocked Erik ten Hag's attempt to sign Danny Welbeck in 2024 - and now the veteran striker could end up at rivals Chelsea. The Blues have opened talks with Brighton to sign Welbeck, who's still banging in the goals at Premier League level aged 35.

‌



The former United star is understood to be keen on a move to Stamford Bridge. But Welbeck could've returned to Old Trafford a couple of years ago, with Ten Hag pushing the Red Devils to re-sign him as a replacement for Anthony Martial.

‌



Ten Hag had seen Welbeck's ability first hand, having tormented United in the Dutchman's very first game in charge two years prior. His goalscorer record, impeccable fitness and leadership qualities appealed to him.

‌



But Ten Hag didn't get his wish. According to The Athletic, United discussed signing Welbeck after Ten Hag's recommendation, but they ultimately didn't make an offer during what was a summer filled with changes above Ten Hag, with his own future uncertain at one stage.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

Welbeck addressed the report during an interview with The Times a few weeks later. "It's speculation and there's always that link for me because I've been at the club," he explained. "As I said, I'm just focusing on what I can control myself and all the other stuff is pretty irrelevant."

‌



The Red Devils' focus turned to signing younger players, with Benjamin Sesko arriving last summer at the age of 22. United have been linked with signing an experienced striker this summer but nothing has materialised, with Michael Carrick's three signings coming in goal and midfield.

As for Welbeck, he's set to join Xabi Alonso's Chelsea. The ex-England international, who was tipped for a World Cup call-up this summer, scored a career-best 13 league goals last season.

Should Manchester United hijack Chelsea's move for Danny Welbeck? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Erik ten Hag wanted to sign Danny Welbeck (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

United legend Gary Neville reckons that Welbeck should never have been allowed to leave Old Trafford, having been sold by Louis van Gaal to Arsenal for £16million in 2014. "Danny Welbeck, to be fair, should never have been let go at United," Neville affirmed on the Stick to Football podcast.

"If you've got a squad of 24, 23, and you want to keep five or six strikers, he's got to be one of those. You've got to keep him."
