World.title: Why public servants have less than a month to update pension records
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Public servants given until August 14 to update pension records [File]

Government has directed all public servants to update their records with the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) by August 14, 2026, in the latest step towards modernising pension administration.

In a circular signed by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Capital Development Dr Jane Imbunya, all PSSF members are expected to update their personal information and beneficiary details through the PSSF Member Self-Service Portal or the PSSF Mobile Application.

The circular was addressed to Ministries, State Departments, Constitutional Commissions, Independent Offices, County Public Service Boards and County Governments.

The exercise is expected to streamline pension administration and accelerate the processing of retirement benefits supported by a new Pension Administration System (PAS), a digital platform developed by PSSF to deliver faster, more transparent and more efficient pension services.

The registration exercise targets 529,635 members drawn from across the public service, including 332,950 teachers under the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), 120,084 officers in the disciplined services, 60,322 employees in Ministries, Departments, Constitutional Commissions and Agencies (MDCAs), and 16,279 county government employees.

PSSF Chief Executive Jonah Aiyabei said updating member records is critical to the success of the pension reforms and the delivery of efficient retirement services.

“By updating their records, public servants will enable quicker processing of retirement benefits, reduce administrative delays, improve data integrity, allow members to access pension services seamlessly through digital channels and ensure that the right benefits reach the right beneficiaries at the right time,” he said.

Under the new system, members can access their pension statements in real time, monitor contributions, view projected retirement benefits, update beneficiary nominations and personal details and initiate and track pension claims remotely.

The platform also features a Sponsor Portal that enables employer institutions to submit payroll information, contribution schedules and member data electronically, significantly improving efficiency and accountability in pension administration.

Dr Aiyabei said the Pension Administration System marks a significant milestone in the government’s efforts to digitise pension administration and restore dignity to retirees through faster, more accessible and transparent services.

“It will provide our members with real-time access to their pension information, enable seamless engagement with the Fund and support a fully digital, paperless pension administration process. Ultimately, our goal is to restore dignity in old age by ensuring every public servant receives timely and efficient pension services,” he said.

World.title: Madrid wildfires advancing more slowly but remain “uncontrolled,” authorities say
World.content:
The wildfires tearing through the landscape just west of Madrid advanced more slowly overnight but remain “active and uncontrolled,” Spanish authorities said this morning.

The slower pace of advance allowed firefighting teams to battle the flames, and they identified three fronts, with the most active one located in the hills just north of the San Juan Reservoir, which contain several hiking trails and local beauty spots.

About 15 kilometers south of that hotspot, some elderly residents will be allowed to return to their care home in the town of San Martín de Valdeiglesias, said local official Francisco Martín Aguirre, the Spanish government’s delegate in Madrid.

World.title: AI devices that see, listen and record: Are we ready for the post-smartphone world?
World.content:
Picture this: On a normal workday, you and your coworkers walk around the office with tiny recorders clipped to your clothes. The glasses on your face nearly instantly identify what you see. Your bracelet records and analyzes all your conversations.

This is the future tech companies envision in the age of AI, whether consumers want it or not.

Major tech companies and startups are developing new types of wearable gadgets that can “see” or “hear.” Meta is selling millions of its EssilorLuxottica AI glasses with embedded cameras and microphones; Samsung will launch its own smart glasses later this year.

Wearing these items can give AI assistants instantaneous access to your life. Tech leaders hope that will help AI agents give advice tailored to users and, eventually, do things for you.

I personally tried to live in that future, integrating different wearables into my work and personal life. They were helpful in certain situations. But I often felt awkward asking friends and coworkers to record our interactions.

Devices that can watch you – and others – also put privacy at risk, experts say.

Unlike phones, they’re harder to spot, said Irina Raicu, director of the internet ethics program at Santa Clara University’s Marukkula Center for Applied Ethics.

“So the whole notion of consent is kind of disintegrating,” she said.

Trying them out

For years, tech companies tracked our lives via search trends, shopping habits, locations, and fitness routines online. Now, AI-enabled devices open up the possibility of using broader input from your real-world surroundings.

I wore three devices over the past several months – Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses, the Amazon Bee Pioneer wristband and Plaud’s Notepin S, a small recorder that you can clip onto your clothing. I took them to office, on work trips, even during vacation and at social gatherings. (The companies all provided them to CNN for testing.)

At times, I understood the appeal.

On a trip to Lisbon in April, I didn’t have to take out my phone to Google information about the Jerónimos Monastery, one of city’s most iconic landmarks. Meta’s smart glasses took a photo (with my consent), analyzed the image and came back with a response almost instantly.

I wore the Meta Ray-Ban glasses during my visit to Lisbon to learn about landmarks and take photos without reaching for my phone. CNN

The Amazon Bee Pioneer, a tiny recorder worn as a wristband that listens and offers advice, was helpful for networking events. It felt more natural to record conversations (with permission) without holding my phone, and the app suggested a contact for me to follow up with afterwards. The same goes for Plaud’s Notepin S, which I usually attached to the top of my shirt.

But often, these gadgets sat buried in my backpack or a desk drawer. That’s because using them socially felt strange.

As a journalist, I’m used to asking for permission to record an interview, but it felt odd during a game night with friends or even a one-on-one meeting with a coworker. Was the social unease worth taping these conversations?

A new wave of AI gadgets aims to listen to your conversations and provide advice or suggestions based on those chats. Ian Berry/CNN Photo Illustration

Things also took a weird turn at times. During that board game night, I mentioned moving to a new apartment in the fall. The next time I opened the Bee app, it reminded me to book movers for October, which was useful.

Then Bee said it thought my words indicated the move was triggering anxiety about “stability” and my “sense of home.” It suggested I photograph “one beloved corner” of my current space to take with me.

It was a glimpse into what could happen when AI assistants try to make conclusions by observing you instead of what you’ve specifically told them. I didn’t feel anxious about the move and certainly didn’t mean to convey that to anyone – not my friends, not my husband and certainly not my AI bracelet.

Amazon said Bee is designed to surface insights and recommendations based on what it learns about a user over time, and that insights can be less precise early on when drawing from limited context. Users can also mark certain Bee insights as inaccurate to help it surface more relevant advice moving forward.

“We’re constantly refining how Grow works, and the experience will continue to improve,” an Amazon spokesperson said in a statement to CNN.

The push for AI gadgets

My experiences are likely just a slice of where things are headed.

“Some of the largest companies in the world right now” are developing gadgets like AI pendants, pins and jewelry, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon told CNN and a small group of journalists in June.

For Amazon, Bee is key to the future of its Alexa assistant. Most people would want a personal assistant that has context about their entire day, not just time spent in the house, Panos Panay, Amazon’s senior vice president of devices and Alexa, told CNN.

Plaud’s Notepin S can be clipped to your shirt to record conversations. CNN The Amazon Bee Pioneer bracelet can record conversations with the press of a button. CNN

“The more they know, the better off they can complete tasks for you, and help you do what’s next. That’s quite powerful,” he said. “So it kind of leads to this: What are the future devices that connect you to your assistant?”

Nathan Xu, the CEO of Plaud, thinks his company’s recording devices may one day create a shorter work week. He thinks what’s captured on devices could help AI models better understand our jobs with less prompting, potentially helping people get work done faster.

OpenAI is working on a family of hardware gadgets, President Greg Brockman told reporters on Thursday. As AI agents advance, Brockman said the days of keyboards and mice will soon be behind us.

“Clicking things and typing things, it was a phase,” he said. “It was never what we wanted to be.”

‘Misused in dangerous ways’

The tech industry’s rosy outlook is at odds with how many people feel about AI – especially AI gadgets that can record you.

None has gotten more pushback than Meta’s AI glasses. Women have reported that men have used the eyewear to film and post videos of them on social media without their consent.

That inspired harsh words from pop singer Lorde.

“Can I just say for the record: F**k the glasses,” she recently said on stage.

Meta is now taking down those videos from Instagram. And Meta’s glasses – as well as the Bee Pioneer bracelet and Plaud Notepin S – have lights to indicate recording. Meta said the glasses’ camera won’t work if it’s covered up.

“We’ve built privacy into the camera for the glasses from the ground up – a capture LED will blink bright white when you take a photo or video you can save or share,” Meta spokesperson Dina El-Kassaby said in a statement to CNN. “This light has no off switch so both people wearing the glasses and those around them feel comfortable.”

A picture taken on March 2, 2026 in Barcelona shows Ray Ban META AI glasses displayed at the Mobile World Congress (MWC), the world’s biggest mobile technology showcase and fair. Manaure Quintero/AFP/Getty Images

But lights on some devices can be difficult to see since most people aren’t looking at your wrist or shirt when talking to you.

Wearable gadgets with microphones and cameras are risky because they can be discretely worn in areas that are meant to be private like a dressing room, said Calli Schroeder, senior counsel and director of the AI & Human Rights program at the Electronic Privacy and Information Center.

“There are some real concerns with how this could be misused in dangerous ways,” said Schroeder.

But tech giants seem sold on the idea of computers that can observe our surroundings. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg suggested on an earnings call last year that AI glasses could give people a “cognitive” edge.

“If you don’t have glasses that have AI or some way to interact with AI, I think you’re … at a pretty significant cognitive disadvantage compared to other people who you’re working with, or competing against,” he said.

World.title: Iran “will never allow the United States to determine timing of war,” foreign ministry says
World.content:
Iran on Monday said it is not currently engaging in peace talks with the United States and will “defend ourselves for as long as our interests” require, after President Donald Trump paused the US’ bombing campaign following nearly two weeks of strikes.

Esmaeil Baghaei, the Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, said in a televised press conference that Tehran “will never allow the United States to determine the timing of war and peace.”

“We hold America responsible for the military aggression against Iran,” added Baghaei. “What exists at present cannot be called a ceasefire.”

Trump over the weekend halted lethal strikes, which had steadily intensified over the past 13 days. US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said Sunday the pause in strikes was to allow talks with Iran to develop.

The recent dip in attacks came as Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers have convened in Tehran to discuss shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Baghaei said those ongoing bilateral discussions, are “useful negotiations regarding the management of shipping traffic” in the crucial waterway and “are unrelated to the United States.”

“The goal is for Iran and Oman, as two coastal states, to establish mechanisms to ensure safe shipping in the Strait of Hormuz while respecting the sovereign rights and sovereignty of both coastal states and observing Iran’s security and national interests,” he said.

The foreign ministry spokesperson also condemned US-allied European countries, including France and the UK, for “complicity with the aggressor.”

“We expected the new British government to act more wisely than the previous government,” said Baghaei.

World.title: Iran war casualty count eclipses 600 as Pentagon quietly changes accounting
World.content:
The Pentagon updated its war casualty database Saturday, recording more than 140 additionally wounded and restoring the four soldiers killed due to Iranian strikes last week amid questions about a lack of transparency over the war’s toll.

The Defense Casualty Analysis System, or DCAS, also featured a new tracking category — “Overseas Operations” — for killed and wounded “starting July 7.”

When the new Pentagon data is combined with updated totals for Operation Epic Fury, 18 troops have died and another 624 have been wounded since the US launched its war against Iran on Feb. 28. The number of wounded is a significant increase from the previous peak of 482 observed by CNN last week.

The Pentagon drew scrutiny from media outlets and lawmakers last week when killed and wounded numbers decreased in the DCAS system as Iranian attacks continued. The 12 Democratic lawmakers on the Senate Armed Services Committee sent a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday requesting answers on what was causing the changes.

The Defense Department’s acting press secretary, Joel Valdez, insisted in a Thursday social media post that the decreases were due to “temporary data disruptions on the (DCAS) website.” CNN observed data glitches that led to fluctuating casualty totals when monitoring the DCAS site on a minute-by-minute basis last week.

On Friday, CNN asked the Pentagon for more details about the data interruption, but the department neither acknowledged nor responded to the inquiry as of Sunday afternoon.

Beyond the July 7 starting date, the new “overseas operation” category on the DCAS site does not include any distinguishing details or specify the conflict in which the casualties occur, and the Pentagon did not immediately respond to questions seeking clarification on what the category covers. The category features a by-name list of fallen troops, though, that includes the three Army soldiers killed in Jordan due to an Iranian strike and the soldier killed in northern Iraq last weekend during a controlled detonation of an Iranian drone.

The July 7 date coincides with when President Donald Trump claimed a new conflict with Iran began in a War Powers notification the administration sent to Congress earlier this month. (The War Powers Act of 1973 requires the president to end military operations within 60 days unless authorized by Congress to continue; the Trump administration argued that the April ceasefire with Iran stopped the clock on May 1 for the conflict’s initial period.)

Lawmakers of both parties have argued against the administration’s interpretation of the War Powers clock, though some analysts and officials contend that the act itself represents an unconstitutional limit on presidential war-making authority. Secretary of State Marco Rubio argued the law is “unconstitutional, 100 percent” during a May press briefing at the White House.

Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski of Alaska said to Hegseth during a July 21 hearing that she is “concerned” the administration is circumventing Congress through the ceasefire clock reset.

“The claim essentially allows the president to extinguish the War Powers clock just at the moment that it becomes legally inconvenient … avoiding the congressional authorization that the Constitution requires and the War Powers (Act) intends,” she said.

Davis Winkie’s work at CNN is supported by a partnership between Outrider Foundation and Journalism Funding Partners (JFP). CNN retains full editorial control of the reporting.

World.title: Egyptian, Tunisian FMs hail bilateral relations and regional coordination
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and Tunisian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Migration, Mohamed Ali Nafti affirmed on Sunday, July 26, 2026, during a phone call that the special nature of bilateral relations and historic bonds uniting both nations.

The two ministers praised the development of ties and hailed the outcomes of the 18th Egyptian-Tunisian Joint Higher Committee held in Cairo last September, emphasizing the importance of following up on agreements to boost economic, commercial, and investment cooperation.

Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations across various fields.

Regionally, Abdelatty briefed his Tunisian counterpart on Egypt’s efforts and contacts with regional and international parties regarding rapid regional developments to de-escalate tension and support stability.

He underscored Egypt’s stance calling for an immediate halt to all military actions, prioritizing political solutions, and intensifying Arab coordination to safeguard regional security.

Regarding Libya, Abdelatty praised the results of the Tripartite Neighboring Countries mechanism ministerial meeting hosted by Cairo on May 21, stressing the need to maintain its regular meetings to support Libyan unity, sovereignty, and national institutions.

World.title: Electricity Minister presents renewable energy plans to ambassadors
World.content:
Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat met on Sunday, July 26, 2026, with Egyptian ambassadors and heads of diplomatic missions to present investment opportunities in the country’s renewable energy sector and discuss plans to expand international cooperation.

During the meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the New Capital, Esmat reviewed Egypt’s strategy to increase investment in solar and wind energy, modernize the national power grid and accelerate the transition to smart grid technologies.

He said that Egypt offers many investment opportunities in renewable energy and electricity infrastructure, supported by an expanding network of international partnerships and government policies aimed at increasing private sector participation.

Esmat added that Egypt is working to strengthen its position as a regional energy hub through electricity interconnection projects with Sudan, Libya, Jordan and Saudi Arabia, as well as planned links with Greece and Italy, which will support cross-border trade in clean electricity.

He also noted that the updated national energy strategy targets increasing the share of renewable energy to 45% of total electricity generation by 2028, while continuing efforts to localize electrical equipment manufacturing and attract foreign investment.

Additionally, the minister reviewed the ongoing projects to improve grid efficiency, expand battery energy storage, upgrade electricity distribution networks and reduce reliance on conventional fuels.

World.title: Egypt, Bosnia discuss boosting tourism cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy discussed with Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations Stasa Kosarac on Sunday, July 26, 2026, ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism during a meeting at the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM).

Fathy highlighted the strong ties between the two countries and their shared commitment to expanding cooperation, particularly in the fields of tourism and antiquities.

He also reviewed the outcome of his recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina, including talks on advancing bilateral tourism cooperation.

The discussions focused on increasing tourist flows between the two countries, promoting their tourism products and expanding air connectivity to support travel and tourism.

The two ministers also explored cooperation in tourism training and capacity building, as well as mechanisms for activating a memorandum of understanding on tourism cooperation signed during Fathy’s recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

They further discussed participation in Expo 2027 in Belgrade, describing the event as an opportunity to promote the tourism destinations of both countries and organize business-to-business (B2B) meetings between tourism stakeholders to explore new avenues of cooperation.

Following the meeting, Kosarac and his delegation toured the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Giza Pyramids, accompanied by Fathy.

World.title: FM asserts Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty asserted Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait, its leadership, government and people.

He also asserted Egypt’s condemnation of all unjustified attacks targeting the country’s security, stability and sovereignty.

The remarks came during a phone call between Abdelatty and Kuwaiti Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah as part of ongoing consultations and coordination between the two brotherly countries on regional developments and efforts to de-escalate tensions and restore security and stability across the region.

During the call, Abdelatty conveyed the greetings of President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to Kuwaiti Emir Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah and Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah.

The two ministers also discussed regional and international efforts aimed at reducing tensions.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of an immediate halt to all military actions and escalation, a return to negotiations and prioritizing political and diplomatic solutions to contain growing tensions and preserve regional security and stability.

He emphasized that the security and stability of the Gulf are an integral part of Arab national security, underscoring the importance of adhering to the principles of good neighborliness, respecting state sovereignty and refraining from interference in the internal affairs of other countries.

Abdelatty also briefed his Kuwaiti counterpart on Egypt’s intensive consultations with a number of regional and international partners to advance de-escalation efforts.

He stressed the importance of maintaining close coordination and consultation between Egypt and Kuwait in the coming period and continuing joint efforts to support initiatives aimed at restoring security and stability in the region.

For his part, the Kuwaiti foreign minister praised Egypt’s commitment to continuous consultation with Kuwait and commended Cairo’s firm stance condemning the attacks directed against Kuwait.

World.title: Clergy hail peaceful campaigns
World.content:
The clergy on the Copperbelt have commended the peaceful conduct of political campaigns, describing the prevailing calm as a sign of growing political tolerance among candidates and their supporters.

House of Clergy Zambia National Executive Director Jimmy Ng’ambi told the media in an interview that the peaceful campaigns demonstrate that political players now appreciate that elections are a democratic process in which differing views and ideas should be respected.

Mr. Ng’ambi said tolerance among political parties is essential to maintaining peace before, during and after the general elections.

He noted that people are now able to move about freely wearing the regalia of their preferred political parties without fear of intimidation or persecution.

Mr. Ng’ambi also commended the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) for introducing a campaign timetable, saying it has helped maintain law and order.

“The timetable clearly shows which political party is scheduled to campaign in a particular ward at a given time, and this has helped maintain peace and order during the campaign period,” he said.

Meanwhile, Kingdom Springs of Life Embassy Church Senior Pastor Reverend Trevor Muziya attributed the peaceful campaigns to responsible leadership and political maturity among contestants.

Rev Muziya said most political parties have respected the ECZ campaign guidelines by adhering to the designated campaign schedules, despite a few isolated incidents.

“From my observation, political parties have respected the ECZ guidelines on campaign schedules. Apart from the incident in Ndola’s Mapalo area, where two parties almost clashed, the situation was resolved peacefully,” he said.

Rev. Muziya has appealed to political parties and their supporters to continue upholding peace before, during and after the August general elections.

World.title: Investments worth US$19.07 billion actualised-ZDA
World.content:
The Zambia Development Agency (ZDA) has announced that investments worth US$19.07 billion have been actualised.

Addressing a media briefing in Lusaka today, ZDA Director General Albert Halwampa said the actualisation is for the period between 2021 and 2026, while 2,338 investment licences were issued valued at US$97 billion during the same period.

Mr Halwampa said the actualised investments were recorded from 838 licensed companies monitored by the agency, adding that the figure is expected to rise as more investors submit implementation reports.

“I would like to inform the nation that investor confidence has never been this high. It’s actually the highest ever in terms of investor confidence in the country,” Mr Halwampa Said.

He said the US$97 billion in investment licences issued over the past five years exceeds the US$70 billion worth of licences granted between 2007 and 2020, describing the achievement as evidence of Zambia’s growing attractiveness as an investment destination.

“The manufacturing sector accounted for the largest share of actualised investment at US$7.33 billion, followed by mining at US$6.62 billion, transport at US$1.60 billion, energy at US$1.43 billion, agriculture at US$669 million, construction at US$521 million, while other sectors accounted for US$901 million,” he stated.

He further explained that Lusaka Province attracted the highest actualised investment at US$9 billion, followed by Copperbelt Province with US$4.4 billion and North-Western Province with US$3.3 billion, while the remaining provinces accounted for a combined US$999 million.

Mr Halwampa said the monitored investments created 149,956 direct jobs, with mining accounting for 48,007 jobs, manufacturing 46,759, agriculture 18,627, transport 14,743, services 8,065, and other sectors 13,755.

He indicated that the government remains focused on increasing the conversion of pledged investments into operational projects through the Zambia Investment Deal Room, an online platform that links local and foreign investors with banks, institutional investors and international financiers.

Mr Halwampa has since encouraged both local and foreign investors to utilise the platform and take advantage of incentives offered by the ZDA, adding that the agency remains committed to supporting investment that drives sustainable economic growth and employment creation across the country.

World.title: Copper Queens open WAFCON campaign against Egypt
World.content:
The Copper Queens will kick off their 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) campaign on Tuesday with a Group C clash against Egypt at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat. Kick-off is 19h00.

The Nora Häuptle-tutored side has been in Morocco for three days following preparations in Algeria.

Speaking at a pre-match media conference, Coach Häuptle said the team is fit and ready.

“We can’t wait to start the tournament. Of course we had preparations in Algeria. Our players in camp are fit and ready,” she said.

The Swiss tactician said Zambia will be aggressive but will not underrate the Egyptians.

“We are wary of our opposition to Egypt. We are starting against Egypt, a footballing nation. We can’t underrate them, but we are focusing on ourselves,” Häuptle said.

Captain Barbra Banda said the mood in camp is high.

“The mood is very high in camp. The girls are excited to start tomorrow, and we can’t wait for the game. We take each game as it comes. Our focus is on the game against Egypt,” Banda said.

FAZ General Secretary Charles Chakatazya addressed the team ahead of the tournament.

“The coach picked 26 of you to represent over 22 million Zambian people. Most of you played at the World Cup and saw what happened. It changed the lives of a number of you. Those who have been there should encourage those who haven’t because another opportunity is before us,” Chakatazya said.

He urged the players to support the technical bench and play as a team.

“Let’s work hard, support the coach and the technical bench. We should support our friends; no pointing fingers. Once you are a team, when one makes a mistake, you cover up, correct the mistake and talk later,” he added.

Zambia will be aiming to better their 2022 WAFCON bronze medal achievement.

FULL SQUAD FOR THE 2026 WAFCON

Goalkeepers

World.title: Hamukale seeks higher FRA maize target
World.content:
Agriculture Economist Edify Hamukale has called on the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) to increase its maize purchase target for the 2026 market season from five hundred thousand metric tonnes to one million metric tonnes.

In a statement made available to the media in Chilanga, Dr. Hamukale said the proposed increase is necessary given Zambia’s annual maize consumption and the looming climatic risks that could affect food security in the coming year.

Dr Hamukale, explained that Zambia’s annual maize consumption stands at about three million, five hundred thousand metric tonnes adding that with such high demand, a purchase target of only five hundred thousand metric tonnes leaves the country with a very narrow safety margin.

He observed that climatic risks such as the anticipated El Nino present a serious threat to production.

“Without maximum state storage, we are operating on a very thin risk margin looking at the year ahead, which does not look attractive or predictable,” stated Dr Hamukale.

He recommended that regardless of the current storage inadequacies, the presence of 2025 carry-over stock or budgetary considerations, it is prudent for FRA to aim higher this season.

Dr Hamukale further warned that El Nino is expected in the 2026/2027 rain season and is likely to bring drought and poor harvests in 2027.

He however, welcomed the government’s announcement of K347 per 50kg bag of maize noting that the increase of K7 from last year’s price was marginal and positive for both farmers and consumers.

Dr Hamukale added that maintaining a stable purchase price will help keep food prices stable and predictable over a long period.

World.title: Man commits suicide in Mambwe
World.content:
A 42-year-old man of Mambwe District in Eastern province has committed suicide by taking maize preservative tablets.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba has identified the deceased as David Phiri, who served as an internal auditor at Chadiza Town Council.

Mr Mweemba said that the matter was reported by the deceased’s cousin.

Mr Mweemba said that the motive for the suicide is not known.

However, unverified reports suggest that the deceased defiled a 15-year-old housemaid in Chadiza District.

“Brief facts of the matter are that the deceased was on Leave from work and had travelled to Mambwe from Chadiza to work on his plot in Jumbe Village while lodging at the Mambwe Town Council Guest House.

On July 25th, 2026, the deceased was seen drinking alcohol and playing pool with friends at a bar within the Central Business district, afterwards, he parted ways with his friends,” he explained.

“At around 02 hours, on the morning of 26th July 2026, nearby residents heard someone screaming from the direction of the deceased’s plot but did not go to check.

At 07:00hours, passers-by discovered the deceased lying motionless at his plot and immediately informed the police,” Mr Mweemba added.

Mr Mweemba said police officers visited the scene where the deceased was identified by relatives, adding that a physical inspection of the body showed no visible injuries.

“A strong chemical smell was emanating from the body and particles suspected to be from the maize preservative tablets were found near the body together with a bottle of whiskey,” he detailed.

He said that the body of the deceased was deposited into Mambwe District Hospital Mortuary awaiting burial as no foul play was suspected.

World.title: Voter education gains momentum in Chinsali
World.content:
Mafinga District Election Officer (DEO) Joseph Nonde says Voter Education has continued to gain momentum in all the wards of Mafinga South and North Constituencies as voting day draws closer.

Speaking in a telephone interview this morning with the media in Chinsali, Mr. Nonde described the voter education so far facilitation as a success.

He said the Voter Education Facilitators have performed extremely well, owing to the fact that the district has no community radio station and lacks a radio signal from the national broadcaster, ZNBC.

Mr Nonde pointed out that the VEFs are utilizing community engagements such as community gatherings, functions, and roadshows, coupled with door-to-door sensitizations to ensure that the right information reaches the general public.

“We are also taking advantage of church gatherings, public meetings, and open markets which are held in all the wards every week,” he said.

The DEO said the program is on course in terms of meeting targets to ensure that every electorate is sensitized on what is expected of them before, during, and after the election, despite communication challenges in some instances.

He added that the district has continued to maintain a peaceful atmosphere throughout the campaigns, stating that no violence has been recorded.

The DEO, however, said the district has witnessed clashes between political parties due to a failure to adhere to the campaign timetable, which was resolved amicably between the parties involved.

Mr Nonde attributes the peace prevailing in the district to the successful implementation of voter education by the VEFs.

The DEO has since commended the VEFs for the job they are doing in sensitizing electorates across communities.

He said the Commission’s activities, such as the liaison meetings for political parties where parameters, expectations, and zones were set, have helped in fostering peace and peaceful campaigns among political players.

“So far, this is what has helped us to maintain peace, and I wish to commend political parties for upholding peace since the campaigns started. As a district, we are happy that Mafinga is violence-free,” he said.

Mr Nonde further disclosed that the district is ready for the forthcoming polls next month, adding that currently, the Commission is sorting out applications for polling staff in readiness for the national exercise on August 13th, 2026.

He said by next week, the selection of ECZ polling staff will be underway, as human capital is a major milestone in the election process.

The DEO all activities leading to the successful implementation of the electoral process have been done in line with the Commission’s guidelines.

World.title: Mpulungu Clergy calls for compassionate campaigns
World.content:
A Catholic clergy in Mpulungu District has called on Catholic faithfuls to continue conducting their election campaigns with empathy and compassion.

Henry Chisoka has emphasised the importance of understanding and kindness in community outreach efforts, urging believers to prioritize empathy over mere rhetoric.

Speaking during his farewell message to the Christians at Stella Maris Parish during the Sunday service yesterday, Chisoka highlighted that genuine compassion can foster unity and positive change within society, which aligns with the core teachings of the Catholic Church.

He encouraged faithfuls to reflect on Christ’s love in their actions, especially during the election period.

“Social development, charity work, and politics should not be a battleground of hatred and division, but a platform for unity and understanding among all citizens,” he said.

“Political campaigns often become heated and divisive, which usually lead to unnecessary conflict and misunderstandings but as faithfuls we must strive to resist the temptation to engage in inflammatory rhetoric and instead focus on listening to different perspectives with an open heart,” he added.

Brother Chisoka further explained that prayer and reflection during this time is vital for the nation and fostering empathy can help reduce tension and promote constructive dialogue among candidates and voters alike.

He urged Catholics to pray for wisdom and patience as they navigate the political landscape noting that a prayerful approach can help voters discern their choices wisely and act with integrity.

He reminded the faithful that their conduct during campaigns reflects their faith and can influence others positively, adding that faith and politics can coexist harmoniously when guided by compassion and empathy.

Brother Chisoka has also called on political leaders to run their campaigns with honesty, humility, and respect for their opponents.

He said by setting an example, leaders can inspire their supporters to conduct themselves with similar compassion as true leadership is rooted in service and understanding rather than arrogance and divisiveness.

He expressed hope that the upcoming elections will be conducted in a spirit of unity and mutual respect as Christians must take political campaigns as an opportunity to demonstrate the core Christian values of love and empathy in the public sphere.

And Christians of Stella Maris Parish have praised Chisoka for his dedication to the church.

Center Executive Chairperson Carol Chomba who spoke on behalf of the congregation said the unwavering commitment of Chisoka to the church community is highlighted in his numerous contributions to spiritual growth and outreach programs over his 14 months pastoral stay.

“As a community we will continue to pray for you and we hope our collective prayers and well-wishes will serve as a source of strength for you as you move forward, carrying with you our love and blessings of Stella Maris Parish,” she said.

Ms Chomba said Brother Chisoka’s leadership and compassion have left an indelible mark on both parishioners and staff, fostering a sense of unity and hope within the parish.

She revealed that Chisoka’s kindness and devotion had positively impacted people’s lives both old and young because of his willingness to lend a helping hand during times of need.

World.title: Parents hail new classroom construction in Mbala
World.content:
Parents in Mwambala area in Mbala District in Northern Province, have commended Government for constructing a new classroom block at Mwambala Primary School.

The construction of a classroom block follows the collapse of the school’s previous classroom structure during the last rainy season, prompting the Government to construct a new classroom block.

Speaking on behalf of the parents, Parents Committee Chairperson, Alick Chazya has also thanked the Government for providing 120 desks to Mwambala School, saying the gesture has greatly improved the learning environment.

Mr, Chazya has since appealed to the Government to deploy more teachers at the school.

He explained that the school has been experiencing a shortage of teaching staff following the transfer of three teachers since last year and during the first term of this year, without any replacements.

“The school currently has only four teachers, down from seven, making it difficult to effectively manage teaching and learning, we appeal to the government to consider sending more teachers to the school,” he said.

Meanwhile, Mwambala Primary School Headteacher, Ivor Sikazwe said the School offers classes from Grade One to Grade Seven and has a total enrolment of 316 pupils.

Mr Sikazwe notes that although some schools operate with as few as three teachers, the staffing levels at Mwambala Primary School remain inadequate considering its enrolment.

He expressed hope that the school would benefit from the Government’s upcoming teacher recruitment exercise.
