World.title: World’s third public statue of Freddie Mercury unveiled on Lake Balaton – but it bears a striking resemblance to a Hungarian poet
World.content:
The first public statue of Queen legend Freddie Mercury in Hungary has been unveiled on the shores of Lake Balaton, in what is – somewhat surprisingly – only the third such monument in the world.

The statue was inaugurated on Saturday evening in Balatonszemes, a lakeside town that has hosted an annual Queen fan camp for the past 32 years, organised by the Queen Fan Club Cultural Association – making the choice of location a natural one. More curious, however, is the observation that the sculpture bears a remarkable likeness to a celebrated Hungarian poet.

According to a report by Blikk, the project was realised as a joint venture between the association and the local council. Among the guests at the unveiling was Peter Freestone, Mercury’s former personal assistant. The rights to Mercury’s name and legacy, currently managed by Sony Music, were also formally cleared for the statue in an official letter.

“This is my second visit to this wonderful place, where I have once again been able to meet Hungarian Queen fans in person,” said Freestone, who spent 12 years as Mercury’s assistant, close friend and confidant. He first visited Hungary for an exhibition in Budapest. He added that he appreciated the artist’s decision to depict not the flamboyant performer on stage, but a more reflective and quietly brilliant figure.

This year will mark the 33rd Queen camp in Balatonszemes, commemorating both what would have been Mercury’s 80th birthday on 5 September 2026 and Queen’s legendary 1986 concert in Budapest.

As for the Hungarian poet many believe is echoed in the statue’s features, the answer is Attila József.

One thing, however, is certain: in 1986, Freddie Mercury even sang in Hungarian – and the footage still survives.

World.title: Revealed: How Russian intelligence recruits Hungarian youth – and gets away with it
World.content:
A third secretary of the Russian Embassy in Budapest believed to be serving as an agent of Russia’s SVR intelligence agency remains posted in Budapest, despite allegedly attempting to place at least one Hungarian young person into a senior government position in order to extract sensitive information for Moscow.

The case sheds light on how Russian services have sought to build their own espionage networks in Hungary, including during the years of Viktor Orbán’s governments — and how only weakly these efforts have been countered by the Hungarian state. Whether this will change remains an open question.

Russia did not relent under ‘friendly’ Orbán governments

Even after Russia’s attempted invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and throughout the protracted war that followed, successive Orbán governments have struck a conspicuously understanding tone towards Vladimir Putin’s regime. Officially, this has been justified by Hungary’s heavy reliance on Russian energy supplies, making the maintenance of cordial relations a matter of national interest.

Former PM Orbán last year in Moscow with President Putin. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

At times, government rhetoric has also hinted — albeit vaguely — that some of Putin’s criticisms of the West and its eastward expansion are not without merit.

Yet despite this relationship, widely viewed in Brussels as unusually close and politically costly within the EU, Russian intelligence activity in Hungary has not abated. One such operation appears to have failed rather spectacularly — though its alleged organiser continues to work undisturbed at the Russian embassy in Budapest.

The Russian embassy in Budapest’s city centre, near the Andrássy Avenue. Photo: FB/Russian embassy in Budapest

The case offers a stark warning to ambitious young Hungarians tempted by seemingly “irresistible” invitations to travel to Russia.

Talent-spotters target Hungarian youth

Russia’s efforts extend well beyond military force and drone warfare. The Kremlin continues to deploy soft power with intent, including language-study trips, cultural programmes, and international events such as the World Youth Festival held in Sochi in March 2024.

A Hungarian delegation attended the festival, led by Roland B., a Hungarian national living in Russia. Officially an entrepreneur, he is described by Telex as acting in a talent-spotting role — identifying individuals who could later prove useful to Russian intelligence.

It was at this event that Alexander V., the Budapest-based diplomat believed to be linked to the SVR, was introduced — via Roland B. — to a Hungarian applicant for a senior public administration post. The role required national security clearance. Although the candidate allegedly attempted, on instruction, to conceal his contact with Alexander V., the connection was uncovered, and he was denied the position.

Putin again suggests Hungary could regain territory from Ukraine: what he may have meant

Soft power operations continue unhindered

It remains unclear how many Hungarians — young or otherwise — have taken part in similar trips. Participants may find their digital devices accessed, their activities monitored, or themselves placed in compromising situations at informal social events, potentially rendering them vulnerable to coercion or recruitment.

Such gatherings often involve loosely structured programmes, where attendees cannot be certain whether they are speaking to fellow participants or intelligence operatives. According to Telex, even those who do not become agents may still serve a purpose: speaking positively about Russia online or acting as informal advocates for its interests.

Both B. Roland and Alexander V. remain active and are reportedly organising another major event in Yekaterinburg this September, which is again expected to attract numerous Hungarian participants. Roland B. refused to respond to Telex’s questions concerning the issue.

World.title: FM Anita Orbán received bipartisan US Congress delegation in the Hungarian Parliament – photos
World.content:
A bipartisan delegation from the United States Congress was received at the Hungarian Parliament on Monday by Foreign Minister Anita Orbán, with talks focusing on defence and economic cooperation.

In a post on her Facebook page, Orbán underscored that “Hungary and the United States are bound by a close alliance, shared values, and common strategic interests. The foundation of our cooperation lies in our NATO membership, our security partnership, and our strong economic and technological ties.”

The meeting, which was also attended by István Kapitány, Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy, and Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, Minister of Defence, centred primarily on strengthening defence cooperation, deepening partnership within NATO, and exploring opportunities to expand defence investment and economic links, the Foreign Minister said.

“Our aim is to ensure that the results of this cooperation not only reinforce relations between our two countries, but also bring tangible benefits to the Hungarian people — whether through more secure energy supplies, new investments and jobs, or advanced technological and defence collaboration,” Orbán concluded.

World.title: Another brutal heat dome arrives as Danube nears record low — what to expect this week
World.content:
A weak cold front on Monday will offer little in the way of relief, with searing heat set to return in the second half of the week. Barely has the previous heat dome passed than, according to HungaroMet, several days of peak temperatures between 33C and 38C are again on the cards. Meanwhile, a prolonged lack of rainfall could push the Danube in Budapest to historic lows, disrupting river traffic and deepening drought conditions across Hungary and much of Europe.

New heat dome to follow ‘dry cold front’

HungaroMet forecasts that a weak cold front will cross the country on Monday, bringing cloudier skies in the first half of the day, along with scattered light rain, showers or thunderstorms — mainly east of the Danube, later shifting to the north-east. North-westerly winds may strengthen widely, with gusts turning gale-force in the vicinity of storms. Daytime highs are expected to reach between 29C and 33C, MTI wrote.

Any respite, however, will be short-lived. By Tuesday, sunny spells with fair-weather cloud are expected, with only isolated showers possible in the east. Afternoon temperatures will range between 25C and 32C.

Another brutal heatwave approaches. Photo: Facebook/MÁV-csoport

From Wednesday onwards, clear and dry conditions will increasingly dominate. Highs of 28C to 34C are forecast for Wednesday, rising to 30C to 36C by Thursday. From Friday, a new heat dome is set to develop: temperatures could climb to between 33C and 38C on Friday and Saturday, with local readings of up to 39C possible by Sunday. Nights will bring diminishing relief, with minimum temperatures rising to between 17C and 24C by the weekend.

Danube in Budapest may fall to historic low

The prolonged dry spell is already being reflected in river levels. According to the National Hydrological Forecasting Service, the Danube at Budapest could fall to just 35 centimetres on Tuesday. Given a margin of error of plus or minus 7 centimetres, there is a realistic chance that the current record low could be broken.

The lowest level ever recorded in Budapest was 33 centimetres, measured on 25 October 2018 — though that record had already surpassed a benchmark that had stood since 1947.

The water level of the Danube in Budapest is extreme low. Photo: Facebook/Fővárosi Vízművek

Conditions are unlikely to improve in the near term. Little to no significant rainfall is expected across the Danube’s catchment area over the next six days, leaving scant hope for any meaningful rise in water levels. The low water has already caused serious disruption to shipping: both cargo and passenger vessels have been unable to proceed along several stretches of the river, while restrictions have been introduced in Budapest. Near Komárom, river cruise ships have recently been forced to queue, with passengers transferred to the capital by bus.

Persistently low water levels could, in the longer term, threaten drinking water supplies drawn from the Danube, although no such issues arose during the late-June heatwave, and Budapest Waterworks has issued reassuring statements on the matter.

If you missed: Hungary gripped by alarming drought as iconic lakes and rivers face unprecedented peril

Drought set to intensify

While Monday’s cold front may briefly temper the heat, it will do little to alleviate the lack of rainfall. High-pressure conditions are expected to reassert themselves thereafter, suppressing cloud formation and ensuring continued dry, sunny weather through the rest of the week, Portfólió wrote.

Hungarian agriculture must adapt to the changing weather conditions. Photo: depositphotos.com

Any showers that do develop on Monday will fall well short of replenishing parched soils. HungaroMet’s weekly precipitation anomaly map suggests that not only the Carpathian Basin but much of Europe is likely to receive below-average rainfall for this time of year. A particularly extensive dry zone is emerging across Central and Eastern Europe, pointing to a process on a continental scale.

All signs indicate that drought conditions will deepen in the coming days. The sustained rainfall deficit is placing increasing strain on vegetation, agriculture and water resources, with forecasts offering little indication of prolonged or substantial rainfall in the near future.

From 40°C to frost: Hungary records its coldest summer night as temperatures plunge below zero

World.title: How could a 14-year-old girl fall from the roof of a children’s home? Internal probe and police investigation began
World.content:
Local police are conducting an investigation and the institution has launched an internal probe into the case of a 14-year-old girl who fell from the roof of a children’s home in Pécs (Southwest Hungary) earlier this month, police and the Directorate General for Social Affairs and Child Protection (SZGYF) told MTI on Monday.

14-year-old girl on the roof of the children’s home

The incident was first reported by Telex.hu news portal on Sunday. The SZGYF said the girl was returned to the institution by police officers late on July 11 after she had been absent without permission for more than ten days. As it later turned out, the girl removed the screws securing the safety chains of the skylight of a kitchen and climbed out onto the roof of the building, MTI wrote.

By this time, a staff member of the children’s home had noticed the girl’s disappearance, but since she could not find her in the building, she asked for help from police officers. One of the residents reported seeing someone on the roof, prompting police to alert paramedics and begin a search of the surrounding area. It was during this sweep that they discovered a girl lying on the ground. She was treated at the scene before being taken to hospital, while officers carried out an on-site investigation.

According to the Directorate-General, an internal inquiry into the circumstances remains under way. The Baranya County Police Headquarters told MTI that the Pécs Police Department is examining the case במסגרת criminal proceedings.

The Directorate-General noted that standard upper-floor windows at the home had already been secured against opening prior to the incident. The girl was able to escape only after breaking a safety chain. As an immediate measure, a non-removable fixing has now been installed on the window, while a specialist will implement a permanent solution using a bespoke fastening method.

Systematic problems

Officials also pointed to “serious systemic issues” raised by the case. When police returned the girl to the children’s home that evening, a single night-duty supervisor was responsible for ten children. The institution, they stressed, can only employ a qualified educator alongside supervisory staff during daytime hours.

For years, the system has struggled with single-person night shifts. The home currently has only limited, temporary scope to deploy two staff overnight in severe crisis situations as an exceptional measure.

Magyar government reveals historic modernisation programme of Budapest’s suburban railway system

Further difficulties stem from the increasingly acute mental health conditions of children entering care. A shortage of specialists, inadequate pay, and the regular aggression directed at staff by residents all place significant strain on daily operations, the statement said.

This is compounded by a severe lack of places, particularly for children with special needs, alongside a growing administrative burden and increasingly complex bureaucratic procedures, the Directorate-General added in its response to MTI.

World.title: Turning point in the polls: Orbán may welcome latest survey — are voters really punishing Péter Magyar?
World.content:
The latest survey by the independent pollster Medián — which accurately forecast April’s election result and has an excellent record in predicting previous parliamentary contests — suggests that the Tisza Party’s months-long surge has stalled. Although it remains by far the most popular political force, its support has fallen by several percentage points compared with June, while both Fidesz and the far-Right Mi Hazánk have edged upwards. The research also indicates that Péter Magyar’s nomination of Judit Polgár for the presidency — made without the promised public consultation — amounted to a serious political misstep.

Tisza’s rise falters

The upward trajectory of the Tisza Party’s popularity appears to have broken. According to Medián’s poll, conducted between July 22 and 24 for HVG, support for the party has slipped by 3–5 percentage points since June.

At present, 57 per cent of the overall population would back Tisza in a hypothetical near-term election, while among decided voters the figure stands at 66 per cent. Although this remains significantly higher than the party’s mid-April rating — and far exceeds the best result ever recorded by Fidesz — the decline from late June is unmistakable.

PM Péter Magyar yesterday at the Hungaroring. Photo: MTI

That said, with support at such extraordinary levels, some degree of correction was arguably inevitable. Under Hungary’s electoral system, it remains notable that Tisza would still secure a two-thirds majority among committed voters even in a purely list-based vote. Medián emphasised that no clear causal link can be established between the dip in support and the so-called “Polgár affair”.

Fidesz and Mi Hazánk gain ground

As Tisza’s support softened, Fidesz registered a modest uptick within the margin of error. The governing party would attract 19 per cent of the total population, 22 per cent of decided voters and 23 per cent of committed voters — slight increases across all categories compared with the previous month.

Former prime minister Viktor Orbán with Fidesz MP Zsolt Németh during the 35th Bálványos Summer University and Students’ Camp last weekend in Transylvania. Photo: MTI/Veres Nándor

Mi Hazánk also improved its standing: 7 per cent of the total population and 9 per cent of decided voters would support the party. The survey further suggests that relatively few voters remain undecided.

Analyst: honeymoon over

Political analyst Gábor Török wrote that the data now support the view that the Tisza government’s “honeymoon period” has come to an end, and that Péter Magyar’s nomination of Judit Polgár was a political error. At the same time, he cautioned that the downturn is hardly surprising: Tisza’s lead remains unprecedented, and levels of support for Fidesz-KDNP are still historically high.

Péter Magyar with his voters prior to the April elections. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

In an earlier post, Török shared a trend line charting Fidesz’s support between 2010 and 2014 — the first term of its two-thirds majority — suggesting it may prove instructive to compare this with Tisza’s trajectory. Even now, he argued, two data points and a discernible trend line can already be identified.

This bothered voters about Péter Magyar’s process

The poll was conducted at a time when public debate was dominated by the resignation of President Tamás Sulyok and Péter Magyar’s ultimately unsuccessful attempt to nominate Judit Polgár for the presidency. According to Medián, 97 per cent of adults were aware that a new president must be elected, and 94 per cent had heard Polgár’s name mentioned in connection with the post.

Yet only one-third of respondents considered the chess grandmaster a suitable candidate, while 42 per cent opposed the idea. Even among Tisza voters, fewer than half (43 per cent) viewed her as a good choice, and roughly a third were explicitly against her. The controversy, however, centred less on Polgár herself.

Judit Polgár with Arnold Schwarzenegger in Budapest playing chess. Forrás: Facebook/Polgár Judit hivatalos oldala

Two-thirds of respondents were troubled by the manner of the nomination: only hours before putting Polgár forward, Magyar had promised a public consultation, only to announce her candidacy abruptly. Even among Tisza supporters, 60 per cent criticised this approach, while just 22 per cent approved. Polgár ultimately declined the nomination, and Magyar later apologised, admitting he had been carried away and had made a communication error.

PM Magyar presents Hungarian Grand Prix trophy to Lando Norris after record-breaking race

Little enthusiasm for presidency

Medián also examined whom voters would prefer as head of state. When asked an open-ended question, however, 60 per cent of respondents could not name a candidate.

Former justice minister Péter Bárándy received the most spontaneous mentions, cited by 8 per cent of respondents. Ákos Hadházy, a former Momentum politician turned independent MP, was named by 6 per cent, while Péter Márki-Zay — the opposition’s 2022 prime ministerial candidate — was mentioned by 5 per cent.

Orbán changes tone at Tusványos: Fidesz recast its role as “resistance politics” shifts into gear

World.title: Extraordinary parliamentary session: new Constitutional Court member, crypto trade changes, EU funds
World.content:
Hungary’s two-day extraordinary parliamentary session is set to open on Monday with an address by the Prime Minister, as MPs prepare to elect a new Constitutional Court judge.

Parliament to elect new Constitutional Court judge

According to the draft agenda published on Parliament’s website, proceedings will begin at 1pm with pre-agenda statements, with Prime Minister Péter Magyar speaking first, the Hungarian news agency wrote

Following statements by parliamentary groups and the adoption of the agenda, MPs may—depending on nominations—elect a new member of the Constitutional Court to replace Csaba Hende, whose mandate has expired. The judge will be elected by secret ballot, requiring a two-thirds majority, for a nine-year term.

Members will also have one hour to question government ministers through interpellations, followed by a session of immediate questions and answers, and a further half-hour of oral questions.

PM Péter Magyar and FM Anita Orbán. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Anita

A final vote, postponed last week, on legislative amendments aimed at improving the competitiveness and efficiency of public transport—and establishing a national transport organiser and rolling stock management company—remains on the agenda.

Speaking at Thursday’s government briefing, PM Magyar said the delay was due to technical amendment proposals from the European Commission. On Monday, Parliament will resume debate on the report and amendments ahead of the final vote.

National Asset Recovery and Protection Office, crypto trade, EU funds

MPs will also consider committee reports and consolidated amendments on five additional proposals, including changes to legislation governing the management of weather-related and other natural risks affecting agricultural production. The amendment would allow advance payments under the agricultural damage mitigation scheme.

Lawmakers are due to debate a bill establishing the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office, intended to ensure that unlawful management of public assets does not go unpunished. The proposed body would be tasked with identifying, securing, preserving and recovering misappropriated public assets, as well as initiating the necessary administrative and judicial proceedings.

Putin again suggests Hungary could regain territory from Ukraine: what he may have meant

Two further proposals relate to Hungary’s Recovery and Resilience Plan. Amendments required to meet energy-related commitments would, among other measures, facilitate investment in wind power to increase the share of renewable energy in electricity generation.

A separate bill, concerning tax measures linked to the implementation of the recovery plan and certain government programmes, would abolish tax advantages for public-interest asset management foundations performing public functions, remove tax base allowances for heritage projects, scrap the special immigration tax, and eliminate both the municipal tax and the dog ownership levy.

Parliament will also debate a proposal to repeal certain provisions governing crypto-asset conversion services. The justification is that so-called validation services for crypto-asset exchanges are incompatible with European Union law, as they restrict competition and therefore undermine the functioning of the internal market.

If you missed: Magyar government unveils 12-point plan to save Lake Velence after water levels hit historic lows

World.title: Romanian authorities mull new dynamic excise duty mechanism to curb fuel prices
World.content:
The Economic Committee, part of Romania’s upper legislative chamber, adopted a favorable report for the draft law on measures to reduce fuel prices on Monday, July 27.

The bill must also receive the approval of the Senate plenary in order to continue its legislative process. If adopted, it will introduce, for the first time, a "dynamic excise duty" mechanism, under which the excise duty on fuel may be reduced by between 5% and 25%, depending on developments in pump prices.

The new version of the bill abandons the VAT reduction initially proposed and retains only the excise duty reduction mechanism, after the Ministry of Finance warned that a VAT cut would not have been compatible with European legislation and would have sent a negative signal to rating agencies.

Former energy minister Bogdan Ivan said the bill creates the legal framework for government intervention during crises on the fuel market through the progressive reduction of the excise duty on diesel.

"At the current pump price of diesel, we are talking about a reduction of RON 0.34 per liter of diesel. If we see an increase in international diesel and oil prices, the reduction could go to as much as RON 0.68, depending on the final price," Bogdan Ivan said, cited by Digi24.

According to him, the purpose of the measure is to keep the price of standard diesel around the threshold of RON 10 per liter, even in the event of further price increases on the international market. The measures are to be applied initially for a period of three months, with the possibility of extension by government decision.

In addition, the Ministry of Finance will be able to update the level of the excise duty once every two weeks, depending on developments in Brent and Platts international quotations.

"Dynamic excise duty means that, depending on the price increase, it can decrease by between 5% and 25%. It is a much more flexible option, which gives us the possibility to act during the three months following promulgation through a Government decision, and every two weeks the Ministry of Finance will analyze the level of the excise duty and take action," interim finance minister Alexandru Nazare said.

He explained that the VAT reduction was dropped because the measure was not compatible with European legislation and would have affected the assessments Romania is expecting in the coming period from the rating agencies.

"We are expecting Fitch's report this week and Moody's report next week, and such announcements regarding VAT reductions would not have helped us at all in maintaining the rating," the minister added.

Nazare specified that the mechanism will be applied for a period of three months, with the possibility of extension, and that the budgetary impact is estimated at approximately RON 100 million per month, depending on price developments. At the same time, he warned that any price-capping measure also involves supply risks, which is why the authorities are in permanent contact with operators in the sector.

World.title: France’s Reed Capital acquires high-precision metal components factory in central Romania
World.content:
French investment fund Reed Capital has acquired Walor Precision Turning, a manufacturer of high-precision metal components for the automotive industry that also operates a factory in Sfântu Gheorghe, central Romania.

Overall, the company has nearly 420 employees and three production facilities in France, Romania, and Mexico. The factory in Sfântu Gheorghe is one of the group's most important assets and supplies major automotive manufacturers, producing high-precision components for airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. According to the company, its products are found in nearly one out of every two cars sold worldwide.

The Romanian subsidiary ended 2025 with a turnover of RON 207.3 million (approximately EUR 40 million), up from RON 202.6 million in 2024. The company returned to profit, reporting a net result of nearly RON 8 million, after a loss of RON 2.8 million recorded the previous year, and had an average of 183 employees.

The acquisition follows the separation of Walor Precision Turning from Walor International, a company previously controlled by the German group Ferral United. Reed Capital said it will retain the current management team and finance investments to expand industrial capacity and diversify the portfolio.

In addition to production meant for the automotive industry, the company wants to expand more strongly into growing industrial markets. The strategy includes developing components for active and semi-active suspension systems, solenoid valves, and, above all, cooling solutions for data centers, a segment driven by massive investments in artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure.

At the same time, Reed Capital intends to accelerate the company's development in Asia, with a focus on the Chinese market.

"Our ambition is to accelerate the company's diversification toward new industrial applications, particularly cooling solutions for data centers, while at the same time strengthening its international presence, especially in Asia," said Renaud Delaage, managing partner of Reed Capital.

World.title: Western Romania: Music, culture and sports at Timișoara City Celebration this weekend
World.content:
Timișoara is gearing up for four days of concerts, cultural experiences, sports, heritage and community activities as it holds its City Celebration from July 31 to August 3.

The celebration will bring 203 free events held in the Civic Park, I.C. Brătianu Park and Boulevard, the Uszoda area, Nicolae Titulescu Riverside Promenade, Victory Square and more than 30 other venues throughout the city, the organizers said.

Held under the theme "One city. A thousand ways to experience it," this year's edition “celebrates the communities, cultures, generations and forms of expression that shape contemporary Timișoara.” The music program will bring American singer-songwriter Beth Hart, Irish band The Script, and Serbian singer Marija Šerifović, a 2007 Eurovision winner, to the city.

Alongside the international headliners, the program will feature established local artists and emerging performers from Romania and the Republic of Moldova, including Irina Rimes, Satoshi, Dora Gaitanovici, Alexandra Căpitănescu, JazzyBIT & K-lu by Monica Anghel, Nico, Daniel Iordăchioaie, the folk ensemble Ansamblul Timișul, and Andreea Voica, Alexandru Brădățan, Aurora, and Săndel Mihai.

Timișoara City Celebration will also bring together artists, festivals, and organizations active in the city throughout the year. In the Civic Park and I.C. Brătianu Park, Psihodrom, Muzicon Hub, Time to Rock by FITT, CODRU, Guilty Corner, AnonimTM, Embargo Hub and JAZZx will host concerts, showcases and community-focused events.

From July 31 to August 2, the Uszoda area and the Nicolae Titulescu Riverside Promenade will become a hub for outdoor sports and recreation, featuring competitions, demonstrations and activities for all ages. The program includes 3x3 basketball, rugby and handball tournaments, skateboarding, BMX and scooter competitions, and other activities.

On the evenings of August 1 and August 2, the city’s Victory Square will host Meraviglia | Dancing Fountains, Flames and Aerial Acrobatics, a production combining water, fire, light, music, video projections and aerial performance.

World.title: Car rental company Autonom lists bonds worth EUR 30 mln on Bucharest Stock Exchange
World.content:
Autonom, one of the largest independent Romanian companies in the mobility solutions market, listed its third sustainability-linked bond issue, worth a total of EUR 30 million, on the Main Market of the Bucharest Stock Exchange, or BVB, on Monday, July 27.

The bond issue listed under the ticker AUT31E is made up of 300 bonds with a nominal value of EUR 100,000 each, with a fixed interest rate of 5.97% payable annually. The bonds, set to mature in 2031, are unsecured. Nine institutional investors subscribed to the bond offer.

The funds will be used to achieve the sustainability objectives set out in the company's development strategy.

The bond issuance is structured under the Sustainability-Linked Financing Framework, as the company continues to integrate ESG criteria into its growth strategy. Key ESG performance indicators tracked by Autonom include carbon emissions reduction and gender equality performance. The company aims to reduce the average carbon emissions of its operational passenger car fleet by 30% by 2028 and by 55% by 2030. Moreover, it aims to increase the share of women in management positions to 46% by 2030.

“The fact that the offer was oversubscribed highlights the growing investor interest in sustainable businesses. I congratulate the Autonom team for the consistency and clarity with which they pursue their goals. BVB remains a long-term partner and a steadfast supporter of the company's evolution," stated Remus Vulpescu, CEO of the Bucharest Stock Exchange.

“This new listing confirms that a Romanian entrepreneurial company can repeatedly rely on the capital market to meet its financing needs and integrate sustainability targets into its growth strategy. We would like to thank our investors for their trust and all the partners involved in this new successful listing,” stated Marius and Dan Ștefan, Co-Founders of Autonom.

The listing of the bond issue was carried out with the support of the consortium consisting of BRD – Groupe Société Générale, Banca Comercială Română, BT Capital Partners, Raiffeisen Bank, and UniCredit Bank as Co-Arrangers. Additionally, BRD – Groupe Société Générale represented Autonom for the admission to trading of the AUT31E bonds on the BVB Regulated Market.

Since 2021, Autonom has listed three consecutive sustainability-linked bond issues. The previous bond, AUT26E, valued at EUR 48 million and listed in 202, remains to this day the largest bond issuance by a Romanian entrepreneurial company on the local capital market, maturing in November this year. The third issuance, AUT29E, worth EUR 30 million, will mature in 2029. Before these listings, in 2019, Autonom listed its first bond issue, AUT24E, worth EUR 20 million, which was fully redeemed at maturity.

Autonom is a company with 100% Romanian capital, started in 2006 in Piatra Neamț, and is a top 3 player, by turnover, in the main sectors of activity: operational leasing and car rentals. The company offers modern mobility and financing solutions, including short- and medium-term rentals, operational leasing, chauffeur-driven transfers, temporary fleet rentals, fleet management services, roadside assistance, car wash services, and equipment rentals.

World.title: Head of Romania’s Department for Emergency Situations says prosecutor abused powers in alleged fictitious employment case
World.content:
The head of Romania's Department for Emergency Situations (DSU), Raed Arafat, claimed in a video posted on Facebook that the case concerning fictitious employment contracts at the institution he heads was fabricated.

The DSU head said that official checks "confirmed that the prosecutor artificially established jurisdiction in the case by invoking a fabricated factual circumstance." The discovery “dismantles the foundation on which the entire case was built,” Arafat argued.

According to him, based on these "artificial premises," the prosecutor conducted investigations for more than a year without the targeted persons being informed and without them being able to exercise their procedural rights.

At the same time, Arafat added, "the same allegations" were used to obtain "authorization for technical surveillance measures with the highest degree of intrusion." The surveillance lasted 5 months.

"The escalation of the measures did not stop there. The prosecutor also requested authorization for house searches against the investigated persons. However, the judge at the Court of Appeal found these requests to be manifestly disproportionate and rejected them. Instead of accepting the legality review exercised by the court, the prosecutor ordered the forcible seizure of the mobile phones belonging to all 13 targeted persons, obtaining by another route what the court had refused to authorize," Arafat explained.

The DSU chief said that considerable human, logistical, and financial resources were consumed to support a case built on fabricated premises, instead of being directed toward combating real criminal acts.

On March 27, prosecutors conducted searches at the headquarters of the Department for Emergency Situations (DSU) in a case reportedly involving fictitious employment. Subsequently, Raed Arafat "categorically" denied the existence of any possible fictitious employment of doctors within the institution and announced that he had cooperated and would continue to cooperate with investigators.

According to Arafat, the case concerns four doctors and one nurse, all "with extensive experience," employed part-time at the DSU, whom the prosecutor claims were paid without performing the work for which they had been hired. To counter the claims, DSU representatives sent the Military Prosecutor's Office "44 binders containing 20,000 pages demonstrating that the attendance records showed they worked both remotely and physically," and nearly 8,000 pages demonstrating that the people delivered materials, that they worked, and communicated by email, including at midnight."

"In no way can we speak of fraud or fictitious work, as has been claimed," Arafat also said.

Arafat is also included in another case handled by the military section of the National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) in connection with the 2017 purchase of a helicopter for EUR 4 million, for which VAT allegedly had not been paid. The alleged damage is estimated at approximately EUR 1 million. The DSU head denied any wrongdoing.

World.title: Mortgage-financed home purchases account for over half of Romania's residential transactions
World.content:
More than half of Romania's residential property transactions are now financed through mortgage loans, with the share rising significantly over the past four years, according to an analysis by online mortgage broker Ipotecare.ro based on official data. Nationally, mortgage-backed purchases accounted for just over 57% of residential transactions in the first half of 2026.

In the Bucharest-Ilfov region, mortgages represented almost 59% of residential sales in the first six months of 2026, down slightly from nearly 63% in the same period of 2025, but well above the 50% recorded in 2022, according to calculations based on data from the National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (ANCPI).

At the national level, the share of residential transactions completed through mortgage financing remained broadly unchanged from last year at just over 57%, compared with 43.5% in 2022, reflecting a stronger increase than in the Bucharest-Ilfov region.

According to the analysis, the nationwide increase in mortgage-financed purchases has coincided with rising home prices in recent years, making it more difficult for buyers to accumulate the funds needed for cash purchases.

The broker also noted that the number of registered mortgages includes refinancing loans. However, refinancings represented only 16% of the loans brokered by Ipotecare.ro this year, with the remaining 84% used to finance home purchases.

“The share of residential transactions completed through mortgage lending has increased and will continue to grow as young people from Generation Z become the main active economic force in the property market. […] The steady fall in mortgage interest rates and the launch of attractive products have also increased interest in mortgage lending," said Laurențiu Bogdan, managing partner at Ipotecare.ro.

The number of homes sold in Bucharest and Ilfov in the first half of 2026 was 1.4% lower than in the same period of last year, while residential sales nationwide declined by nearly 9%, according to ANCPI data.

World.title: Central Romania: Bear chased for two hours through Sibiu’s central neighborhoods
World.content:
A bear was tranquilized and captured by specialized teams on Monday, July 27, after a two-hour chase through central areas of the city of Sibiu. The animal and intervention teams ran through several neighborhoods until the former was cornered, according to local news outlet Turnul Sfatului.

The first alert regarding the presence of the bear was issued at 4:55 AM, when a 112 emergency call reported the presence of the wild animal on General Vasile Milea Boulevard. The authorities immediately issued a warning message, recommending that residents remain indoors and avoid any contact with the animal.

The bear quickly crossed the central area and headed toward the Hipodrom neighborhood. Around 05:20 AM, it entered the courtyard of the "Andrei Șaguna" Pedagogical College. For more than an hour, the animal was monitored by Gendarmerie and SMURD crews while it desperately tried to find a way out, even attempting to dig under the school's fence.

Although a hunter was also present at the scene, prepared to neutralize the bear by shooting it if public safety had been directly threatened, the authorities decided to first attempt immobilization by tranquilization. After several attempts, the intervention team managed to secure the area and administer the tranquilizer.

At 06:45 AM, Sibiu City Hall announced that the mission had been completed, with the animal immobilized without any casualties or major material damage. The bear will be relocated to a mountain area.

Romania is home to a large population of brown bears. According to preliminary results from an April 2025 study by the Ministry of Environment, the country’s brown bear population is estimated at between 10,419 and 12,770 animals. In this context, bear sightings are not uncommon in mountain areas in Romania, even near major cities.

World.title: Romanian worker dies after being struck by beam at Barcelona’s Camp Nou stadium
World.content:
A Romanian worker died after being struck in the head by a beam while carrying out painting work on a platform at the construction site of Barcelona's famed stadium Camp Nou.

Rescue crews confirmed the death of the 54-year-old man. His death was the first fatality registered at Camp Nou, Barcelona's legendary stadium, which has been undergoing modernization works since 2023. An investigation has been opened after the death.

"FC Barcelona deeply regrets the death of the worker who lost his life yesterday in the workplace accident that occurred during the renovation works at Spotify Camp Nou. The Club wishes to express its deepest condolences and extend its heartfelt support to his family, friends, and colleagues. FC Barcelona President Joan Laporta wishes to personally convey his condolences to the family and places himself at their disposal on behalf of the entire Club," the Catalan club said in a statement posted on X.

The Camp Nou construction site is staffed mainly by Romanian and Albanian workers, according to sources cited by TVRInfo.

Set to be fully renovated by 2028, the stadium already hosts matches by Barcelona’s world-famous football team. Once complete, the stadium will be able to accommodate more than 100,000 spectators in the stands.

World.title: What’s Driving the Real-Estate Price Surges in Eastern and South-East Europe?
World.content:
Rapidly rising real estate prices to the east and south of the Trieste-Szczecin line made existing dwelling owners happy - but potential buyers, especially younger people, less so.

According to Eurostat, in the first quarter of 2026, property prices in Bulgaria, Slovakia, and Croatia recorded price growth of 14 per cent over the first quarter of 2025. In a longer perspective of 3 and 10 years, the fortunes of individual countries have changed.

Generally, the total appreciation of housing real estate has been rapid, with Hungary in 10 years heading the list, followed by Bulgaria, Czechia, and Croatia.

However, Eurostat does not provide comparable data for countries southeast of Croatia, but Bosnia, Serbia, Montenegro, and others have followed similar paths. According to the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia, housing real estate prices increased by 20.4 per cent in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the first quarter of 2025. Nussubpekova recently reported a double-digit growth rate for Serbia.

World.title: North Macedonia Mourns Much-Loved Actor Goce Todorovski
World.content:
Goce Todorovski. Photo: Drama Theatre.

Actor Goce Todorovski has died aged 75, his family and the Drama Theatre in Skopje, where he spent most of his career, confirmed on Monday. The cause of death was not immediately announced.

Born in the western town of Kichevo in 1951, Todorovski graduated from the Faculty of Dramatic Arts in Skopje before joining the Drama Theatre in 1978. He went on to perform in more than 50 theatre productions, while also building a prolific career in television, radio and cinema.

His gift for comedy made him one of the country’s most enduring and popular actors.

For many Macedonians, Todorovski will be remembered above all for his appearances in the cult television series Macedonian Folk Tales (Makedonski Narodni Prikazni), whose humorous adaptations of traditional folklore became a fixture of family viewing for decades.

He was also a familiar face to generations of children through the educational television series “Scruffy Alphabet” (Bushava Azbuka), while radio audiences knew him from the long-running satirical comedy programme Hihiriku.

His film career included memorable roles in several classics of Macedonian and former Yugoslav cinema, including Happy New ’49 (Srekna Nova ’49), Weekend of the Dead (Vikend na Mrtovci), Trieste Via Skopje (Trst via Skopje), The Red Horse (Crveniot Konj), and many others.

Beyond his screen work, Todorovski was one of the leading comic actors of the Macedonian stage, collaborating with many of the country’s best-known theatre directors and helping shape the repertoire of the Drama Theatre for nearly five decades.

“Goce Todorovski never sought the audience’s affection. He won it from the moment he stepped onto the stage,” the Drama Theatre wrote in its farewell.

“His performances possessed a rare immediacy: a precise acting rhythm that seemed entirely effortless, expressive facial gestures, a distinctive stage presence, and the roguish charm with which he could effortlessly bridge the gap between the stage and the audience,” it said.

Todorovski’s performances earned numerous awards, including the state “23 October” prize for culture and the lifetime achievement award at the Vojdan Chernodrinski Theatre Festival in 2025, as well as the Presidential Order of Merit in 2023.

News of his death prompted an outpouring of tributes from fellow actors, public figures and audiences, many recalling the humour, warmth and distinctive characters that made Todorovski one of the defining faces of North Macedonia’s acting scene.

Actress Maja Andonovska Ilijevski wrote that Macedonian theatre had lost “a great man and a great actor”. Recalling their time filming the cult TV series Macedonian Folk Tales, she said Todorovski had been not only an acting legend but also a wonderful colleague, whose humour and warmth made those days unforgettable.

Andonovska said the countless characters Todorovski brought to life will remain part of the country’s collective memory, adding that “some people never truly leave – they live on through their roles, the memories of their colleagues and the love of their audience”.

Photographer Goran Anastasovski described Todorovski as “the man who made us laugh for decades” and “a giant on stage”, adding that his legacy of bringing smiles to various generations will endure.

World.title: The Digital Front of Albania’s ‘Flamingo Revolution’
World.content:
On May 30, protests broke out in Albania in response to a luxury development project in the Vjosa-Narta protected area, linked to investments backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, and a network of powerful local business interests and individuals with a history of legal troubles.

What began as an environmental protest grew into a movement known as the ‘Flamingo Revolution’, a reference to one of the many species of birds that inhabit the protected coastal area.

Alongside demands for environmental protection and the preservation of biodiversity, the movement has evolved into an expression of collective frustration with the status quo, calling for accountability, transparency, and political change.

Rejecting affiliation with the political forces that have dominated Albania’s political landscape for more than three decades, protesters have presented the movement as an independent civic initiative. For more than 50 days straight, they have called for the resignation of a prime minister and government they see as corrupt.

World.title: North Macedonia’s Judiciary ‘Nearing Collapse’, Rights Monitor Warns
World.content:
For Ivana Petkovska, the European Commission's latest rule-of-law report this month highlighted very familiar themes for North Macedonia – political pressure on the courts, insufficient funding and the limited impact of legal reforms.

The programme coordinator at the the All for Fair Trials Coalition, a leading judicial monitoring organisation in North Macedonia, said the report reinforces what watchdogs like hers have been saying for years.

“It is not the first time that international reports have concluded that the judiciary is facing political pressure from the executive or legislative branches,” Petkovska says.

As well as political interference, funding and staffing shortages are rendering the justice system dysfunctional, with the public ultimately paying the price through delayed verdicts and growing legal costs, she argues.

World.title: Child Maintenance Systems Failing Single Mothers in the Balkans and Beyond
World.content:
“According to the French census of 2020, 76 per cent of children under 18 live mostly with their mother, 12 per cent live alternately with each of their parents [shared physical custody], 12 per cent live mostly with their father,” said Emilie Biland, a professor of sociology at Sciences Po in Paris.

The burden of raising children, which falls mainly on the mother after a divorce, contributes to a fall in her standard of living, Biland told BIRN.

“In the year following a separation, half of the mothers who have physical custody of their child(ren) experience a decline in their standard of living of at least 20 per cent,” she said in a written reply. On average, children also experience a decline in living standards of 15 per cent in the year following the separation or divorce of their parents.

In France, child maintenance orders are not automatic. Parents have to claim them.

“Claiming for child support is an administrative burden for mothers,” said Biland. “Some of them may abandon their claim, either because they find the process too time-consuming and uncertain, or because it risks poisoning relations with the father.”

Because of this, France has one of the lowest rates of child maintenance payments in the EU, according to Biland’s research.

“To avoid non-take up, procedures to get child support should be lightened,” she told BIRN. “For example, it could be calculated as soon as a parent comes to the family benefit office to declare he or she does not live with the other parent.”

Tax rules for child support, as well as rules regarding social benefits, should be reformed, Biland said.

“So far, French parents receiving child support amounts have to pay income tax on them [they can lose some social benefits too], while parents paying for child support will pay fewer amounts of tax income.”

In France, the family support allowance, or ASF, provides financial assistance when one or both parents are not contributing to the cost of a child’s upbringing or when court-ordered child maintenance payments are too low.

In 2023, a quarter of children in single-parent families received the allowance, said Biland, adding that “1.4 million children are beneficiaries of ASF, which is more than the number of children who get child support payments overall”.

“It should be kept in mind that only single parents can receive it: mothers who move in with a new partner are no longer eligible for ASF payments,” Biland added. “Child support payments [from the second parent] do not stop when the parent is repartnering, of course.”

A French mother of two said she sees the state fund as her only hope of child support.

“The father should also have contributed by paying child support, but he didn’t,” the mother said in answers to the BIRN questionnaire. “You have to go through the court, and irresponsible fathers avoid it. We, mothers, are the ones who are penalised. Only the state provides help.”

Yet even a court order is not always enough to ensure that a parent comply with their obligations.

“At the hearing, the Family Court Judge ordered the child support to be paid retroactively, but the other parent still has not paid the retroactive amount, even after two years,” said another French mother, who said she waited a full year between filing her application and appearing before the judge.

*Some names in this article have been changed to protect the anonymity and safety of the individuals involved.

Additional reporting for this article was contributed by Ombeline Duprat in Sarajevo.

World.title: Serbian Flag on Cocaine Haul from Ecuador is a Clue – Not Proof
World.content:
On July 21, the Italian authorities seized 650 packages with more than 770 kilograms of cocaine at the port of Vado Ligure. The drugs were hidden among pallets of bananas in a refrigerated container from Ecuador.

Concealing cocaine in commercial shipments of fresh fruit, particularly bananas from Ecuador, is a well-known method used by criminal actors, including groups from the Balkans.

The Vado Ligure seizure, therefore, fits a broader pattern of maritime cocaine trafficking into Europe.

In Serbia, however, it wasn’t the size of the seizure or its route that attracted most attention but the Serbian flag displayed on some of the packages.

Although the comments posted under the media reports offer only a snapshot of public opinion, they reveal two recurring reactions.

World.title: Law and Justice Suffers Split Ahead of Poland’s 2027 Election
World.content:
Following a months-long power struggle, more than 30 MPs – including former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki – are set to be expelled from the Law and Justice party, in the biggest rupture seen on the Polish right in many years.

Law and Justice, or PiS, is Poland’s largest opposition party and one of the country’s two dominant political forces, alongside the governing Civic Coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The split could sharply reduce PiS’s chances of returning to power in next year’s parliamentary election.

On early Friday afternoon, PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski announced that “around 30-something” of the party’s 186 MPs had effectively chosen to leave after refusing to sign declarations of loyalty. The documents required them to state that they did not belong to any political associations operating within the party – an obvious reference to Development Plus (Rozwoj Plus), an organisation created by Morawiecki, until now one of PiS’s deputy leaders.

“Everyone knew what they were supposed to sign, and knew the consequences of not signing,” Kaczynski said. “And so they made the decision they did.”

Kaczynski has been PiS’s undisputed leader and chief power broker for more than two decades, selecting loyal candidates for prime minister who largely continued to defer to him once in office. Morawiecki was initially one of them, serving as prime minister between 2017 and 2023.

But in recent years, Morawiecki – an economist, former banker and comparatively moderate conservative – has grown increasingly impatient with Kaczynski’s dominance. He has pushed for changes to both the party’s internal structure and its political program, arguing that PiS was failing to speak convincingly to younger voters and entrepreneurs.

Friday’s rupture was the culmination of months of increasingly open conflict.

“Until the very last moment, we fought for the unity of the Law and Justice camp,” Morawiecki said at a press conference. “We could not accept being forced to sign a loyalty pledge.”

He accused the party leadership of using ultimatums and political blackmail to discard a strategy that had been agreed only recently.

Morawiecki did not formally announce the creation of a new party. He did, however, declare the beginning of “a new chapter in Poland’s political history”, promise a major nationwide tour and announce that his camp would soon present a new political program.

He said his political circle now included 40 MPs (which stands at odds with Kaczynski’s estimate), one senator and three members of the European Parliament, describing it as a “very strong representation”. Its offer, he said, would reach beyond PiS’s traditional base and target young people, entrepreneurs, local-government officials and even some voters currently supporting the governing coalition.

Morawiecki presented his project as a modern, patriotic and pro-state conservative force, capable of responding to social and economic change without falling back on outdated ideas.

The electoral consequences could be enormous. An Opinia24 poll conducted before the split tested precisely such a scenario. With PiS united, the party would receive 23 per cent of the vote, behind Civic Coalition on 31.6 per cent. When respondents were offered a separate Morawiecki-led Rozwoj Plus list, support for PiS fell to 17.7 per cent, while Morawiecki’s group received 6.2 per cent. Civic Coalition remained clearly ahead on 30.9 per cent.

Tusk responded with a single cutting line: “They are fighting so hard for party unity that there won’t be one stone left standing.”

Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski was blunter: “Kaczynski went all in and lost.”

World.title: Croatia Braces for Another Heatwave as Temperatures Could Reach 40°C
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – Following a brief but very welcome period of cooler, fresher and somewhat unstable weather, Croatia is set to face another heatwave with temperatures likely to reach 40 degrees.

After a brief spell of unsettled and sometimes stormy weather, Croatia is preparing for another intense heatwave, with temperatures expected to climb steadily throughout the week and potentially reach 40°C in some inland areas. Index reports that meteorologists are claiming that the hottest conditions are likely to arrive during the second half of the week.

above 35 degrees by the end of the week

Weather conditions are expected to stabilise on Tuesday and onwards. Daytime temperatures will rise each day, with much of the country seeing highs above 35°C by the end of the week. Forecasters say isolated locations could even record temperatures of around 40°C if current forecasts hold.

The Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ) has already issued an initial yellow heat warning for Thursday, cautioning that the heat could pose a risk to human health. Meteorologists warn that higher-level warnings may be introduced if temperatures continue to increase as expected.

The upcoming heatwave follows an unusual period of unstable weather that brought thunderstorms, strong winds and a series of strange meteotsunamis along parts of the Adriatic coast. Once the current weather system moves away, a strengthening area of high pressure is expected to bring prolonged sunshine and very little rainfall.

records were broken in june

Forecasters also pointed to this summer’s exceptional conditions. During June, fourteen of Croatia’s 35 main meteorological stations recorded new monthly temperature records, while Split reached an all-time record of 40°C at the Marjan weather station. Staggeringly, even sea temperatures climbed to around 30°C in some areas, highlighting the intensity of this year’s hot summer season.

Authorities are advising residents and visitors to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to the sun during the hottest part of the day and keep a close eye on vulnerable groups, including the elderly, young children and those with existing health conditions, as Croatia prepares for another spell of extreme summer heat.

World.title: Sea Floods Stari Grad on Hvar for the Third Time in Just 10 Days
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – The sea has created floods in Stari Grad on the island of Hvar for the third time in just 10 days due to repeated meteotsunamis.

Index reports that visitors and residents of Stari Grad on the island of Hvar have once again found themselves dealing with flooded streets after the sea overflowed onto the town’s waterfront, marking the third such event in just ten days. The repeated flooding has drawn attention to increasingly unusual sea level fluctuations affecting parts of Croatia’s coastline and islands.

Videos shared by residents showed seawater spilling over the promenade and into the historic centre, covering streets and public spaces before gradually receding. Although the flooding caused disruption, there were no reports of serious injuries or major structural damage.

According to meteorologists, the flooding was not caused by rainfall but by a combination of low atmospheric pressure, strong southerly winds and elevated sea levels. These conditions created what is known as a storm surge, pushing large volumes of seawater onto the shoreline and into low-lying coastal areas.

The phenomenon has affected Stari Grad several times over the past two weeks, with each event occurring under similar weather conditions. Locals say the repeated flooding has become a growing concern, particularly for businesses and residents along the waterfront who have had to repeatedly clear seawater from their properties.

Experts note that enclosed bays and historic harbour towns such as Stari Grad are especially vulnerable to this type of coastal flooding. When strong winds coincide with low air pressure, sea levels can temporarily rise enough to overwhelm quays, promenades and streets built just above normal sea level.

As weather conditions improved, the seawater gradually retreated and life returned to normal. However, the latest flooding serves as another reminder of how quickly changing weather patterns can impact Croatia’s coastal communities, with residents hoping calmer conditions will prevent another repeat in the coming days.

World.title: Sveti Ivan Beach: The Hidden Paradise That Requires a 50-Minute Hike
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – The entire island of Cres is stunning, but Sveti Ivan beach takes it a step further. If we’re being honest, it takes it many steps further, as a 50-minute hike is needed to reach this hidden paradise. Trust us, it’s so worth it.

Hidden beneath the ancient hilltop village of Lubenice on the island of Cres lies one of Croatia’s most spectacular beaches, Sveti Ivan beach. Putni kofer reveals that it is best known for its white pebbles, crystal-clear waters and particularly dramatic surroundings. It is very often considered one of the most beautiful beaches on the Croatian coast (and that’s a challenging title to receive in itself).

The beach sits in a secluded bay beneath the historic settlement of Lubenice, which is perched high on a cliff overlooking the Adriatic. Surrounded by steep rocks and untouched nature, Sveti Ivan offers the kind of peaceful atmosphere that is becoming increasingly rare on the Croatian coast.

Part of what keeps this beach so special is also what makes it difficult to reach. Visitors who choose to walk from Lubenice must follow a steep trail that takes around 50 minutes downhill, and the return journey can be even more challenging, especially during the intense summer heat. Proper footwear and enough water are essential, and we’d go as far as to discourage anyone doing this during the height of summer.

Because of the demanding access, even during the height of summer Sveti Ivan usually avoids the large crowds found at many other Croatian beaches. Those who make the journey are rewarded with incredible views, peaceful surroundings and some of the clearest waters on the Adriatic.

The beach can also be reached by sea, either with a private boat, organised excursion or water taxi. Nearby is another natural attraction, Plava Grota, a sea cave where sunlight creates beautiful blue reflections inside the cave.

Above the beach sits Lubenice, one of the oldest settlements on the Croatian islands. Located on a 378-metre-high cliff, the village has a history stretching back more than 4,000 years, with archaeological remains from the Bronze and Iron Ages found in the surrounding area.

Once one of Cres’ most important settlements, Lubenice is now home to only two permanent residents. However, during the summer months, visitors arrive to explore its ancient stone streets, admire the views and discover one of Croatia’s most breathtaking beaches down below.

World.title: Should Croatia Charge Tourists Who Need Emergency Help After Excessive Drinking?
World.content:
July the 27th, 2026 – Should Croatia be charging tourists who take it too far and require emergency medical help after excessive drinking or even illicit drug use?

Every single summer, Split in particular faces the same old problem, and that is tourists being found unconscious on city streets after heavy nights of drinking, with emergency services called to help them. The issue has sparked a debate over whether people who put themselves in danger through excessive alcohol consumption should contribute to the cost of medical interventions.

over 50 calls because of alcohol in june alone

During June alone, the Split-Dalmatia County Emergency Medical Service recorded more than 50 calls related to alcohol intoxication. Lukrecija Zderic reveals for Index that medical teams treated 44 people, while eight people were no longer at the location when emergency crews arrived. Among those who received help were also two minors.

Many of these cases involve young foreign tourists visiting Split during the summer season. Locals say it has become common to find intoxicated visitors lying on streets in the early morning hours after nights out and organised pub crawl tours.

The question now being raised is whether tourists who end up needing emergency medical assistance because of extreme alcohol consumption should help cover the cost. Some European countries already charge part of the expense in similar situations, but Croatia currently does not have such a system.

an abuse of already thin resources

Croatia’s emergency services are required to help anyone whose health is at risk, regardless of how the situation happened. However, every intervention requires medical staff, vehicles and resources.

The Croatian Health Insurance Fund explained that emergency medical teams are funded through contracted healthcare costs. A single emergency team consisting of a doctor, nurse and driver represents a significant annual expense for the healthcare system.

For foreign visitors, the final bill depends on their insurance situation. Tourists from EU countries, the European Economic Area and Switzerland with valid European Health Insurance Cards have their costs covered through international healthcare agreements. Visitors from countries without such agreements may have to pay themselves unless they have travel insurance.

irresponsible behaviour should face consequences

However, if a tourist leaves Croatia without paying a medical bill, the unpaid cost can ultimately fall on Croatian public funds. This means taxpayers may end up covering expenses that were never recovered.The debate comes as Split continues to balance the benefits of being one of Croatia’s most popular tourist destinations with the challenges that come from large numbers of visitors, particularly during the peak summer months.

As tourism grows, Croatia faces an ongoing question: should irresponsible behaviour surrounding alcohol and drug use that requires emergency medical intervention come with a financial consequence?

World.title: Search Underway After Skipper Falls Overboard Near Šolta
World.content:
July the 26th, 2026 – A frantic search is currently underway after a skipper fell overboard into the sea not far from Šolta, marking the second serious maritime incident near the island in a short time.

Index reports that a major search and rescue operation is currently underway in the waters off the island of Šolta after a skipper fell overboard from a charter catamaran and disappeared within minutes amid extremely poor weather conditions. The incident was reported at around 09:10, triggering an immediate response from Croatia’s maritime rescue services.

According to the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure, the missing man is an Austrian skipper. At the time of the accident, the sea was being battered by strong winds and rough conditions, making the search particularly difficult.

A large-scale rescue effort was launched involving two rescue boats from the Milna Harbour Master’s Office, one rescue boat from Hvar, three vessels from the Split Maritime and Airport Police, a Pilatus aircraft, and later a helicopter to assist with the aerial search. Authorities also issued a PAN-PAN urgency message via Split Radio, asking all vessels in the area to keep watch for the missing skipper.

The remaining six passengers, all of whom are Austrian nationals, were located unharmed aboard the catamaran. A replacement skipper was transferred to the vessel so it could safely continue to its next destination, where the passengers would disembark.

As of the latest update, the search remains ongoing, with emergency services continuing to comb the waters around Šolta in the hope of finding the missing skipper. Authorities have not released further details while the operation continues.

World.title: Croatian Firefighting Pilots Battle Massive Wildfires in France
World.content:
July the 26th, 2026 – Croatian firefighting pilots are battling massive wildfires in France, which have caused unimaginable destruction in the southwest of the country.

Index reports that Croatian military firefighters are playing a key role in the fight against devastating wildfires sweeping southwestern France, where huge blazes continue to threaten communities near Bordeaux.

Members of the 855th Firefighting Squadron of the Croatian Air Force have been deployed to France as part of an international firefighting effort. They are currently operating in the Biscarrosse area, where large wildfires remain active and conditions continue to challenge emergency crews.

The Croatian crews arrived in France on the 24th of July. On their first day they were assigned to fires near Salernes, before being redeployed to the Bordeaux region as the situation worsened. During their first two days of operations, the crews completed 72 flights, logged a total of 13.5 flying hours, and dropped 402 tonnes of water on the enormous flames.

According to the Croatian Ministry of Defence, the mission remains highly demanding due to the scale of the fires and rapidly changing conditions on the ground. Major Tomislav Vranjić said the situation is still extremely complex, with Croatian pilots making every effort to support French firefighters in bringing the blazes under control.

The deployment comes as France battles one of its largest wildfire outbreaks in decades. The fires in the Gironde region have burned tens of thousands of hectares, forced the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people and prompted international assistance from across Europe.

Croatia’s Canadair crews are among Europe’s most experienced aerial firefighters, regularly assisting other countries through the European Union’s civil protection cooperation mechanisms. Their latest mission once again highlights Croatia’s expertise in tackling large-scale wildfires beyond its own borders.

World.title: Analysis of 1.6 Million Reviews Reveals What Tourists Think of Croatia
World.content:
July the 26th, 2026 – An analysis of a staggering 1.6 million reviews reveals precisely what tourists really think of Croatia in comparison to its competition.

Croatia has triumphantly emerged as the highest-rated major Mediterranean destination based on an analysis of more than 1.6 million online guest reviews, but the data also highlights several areas where the country is falling behind its competitors. This study, as reported by Ivan Ivankovic for Index, examined 1,622,218 reviews written by travellers themselves, offering a broad picture of how visitors perceive Croatia compared with other leading Mediterranean destinations.

greece is still leaving a stronger impression…

The overall results are encouraging. Croatia achieved an average rating of 8.91, narrowly edging out nearby Greece and comfortably outperforming Spain, neighbouring Italy and Turkey in overall guest satisfaction. However, when travellers who had visited both Croatia and Greece were asked which destination they preferred, 11 out of 12 nationalities chose Greece, suggesting that while visitors rate Croatia highly, Greece leaves a stronger overall impression.

One of Croatia’s biggest strengths is its location. Visitors consistently praise the country’s remarkable coastline, islands and natural beauty, while also giving high marks for cleanliness. The analysis found that Croatia is also viewed as one of the fairest destinations in the Mediterranean, with comparatively few complaints about scams, hidden charges or tourist traps.

croatia has the highest number of reviews calling it “too expensive”

The biggest criticism, however, is price. Croatia recorded the highest number of reviews mentioning that it is too expensive, with complaints focusing mainly on restaurants, drinks and other spending outside accommodation rather than hotel prices themselves. Among everyday purchases, tourists most often criticised the cost of bottled water, while cocktail prices were also seen as relatively high. Coffee prices, on the other hand, attracted fewer complaints.

The research also identified several recurring frustrations. Guests most frequently complained about parking, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, noise, cleanliness in some locations and showers or water facilities. Croatia also performed poorly when it came to cashless payments, with many visitors noting that some businesses still accept only cash, which represents a growing inconvenience for international travellers.

croatia performs better outside of the main summer season

Another notable finding is that Croatia receives better reviews during the pre-season and post-season than at the height of summer. This suggests that overcrowding and peak-season prices continue to affect the visitor experience during the busiest months.

The analysis paints a nuanced picture of Croatian tourism as a whole. Visitors continue to love the country’s scenery, safety and overall quality, making it one of the Mediterranean’s top-rated destinations. However, if Croatia wants to remain competitive against rivals such as Greece, the findings suggest it will need to address concerns over pricing, infrastructure and service during the busiest part of the tourist season.

World.title: The Green Cave: One of the Vis Archipelago’s Most Magical Wonders
World.content:
July the 26th, 2026 – The Green Cave is one of the beautiful Vis archipelago’s most incredible natural wonders, and instead of being limited to viewing it by boat, you can swim inside it.

Just off the southern coast of the far-flung island of Vis, the tiny, uninhabited islet of Ravnik is home to one of Croatia’s most spectacular natural attractions, the remarkable Green Cave (Zelena špilja). Putni kofer reveals that unlike very many sea caves in Croatia and indeed elsewhere that can only be admired from a boat, this one offers visitors the rare opportunity to swim inside and experience its unique beauty up close and personal.

This unusual cave gets its name from the remarkable emerald-green glow that fills the interior. Sunlight enters through a circular opening in the cave’s ceiling and reflects off the seabed, which is covered with various types of green algae. Around midday, when the sun is at its highest, the effect is at its most dramatic, bathing the water in an almost unreal green light. Unlike the famous Blue Cave on nearby Biševo, the Green Cave has two large entrances, allowing smaller boats to sail directly inside. Visitors can also jump into the crystal-clear sea and swim beneath the beam of sunlight that shines through the roof, creating one of the Adriatic’s most memorable swimming experiences.

The cave has been protected as a geomorphological natural monument since 1967, while the islet of Ravnik itself is a protected significant landscape. Over the years, the cave has inspired countless visitors, including Emperor Franz Joseph I, who is said to have visited during his tour of the Adriatic back during the 19th century and who was left thoroughly enchanted by it. During World War II, local stories suggest that its spacious interior even provided secretive shelter for small military vessels.

Most visitors reach the Green Cave as part of a boat excursion departing from Vis, Komiža or Hvar, often combined with stops at the Blue Cave, Stiniva Cove and other highlights of the Vis archipelago. Entry is managed under a concession system, with visitors paying a small admission fee before entering or swimming inside the cave.

Although the Blue Cave often attracts the bigger crowds and is definitely much better known globally, many travellers consider the Green Cave an equally unforgettable experience. Its combination of emerald light, clear Adriatic waters and the chance to swim inside a protected natural monument makes it one of the hidden gems of Croatia’s coastline.
