Tech.title: Fed Up With Lettuce Recalls, I Started Growing Greens in This Smart Garden
Tech.content:
The cyclospora outbreak affecting produce from Taylor Farms de Mexico has sickened over 1,600 people across five states, including Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia. It’s one in a long line of severe produce outbreaks, but this time, I’m reconsidering how I approach food safety, given that the greens meant to nourish us continue to pose contamination risks.

Over the last year and a half, I’ve used my Gardyn Studio, a hydroponic growing system, to grow my own produce in my small NYC apartment. I’ve harvested arugula, kale, lettuce, peppers, cucumbers, cherry tomatoes, herbs and edible flowers, even throughout the winter — and, more importantly, I’ve had full control over the safety of my produce.

What to know about the 2026 cyclospora outbreak

Cyclospora is transmitted through food and water contaminated with the parasite, with symptoms typically manifesting approximately 1 week after exposure, though cases can range from two to 14 days or longer. The 2026 numbers represent a significant increase from the 249 cases reported in the US during the same period last year.

According to The Cleveland Clinic, symptoms of cyclospora infection often include sudden watery stools and even explosive diarrhea. Other common symptoms include:

Stomach cramps

Bloating, increased gas and burping

Nausea

Unintentional weight loss

Loss of appetite

Extreme fatigue or weakness

While home-growing your produce doesn’t eliminate all food safety risks, it can eliminate the specific contamination risks present in mass industrial distribution systems and exposure to pesticides. Given these risks, many are looking for ways to bypass mass distribution entirely. This is why I started using the Gardyn Studio.

Nasha Addarich Martinez/CNET

Why I switched to the Gardyn Studio

The Gardyn Studio is a compact, 4.5-foot hydroponic tower with 16 growing slots, LED grow lights and a mobile app that manages your growing from start to finish. Having used it for over a year, I have a clear sense of its benefits and shortcomings.

I appreciate how self-sufficient the device is: You insert the pods, set the lighting schedule, add water and plant food, and refresh the tank every few weeks. Other than that, the plants pretty much grow on their own. Not every pod is a success, though. In every cycle, at least two pods fail to grow. While Gardyn will send replacement pods, you will need the Gardyn Nursery (a separate $80 device) to grow the sprouts before you can insert them into the Studio.

I’ve found the harvesting time to be quick. My arugula reaches maturity in about three to four weeks. The Kale takes about five weeks. In both cases, the taste and quality are unsurprisingly better than store-bought greens.

The Gardyn Studio costs $579 and is great for small spaces. If you have a larger home, you can also consider the Gardyn Home ($899), which fits 30 growing slots, compared to the 16 on the Studio.

There’s also an optional membership that costs between $25 and $39 a month or $259 a year, which includes monthly credits you can use to buy more plants and access to Kelby, the AI gardener that will automate watering cycles and lighting based on your specific plants’ life cycles and the local environment. It also sends push notifications to the Gardyn app to alert you when to add water, add plant food or harvest.

Last year, a CNET Survey found that US adults who shop for groceries waste an average of $125 a month on food that’s not cooked or eaten. That’s $1,500 a year. I rarely waste food grown in the Gardyn since I harvest it as needed, so I rarely end up with excess greens wilting away in the fridge.

Gardyn specs at a glance

Price $579 (hardware) Height 4.5 feet tall Floor Space 1.4 square feet Growing Capacity 16 plant pods simultaneously Technology LED grow lights, automated nutrient delivery via app Pod Pricing $1.99 to $4.99 (member pricing); $4.99 (non-member) Premium Pods Up to $9.98 Monthly Pod Credits 5, complimentary with membership (10 with Gardyn Home) Operating Cost Minimal electricity (comparable to a smart bulb) Warranty 2 years Membership $25 to $39 a month Trial 30 days

The pros and cons

While I use my Gardyn year-round, there are things to consider before committing to it. The upfront cost of $579 puts the Gardyn Studio in the same category as high-end kitchen appliances, but the benefits of growing my own produce at home and no longer having to buy it make it worth it to me.

Pros:

Eliminates contamination risks

Compact design that fits in small spaces

Minimal maintenance (no soil or gardening skills required)

Responsive customer service for pod replacements

Reduced pesticide exposure

Cons:

High upfront costs

Some pods fail to grow

Ongoing pod and nutrient costs

No ability to grow root vegetables

For those without access to hydroponic systems

Nasha Addarich Martínez/CNET

Growing your produce at home is still valuable, even at a smaller scale. Windowsill herb gardens require minimal equipment and investment. My first home garden was in a 10-inch planter, where I grew cilantro, basil and parsley, which I put on my windowsill.

Buying from local farms and building relationships with local farmers’ markets establishes direct supply chains from the source, without the middlemen (distribution centers). Inquiring about produce sourcing at your local supermarket creates incentives for transparency and regional cultivation. These approaches won’t prevent every outbreak, but they reduce dependence on centralized supply chains and create accountability between producers and consumers.

Food safety doesn’t (and shouldn’t) have to be a luxury. It does, however, require deliberate choices about where food originates and who controls its cultivation. The Gardyn Studio is one option among many, and the one that works for my lifestyle and home. What matters most is recognizing that alternatives to mass food systems exist.

Tech.title: Uh Oh: I Learned How to Make Air Fryer Fries Taste Exactly Like Deep-Fried
Tech.content:
Air fryer fries are already pretty great — but a few small steps takes them to peak form.

Pamela Vachon/CNET

Fries are the height of snack food and a big reason why the potato is America’s most popular vegetable. Fries are also the most common form of potato consumption when dining out or ordering in. Making fries at home has historically been a complex and messy affair, but the advent of the air fryer changed all that.

Air fryer fries are consistently good and a lot less trouble than managing a pot of boiling oil. That said, simply tossing a bag of frozen fries — even the best frozen fries — into the air fryer doesn’t quite measure up to the deep-fried version. Air-fried fries tend to come out drier, with an uneven crisp that’s more than edible but falls short of the golden, crackling shell you get when they’re submerged in hot fat.

7 Best Air Fryers, Out of 20 Tested See at CNET

For air fryer fries that taste like the real thing, a little technique and a few small treatments go a long way. Four easy steps close the gap between restaurant fries and the middling versions you’ve been making at home. No hot oil, no mess, no deep fryer babysitting — just really good fries that are admittedly a lot harder to explain away as the healthier version.

Air fryer fries that taste exactly like deep-fried

Ready to take air fryer fries up a notch? Pamela Vachon/CNET

The air fryer french fry hack involves four steps — don’t worry, they’re all easy — beyond air frying, that promise to transform frozen french fries into something actually resembling deep-fried fries: soaking them in water, shaking them to rough up the texture, parcooking them in the microwave (yes, really) and then dousing them with oil only after they’ve had a turn in the air fryer. None of these are especially intuitive, right? But all of these serve specific functions that improve on what the air fryer can do on its own.

In the age of TikTok, it can be hard to trace the origin of certain hacks, but the method was shared with me by Andreas Hansen, founder and CEO of Fritaire, whose tumbler-based model is especially ideal for this French fry preparation, since it both aids in the texturizing of the exterior of the fries and precludes the need to shake several times during air frying.

The Best Frozen Fries to Cook in an Air Fryer, Tested by CNET See at CNET

A little investigation revealed that Chef Joshua Weissman is frequently credited with bringing attention to the method, but even in his video he gives a shoutout to Chris Young, whose video predates Weissman’s by over a year, and who credits Heston Blumenthal for inspiring the “triple-cooked” method, and so on, and so on.

Regardless of the actual origin of this hack, I’m taking their collective wisdom and applying it to french fries, since the method was specifically developed for thick-cut fries, which, I’m sorry, are steak fries, and not at all the same thing.

What you need for perfect air fryer french fries

Here’s everything you need for the best air fryer fries of your life. Pamela Vachon/CNET

While a majority of what is needed here probably already exists among the various compartments of your kitchen, the supplies you’ll need to gather are:

Frozen french fries (I’m using straight cut, not thick/steak fries)

Large bowl with lid for shaking

Microwave-safe bowl

Microwave

Air fryer

Duck fat, goose fat or beef tallow for best flavor

Salt

Step 1: A quick soak

A quick soak removes excess starch from the frozen potatoes. Pamela Vachon/CNET

Completely counterintuitive to the idea of crunchy fries is the notion that you must first make them soggy, but that is indeed what is recommended.

Straight from the freezer, soak the fries in warm water for 30 seconds to remove some of the starch on their exterior. (30 seconds to 1 minute is recommended for thicker-cut fries.) This is phase one of the “roughing up” process that will eventually create small micro-pockets of additional surface area on the fries, allowing the air fryer to really get a good crisp going.

The goal here is to keep the interior of the fries frozen, so set a timer to prevent over-soaking.

Step 2: Shake vigorously

Yep, now we’re really going to rough up the fries. After draining the soaking water, shake fries vigorously for another 30 seconds or so. The fries should be soft enough just on the exterior to add some texture, but not fall apart entirely. If they do, you’ve soaked too hard in the first step.

The more little craters you can add to the surface of the fries, the more area there is for the air fryer’s air to circulate, giving an unparalleled crisp.

Step 3: Nuke for 5 minutes

Before we go for the big crunch, we’re softening the insides a little. Pamela Vachon/CNET

Before we actually get crunchy, though, things are going to get even softer first. Using a microwave-safe dish with a lid, par-cook the fries for 5 minutes. Since I was using thinner fries, I hedged my bets and went with 50 percent power, but still cooked for the full 5 minutes.

Both Weissman’s and Young’s videos use a plastic container for both soaking and shaking, but we know better than to do that. So long as we’re being extra with this french fry preparation, let’s switch out for a glass or ceramic container, OK?

This par-cooking stage steams the interior of the fries, allowing them to get a better deal than they usually do in the air fryer. If you’ve ever found air-fried fries to be hollow, this is the antidote. The unexpected bonus of this step is that microwaving the fries releases a satisfying french-fry aroma.

Unsurprising step: Following the microwave parcooking, proceed airfrying as normal by placing the fries in a shallow layer in the air fryer and cooking at 400 degrees Fahrenheit for about 12 to 15 minutes (longer for thicker fries), shaking once or twice during the process to ensure all surface areas have access to the circulating air. The goal is golden brown with edges just starting to brown, so that the fries are crispy but still pillowy soft on the inside.

Step 4: Season with cooking fat

Use a drizzle of duck fat to send your fries’ flavor soaring. Pamela Vachon/CNET

While certain items get a little dousing in fat before being cooked in the air fryer, here we’re just using cooking fat as a seasoning, allowing the already-crisped fries to absorb the oil for both texture and flavor.

But not just any fat. For best results — since you’ve gone this far, why not go all the way — look to rendered animal fat such as duck fat, goose fat or beef tallow for a rich flavor boost. Salt to your liking, and voilà: air fryer french fries that are actually kind of fried.

Hungry for more? Learn how to deep-clean your air fryer in three easy steps and see how much less energy it uses than a wall oven.

Tech.title: Peacock and YouTube to Bundle Up in 2027
Tech.content:
NBCUniversal and YouTube are continuing to grow their partnership with the rollout of a new streaming bundle that combines Peacock Premium and YouTube Premium. The package will be available to customers in the US in early 2027, NBCUniversal announced on Monday. Viewers can access Peacock content like Love Island USA, Law & Order, The Traitors and live sports from the NBA, NFL and more. As part of the media giants’ expanded deal, NBC will also livestream select sports events on YouTube through its NBC Sports channel.

With this collaboration, NBCU plans to push its international streaming services, Universal Plus and Hayu, to reach more YouTube Premium subscribers.

“We’re incredibly excited to expand our partnership with NBCUniversal to redefine what a modern entertainment subscription can be for consumers,” said Neal Mohan, YouTube’s CEO. “YouTube Premium brings your favorite creators, artists and cultural moments together uninterrupted, and now, we’re pairing that ultimate viewing experience with Peacock’s expansive lineup of live sports like Sunday Night Football and the NBA, blockbuster Universal movies, and original series.”

Additionally, after launching Peacock Premium Plus as a YouTube add-on subscription in June, the Google-owned platform will carry the $11-a-month Peacock Premium plan as an add-on channel later this summer. The streamer’s Premium Plus plan is mostly ad-free and costs $17 per month, while the Premium plan includes ads.

Pricing for the upcoming bundle is not yet available, but YouTube Premium plans start at $9 per month for a standalone subscription.

Tech.title: Switching From a Gas Stove to Electric Can Improve Asthma, Study Finds
Tech.content:
Gas stoves release air pollutants like nitrogen dioxide, which has been linked to adverse health effects. bm_photo/Adobe Stock

When it comes to the gas vs. electric stove dispute, you’ll have people arguing about which is best for cooking and cookware, which is the safest and which is the most affordable and most eco-friendly, but a study published in early July about the health effects of gas stoves may reinvigorate the debate.

Conducted by the MetroHealth System, a Northeast Ohio hospital and academic medical center, in collaboration with six community organizations, the study found that participants with asthma reported improvements in their symptoms after switching from gas to electric stoves.

According to one of the researchers, Dr. Ashwini Sehgal, a professor of medicine at Case Western Reserve University, in an article published by the nonprofit news organization The Conversation, this is the first study to explore whether switching from a gas to an electric stove can reduce asthma symptoms.

What the study found

The study included 85 adults and children in Northeast Ohio with “poorly controlled asthma,” which was based on their symptoms, use of emergency medication and activity limitations. Each participant logged this information not only one to four weeks before their gas stoves were replaced at no cost with electric induction models, but also two to three months after the replacement.

“We chose electric induction stoves because they heat up and cool down rapidly, and they are safer and easier to clean than electric coil stoves,” Sehgal wrote in his The Conversation article. While induction stoves use an electromagnetic field to heat your cookware, electric stoves rely on electricity to do so.

Before and after the stoves were replaced, air quality monitors were used to measure nitrogen dioxide levels for seven-day periods. Nitrogen dioxide, a gaseous air pollutant emitted by gas stoves, can harm the lungs.

After the switch from gas to electric, indoor nitrogen dioxide levels decreased by 70%, and according to Sehgal, participants’ asthma symptoms went from moderate to mild, demonstrating improvements “similar to — or even greater than — those reported in clinical trials of commonly used asthma medications.”

Missed days of work or school decreased by about 80%, while ER visits and hospitalizations decreased by 70%.

Aside from asthma improvement, 98% of participants reported feeling satisfied or very satisfied with their new electric induction stoves, whereas 41% felt the same about their previous gas models.

An induction stove uses electricity, not gas, to work. Juan Algar/Getty Images

The study’s limitations

Sehgal notes that the study followed only a small number of people for a few months and did not include a comparison group with gas stoves. The results were also based on a self-reported questionnaire rather than medical records.

Results may not apply to people with mild asthma or to other US regions with different nitrogen dioxide levels.

Information wasn’t collected on other household sources of nitrogen dioxide, such as fireplaces or kerosene heaters, nor was data on participants’ allergy status, stove usage or additional medications.

As a result, further research is needed to confirm the study’s findings and to better understand long-term outcomes.

Researchers weren’t able to increase the study’s sample size or duration because the Trump administration terminated the project in May 2025, after it was selected for three years of funding by the US Environmental Protection Agency in December 2024.

Important considerations

As Sehgal put it in his article, switching from a gas stove to an electric one will not cure asthma or serve as a replacement for medical care and other health precautions.

It should also be considered that replacing a stove may not be financially feasible for many. “Most of our study participants lived in homes that were built before 1960, and we spent an average of $7,000 per household to upgrade their electrical systems as part of the study,” wrote Sehgal, adding that an electric stove plus installation costs about $1,500 in newer US homes.

If you have a gas stove, make sure you use the range hood’s exhaust fan to reduce airborne pollutants inside your home. Nattawat Jindamaneesirikul/Getty Images

What other stove research shows

Gas stoves are a source of indoor air pollution, as they emit gaseous pollutants, including nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds such as benzene and formaldehyde, both of which can cause cancer.

A May 2024 study found that nitrogen dioxide, in particular, is produced by gas stoves in the US at short-term exposure levels higher than those deemed safe by both the US Environmental Protection Agency and the World Health Organization.

The 2024 study also estimated that, at the time, 50,000 cases of childhood asthma were linked to nitrogen dioxide emitted by gas stoves. If other gas stove pollutants were included, that number could rise to about 200,000 cases. Nitrogen dioxide has also been connected to lung cancer, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and preterm birth.

Along with increased levels of particulate matter and sulfur dioxide, the American Lung Association reports that nitrogen dioxide has been linked to cancer, autoimmune disorders, pregnancy and birth outcomes and harm to the heart, lungs, kidneys and nervous system.

The University of California, Davis, Environmental Health Science Center adds that both electric and gas cooking can release PM2.5 (particles with a diameter of 2.5 microns or less) and ultrafine particles, which can cause or worsen respiratory conditions and increase the risk for cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders and immune system dysfunction.

In fact, frying foods on electric stoves produced higher particulate matter levels than on gas stoves.

However, it should be noted that gas stove pollutant levels can vary from home to home and that health effects will depend on these levels and the length of exposure. One’s lifestyle, health, age and current medical conditions can also determine health effects.

How to reduce indoor cooking air pollution

If you’re unable to switch from a gas to an electric stove, you can take other steps to reduce indoor air pollution when cooking. When outdoor air pollution is low, increase ventilation by opening windows and using your range hood’s exhaust.

If that isn’t feasible, consider purchasing an air purifier for your kitchen, which can filter out cooking particles and, if it includes an activated carbon filter, some gases, such as VOCs. Just make sure you regularly replace your air purifier’s filter so it works as intended, as it can spit pollutants back into your home if it becomes saturated.

At the end of the day, while replacing your gas stove with an electric model can reduce indoor air pollution and its health effects, it isn’t a complete solution. There are other steps you can take to improve your air quality.

Tech.title: Is Your Phone Actually Worth It? Share Your Thoughts
Tech.content:
Jeffrey Hazelwood/CNET

Your phone is essentially a miniature computer. They help us stay connected with friends online, organize our schedules and even stream our favorite shows. And you probably have a strong opinion on how your phone performs, its battery life and which features are actually useful — and which aren’t.

This month, we’re asking which phone you rely on. You can take our two-minute survey to share your experience with your device’s camera quality, battery life, durability and value. The top picks will make it to our roundup, so be sure to check back in a few weeks to see if yours made the list.

Why we want to hear from you

Spec tables on retailer sites don’t capture the full story about a phone. How your phone performs every day, your experience with the camera in dim lighting and whether the hardware holds up over time are invaluable insights for others.

“I’ve been reviewing phones at CNET for a decade and my absolute favorite part of my job is meeting readers and hearing about what they love about their handsets and what annoys them. I’m incredibly excited to hear from you and encourage you to share your experiences with us,” says Patrick Holland, director of content at CNET.

Whether you go for budget phones or prefer devices with all the bells and whistles, you can help other CNET readers find a phone that’s actually worth their money by sharing your thoughts.

How to make your voice heard

This survey is open through mid-August and takes only a few minutes to complete. After we gather enough information, we’ll tally up the numbers and publish the winners.

Need a refresher? Check out our list of the best phones to see which ones CNET editors recommend.

Tech.title: Comic-Con 2026 Trailers Are Here: Check Out Carrie, Reacher, Queen of the Damned and More
Tech.content:
Saturday’s rollout of news and trailers at San Diego Comic-Con wrapped up three days of big reveals, and CNET was in attendance to keep up with it all. Marvel’s Hall H presentation was highly anticipated, but there aren’t any new teasers to share.

Still, we want to make sure you’re clued in to all the biggest trailer drops and release dates for upcoming movies and TV shows. Though fans got an early round of official trailers for Clayface, Other Mommy and Avengers: Doomsday ahead of the convention, Apple TV, Warner Bros., Prime Video, Paramount and more studios continued to push out sneak peeks and thrilling teasers for their slates.

What are the must-watch trailers so far? All of them, basically. You can catch Carrie, The Rings of Power, Lanterns, Avatar: Seven Havens and others, and also be sure to scroll through all the SDCC merch reveals that you may’ve missed, too.

Carrie

Stephen King gave his stamp of approval and is an executive producer for Prime Video’s Carrie TV series that’s set to premiere on Oct. 7. From director Mike Flanagan, the show drops Carrie into a modernized world where cell phones and the internet give bullies a larger audience. But just because the novel took place in 1974 and it’s 2026 now, it doesn’t mean this new take won’t have Carrie’s telekinetic abilities setting things on fire.

Lanterns

When the Earth-heavy Lanters teaser dropped from DC a few months ago, it felt pretty full. There was Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan challenging John Stewart’s worthiness to carry a Green Lantern Corp. ring, desert-bound conspiracy vibes, flashbacks to John’s childhood and even a flash of Guy Gardner on screen. DC teased the ring’s powers, but with its new Comic-Con trailer released on Friday, things ramp up when Manhunters arrive on the planet to take out the Lanterns. Take a look at the interstellar enforcers and Sinestro in the trailer, and prepare for the series to land on HBO Max on Aug. 16.

Blade Runner 2099

Several years in the making, Blade Runner 2099 will debut on Nov. 25 on Prime Video. The eight-episode limited series is a sequel to the 2017 film Blade Runner 2049 and stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, along with Sheila Atim, Katelyn Rose Downey, Dimitri Abold and Daniel Rigby among the cast.

Set in an alternate version of LA where replicants run things, and the humans play second fiddle, the series sees Yeoh’s replicant Olwen chasing down outlaw replicants who’ve gone missing. With her own shelf life on a ticking clock, the stakes are high for her and for her human fugitive partner, Cora (Schafer).

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3

Remember in the Lord of the Rings trilogy, all that talk of “the One Ring to rule them all?” Well, season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is going to be all about that. These episodes take place five years after season 2, and by the looks of things, Sauron’s war with the elves is going strong, and he’s expanded his power across the majority of Middle-earth. Now all Sauron has to do is forge that pesky One Ring so he can, well, rule them all.

Jamie Campbell Bower joins the cast as the elven lord Celeborn, Galadriel’s husband and noble warrior in the fight against Sauron. This season will also introduce Nazgnagôl, better known as the Ringwraiths, in an early form of the corrupted ringholders in the story. The new season debuts on Nov. 11 on Prime Video.

Reacher, season 4

Season 4 of Reacher, which is based on Gone Tomorrow, the 13th book in Lee Child’s hit novel series, finds Jack Reacher traveling from rural America to the streets of Manhattan. Switching gears from previous seasons, the new installment finds Reacher immersed in a political conspiracy, leaving him with few people he can trust.

Stuck on the streets of New York, with the FBI and CIA on the hunt for Jack Reacher, this season finds our hero once again immersed in a mission to bring evildoers to justice. It just so happens that this time, that bad guy is apparently running for president. Alan Ritchson is back as Reacher alongside series newcomers Christopher Rodriguez-Marquette, Sydell Noel, Agnez Mo, Anggun and Kevin Corrigan.

Neagley

Maria Sten’s Neagley has been one of Jack Reacher’s fiercest and most skilled protégés. Now in her own spinoff show, she’ll be taking shots in the name of justice and ends up uncovering something grimmer than imagined. Season 1 of the action series debuts on Prime Video on Sept. 16.

Queen of the Damned

AMC’s Interview With the Vampire series is poised to slide into its fourth season with a focus on the vampire Akasha and has titled the new season as Queen of the Damned. Season 3 (titled The Vampire Lestat) brought her into the story and introduced actor Sheila Atim as the very first vampire. Atim, along with co-stars Jacob Anderson, Assad Zaman and Eric Bogosian, appeared in Hall H to share the news.

Matchbox The Movie

Kids who played with Matchbox cars when they were young grow up and learn their friend is a CIA agent who gets them caught up in a case. That’s the premise of Apple TV’s new comedy film starring John Cena as the spy and Jessica Biel, Teyonah Parris, Sam Richardson and Arturo Castro as said friends. You can stream the movie on Oct. 9.

Neuromancer

Apple TV’s sci-fi shows tend to be top-notch, and the cyberpunk-themed Neuromancer looks like it could be a remarkable addition. Callum Turner is Case, a hacker who gets drawn into a dangerous life-or-death game involving espionage, artificial intelligence and deceit. Based on William Gibson’s 1984 novel, the TV adaptation will have 10 episodes and premiere on Jan. 22, 2027.

Coyote vs. Acme

Formerly shelved by Warner Bros. Discovery, the film is an animation-meets-live-action story that Ketchup Entertainment picked up and will open in theaters on Aug. 28. Fed up with Acme’s unreliable products, Wile E. Coyote decides to hire a lawyer and sue the company. Will Forte plays Kevin Avery, who represents Coyote in his case, with John Cena as Buddy Crane, corporate counsel for Acme. The movie also features Lana Condor along with a host of Looney Tunes characters like Porky Pig, Tweety, Foghorn Leghorn and Granny (who gets dinged by an anvil).

Percy Jackson and the Olympians, season 3

A host of new gods and demigods are set to descend in season 3 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians, including Aphrodite and the children of Hades. The new eight-episode installment will premiere on Nov. 20.

Back in January, Disney Plus gave viewers a tease of what’s to come when it dropped with a scene of Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava’ Jeffries) hitting the dance floor at a middle school dance. But things get a little darker and more dangerous this time for the Camp Half-Blood kids.

Based on the third book in Rick Riordan’s series, The Titan’s Curse, this season takes Percy and crew on a rescue mission to save the goddess Artemis (played by Dafne Keen). Viewers will be introduced to the titan Atlas (Holt McCallany), Annabeth’s human dad (Jesse L. Martin), and Olympian gods Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Demeter (Jennifer Beals) and Apollo (Hubert Smielecki). Kate McKinnon plays Aphrodite.

Ebenezer

Johnny Depp made a surprise appearance at Comic-Con, donning a costume as Ebenezer Scrooge for the upcoming movie, where he plays Charles Dickens’ legendary miser. The film, due in theaters on Nov. 13, also features Rupert Grint, Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley and Sam Claflin in a star-studded cast.

Avatar: Seven Havens

From the creators of Avatar: The Last Airbender, this new series picks up after The Legend of Korra and follows a pair of twin avatars, one of whom is Korra’s successor. Marked as an omen of destruction during a time when the spirit world and physical world are imbalanced, Pavi — and her sister Nisha — will need to look to the past to discover who they are and find a way to save the Seven Havens. The animated series debuts this fall on Paramount Plus.

Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO

Kenji Kamiyama is directing the new anime film from Sola Animation, which will serve as a sort of prequel. Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO takes place about 100 years before Gundam Rogue Orbit, breaking down the origins of the world that fans are familiar with. Guided by Kamiyama’s vision, the 2027 movie will also tie in with a video game universe.

Regular Show: The Lost Tapes

An extended sneak peek for the new season of Regular Show: The Lost Tapes is now out for our consumption. When the show was revived as The Lost Tapes, it gave viewers new adventures with Mordecai and Rigby through the lens of Pops keeping up with them from the afterlife. Well, there are more VHS tapes to dig through when the next season lands on Cartoon Network and HBO Max this September.

@regularshow_official Couldn’t make it to San Diego Comic-Con? Check out this first look at all new episodes of Regular Show: The Lost Tapes! Coming on: 🌍 Cartoon Network and HBO Max | September 7 🇺🇸 Cartoon Network | September 19 🇺🇸 HBO Max and Hulu | October 11 #regularshow ♬ original sound – Regular Show

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe

HBO Max’s spin-off of The Big Bang Theory follows Kevin Sussman’s Stuart as he tries to undo the damage he caused after breaking one of Leonard and Sheldon’s inventions. A multiversal, reality-hopping, trippy joyride ensues, where viewers see alternate versions of characters they know and much more. The first episode debuted on July 23, but a clip was shared during the show’s Comic-Con panel. You can stream new episodes on Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET.

Dark Matter, Season 2

Apple TV’s panel also included a preview of Dark Matter’s second season, which draws the Dessen family deeper into the mysteries of The Box. Their stability is threatened, as is that of Amanda and Ryan when the series returns on Aug. 28.

Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, Season 4

During Star Trek’s 60th anniversary celebration in Hall H on Saturday, the crew gave the audience a sneak peek of what’s coming in season 4 of Strange New Worlds.

Tech.title: Everything New Marvel Announced at Comic-Con 2026
Tech.content:
Marvel capped off Saturday evening’s Hall H presentations at San Diego Comic-Con, giving audiences a small taste of what’s next on the menu. And we mean small. Kevin Feige and cast members teased out some movies (no TV shows, today), and we’re breaking it down for you here.

Footage from Avengers: Doomsday was shown, with Doom commanding sentinels and a history lesson on the dynamic between the Fantastic Four and the doctor. But there were only two other major announcements, and nothing for X-Men, and no chart outlining Phase 6 or Phase 7.

Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider

Johnny Blaze is making his MCU debut with Ryan Gosling in the role, which has been rumored for some time among Marvel’s fandom. Shawn Levy will be directing the new movie for the MCU after his successful run with Deadpool & Wolverine. Could this eventually segue into Midnight Sons? Fingers crossed, my friends.

Just announced in Hall H:



Ryan Gosling joins the MCU in Marvel Studios' Ghost Rider, directed by Shawn Levy. Only in theaters 2028. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/S0FQKt5RGn — Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) July 26, 2026

Agent Carter in Avengers: Doomsday

Hayley Atwell is now officially confirmed to be in Avengers: Doomsday as Agent Peggy Carter, who was first introduced in the MCU in Captain America: The First Avenger. She was in Hall H during Marvel’s presentation for the film.

Black Panther 3 coming in 2028

Feige pretended to exit the stage for the night but then walked back out with one more update: Black Panther 3 will arrive in December 2028. Actor David Jonsson will play T’Challa Jr. in the film, which is directed by Ryan Coogler. Jonsson is best known for roles as Andy in Alien: Romulus, Peter in The Long Walk and as Gus Sackey in Industry.
